Sports.title: Man Utd and Arsenal trumped by Liverpool as Reds bank £53million from Champions League BEFORE group stage draw
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL have already banked a staggering £53m from the Champions League – BEFORE Thursday’s initial draw.

The Anfield side leads the list of the Prem Uefa cash earners, despite finishing FIFTH in the top flight table last term.



Manchester City remain marginally ahead of Arsenal in the pre-season money list, despite the Gunners’ title triumph.

And while Manchester United’s return to the Euro elite after a two season absence is worth just under £45m up front, the Old Trafford side have only earned £500,000 more than Aston Villa.



Uefa splits its annual £2.1 bn Champions League prize pot into a number of components, with more than 60 per cent doled out once the competing clubs are confirmed.

All 36 teams in the draw when Uefa chiefs unveil the fixtures in Monaco on Thursday evening are guaranteed £15.9m at current exchange rates.



The clubs then share £730m in a complicated two-part “value pillar” system.

Some 73 per cent of that total – £533m – is split by a system that combines the value of each country’s TV deal with European results over the past five seasons.

Holders PSG benefit from both France’s TV contract – held until the end of this season by Canal+ – being the biggest in Europe, followed by the deal with TNT Sport and the BBC in England, and their on-field success.

Liverpool end up second overall in that calculation, with City fourth, Arsenal fifth, Aston Villa – after their Europa League triumph – ninth and Manchester United 11th.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The 36 clubs then share a further £197m based on a 10-year coefficient score of European performances.

Bayern, who earn £10.7m, get the biggest share, ahead of third-placed City, Liverpool in sixth, Arsenal eighth and United 10th.

In all, that takes Liverpool’s earnings to £53.1m, with City on £52.4m, Arsenal £50.1m and United £44.8m.



Winning all eight league stage games and going on to triumph in the Final in Madrid would bank a further £79m.

Despite their Europa League triumph last season, Villa are likely to be 26th in those 10-year rankings, worth just £3.3m, and taking their prize money to £41.7m..

But Unai Emery’s side boosted their income by picking up £2.6m despite losing to PSG in the Uefa Super Cup Final in Salzburg earlier this month, with their overall Uefa earnings at £44.3m before a ball is kicked.

The Midlanders’ income also shows the benefit of regular European football, with Newcastle having only picked up £25.4m at this point last term despite earning their spot in the Uefa elite.

PSG, who added £3.4m for their win over Villa, start with a massive £57.9m banked.



The day’s draw will see Arsenal, Liverpool and City in pot one, with Villa and United in the second group of nine teams.

But the new format, now in its third season, means all clubs play two teams from each pot in the eight-match initial phase, with the top tier completed by Real Madrid, Inter, Barcelona and Atletico Madrid.

Clubs cannot play a team from their own country until the knock-out phase begins in the spring.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Prize money is set to increase by around 35 per cent next season, when Paramount will take over the Champions League in the UK for four years with Sky Sports showing the Europa and Conference Leagues.

The overall value of the English deal will overtake France, expected to add even more extra income to Prem sides who qualify.

Sports.title: Man Utd fans brand camera operator ‘GOAT’ for shot immediately after Bruno Fernandes beats Arsenal stars to PFA award
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED fans have branded the camera operator at the PFA awards the “GOAT” after a cheeky dig at Arsenal.

Bruno Fernandes picked up the Men’s PFA Player of the Year award at the glitzy bash at the Manchester Opera House.



However, the team itself was dominated by Premier League title winners Arsenal, with five stars in the team.

That quintet of Declan Rice, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes, Jurrien Timber and David Raya, were all in attendance at the awards looking sharp in their tuxedos.



But as Red Devils captain Fernandes, who broke the Premier League assist record with his 21 last season, went up to collect his individual accolade the camera then panned to the five Arsenal stars.

They were all seen clapping as the midfielder was handed the award by former Man Utd and Chelsea playmaker Juan Mata.



And fans watching the award show found the camera cut hilarious by way of it taking a dig at the Premier League champions.

Taking to social media, one fan said: “Winning the league but still couldn’t win the biggest awards..”

A second said: “All I can see is envy.”

A third added: “Camera man is the real GOAT.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Another said: “Arsenal players looking like they want to cry.”

Despite fans feeling like they are getting one back, in all likelihood Arsenal would not be trading their English title for a PFA Player of the Year award anytime soon.

The Gunners also got off to a better start this season compared to Fernandes and Co.

Arsenal thrashed Coventry in a 3-0 win at home, while Man Utd lost 2-0 away at Hull.

Sports.title: Bizarre reason Liverpool CAN’T play against Real Madrid at Anfield in Champions League league phase this season
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL will not host Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League due to a little-known rule.

The Reds are set to discover their rivals in the early stages of the tournament when the draw is made tomorrow.



But Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola, whose side got their season underway by rescuing a last-gasp point at Newcastle on Sunday, already knows Real Madrid cannot head to Anfield.

The European heavyweights had league phase showdowns on Merseyside in each of the last two seasons.



And Uefa introduced a rule to stop the same clash taking place in three consecutive campaigns.

It means Trent Alexander-Arnold is not on course for another fiery return to Liverpool before the turn of the year.

Paragraph 16.03 of last season’s Champions League regulations read: “Uefa administration may determine alternative conditions for the draw in accordance with the principles set by the club competitions committee and may adapt any of the conditions of the draw to avoid deadlock situations and/or take into account any relevant constraints in light of decisions taken by the Uefa executive committee.

“The Uefa club competitions committee has determined an additional condition that may be applicable to the Uefa Champions League draw for the 2026/27 season, deciding that any individual fixture between the same two teams may not be repeated in the same competition with the same home team for three consecutive seasons.

“This means that if any teams that already played against each other in the league phase of the Uefa Champions League in the 2024/25 season are again drawn against each other, with the same home team, in the league phase of the Uefa Champions League in this 2025/26 season, those teams will not be able to be drawn against each other with the same home team in the 2026/27 season.”

Liverpool sealed a narrow 1-0 win over Real Madrid last November, with Alexis Mac Allister grabbing a late winner.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Reds also notched a 2-0 victory when the Spanish giants headed to Anfield 12 months earlier.

But Jude Bellingham and Co will not be handed another tough trip to Merseyside in the league phase.

Uefa rules mean Liverpool and Real Madrid will not necessarily be kept apart in the draw.

They could still face each other at the Bernabeu in the opening weeks of the Champions League.

Liverpool last visited Real Madrid in March 2023, when a place in the quarter-finals was up for grabs.



Karim Benzema bagged the only goal in a 1-0 win for the LaLiga heavyweights.

Arsenal will also not be drawn away to Inter Milan in the league phase of the competition tomorrow.

The Gunners headed to the San Siro to face the Serie A title holders last season and in the 2024/25 campaign.

Sports.title: Man Utd forced to change kit after breaking little-known Premier League rule in defeat to Hull
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED will change their kit to ensure full compliance with Premier League regulations ahead of the weekend.

The Red Devils will sport official Prem badges on both sleeves when they host Ipswich on Sunday.



Top-flight guidelines stipulate that every club must feature the Premier League badge and “No Room For Racism” element on their right arm.

If a club hasn’t secured a left-sleeve sponsor, league policy dictates that the official badge must be worn on both sides.



United are without a shirt sleeve sponsor, but failed to wear the Prem logo on their left sleeve in their 2-0 defeat at Hull City on the opening weekend.

SunSport understands United will avoid any Premier League sanction for the kit oversight.



Both the club and the league are aware of the error, and United will rectify it in time for Sunday’s home opener against the newly-promoted Tractor Boys.

United had anticipated to unveil a new sleeve sponsor, but efforts to finalise a commercial deal are still in place. The club wore their new third kit on Saturday.

Old Trafford‘s £20m-a-year deal with DXC Technology expired in May, leaving their sleeves unbranded for the first time in eight years.

The practice of wearing two league badges is a direct enforcement of Premier League Rule M.15, which dictates that if a club lacks a commercial left-sleeve sponsor, the official league badge must be applied to that sleeve as well as the right.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Chelsea, Sunderland, and Crystal Palace all featured the league’s iconic lion crest on both sleeves over the opening weekend.

Earlier in August, United agreed a record multi-year training kit sponsorship deal with Betway worth approximately £20million per season.

Snapdragon have been United’s front-of-shirt sponsor since the start of the 2024/25 campaign.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal £50m agreement, Man Utd land huge boost, Barcola to Liverpool
Sports.content:
Ayyoub Bouaddi completes Man City transfer

Ayyoub Bouaddi has wasted no time in sticking the boot into his new rivals - after admitting Manchester City are the best club in the world.

The Moroccan sensation has completed an £85m switch to City from Lille.

The teenage midfielder has agreed a deal that will keep him at the Etihad until at least 2031.

And Bouaddi has told the likes of Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United there is no place he would rather be.

Bouaddi said: "Manchester City are, for me, the best club in the world. It's a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player.

"I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.

"I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football.

"And they have shown they are winners - this club feels like it's built to win.

"The squad is world-class and Enzo (Maresca) is a top manager. And I’m really looking forward to playing at the Etihad Stadium, in front of all the fans.

"I have plenty of improving to do. I am only 18. I am happy with the progress I have made so far, but I also know I can improve so much. This is undoubtedly the best place for me to do that.

"This club demands trophies and I will give everything to make sure we are challenging for every title."

Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice was quick to react to Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes winning his latest individual honour at the PFA Awards

View 2 Images Declan Rice watched on as Bruno Fernandes picked up his PFA Players' Player of the Year award (Image: Getty)

Declan Rice didn't hesitate to clap for Bruno Fernandes after he was crowned the PFA Players' Player of the Year. The Manchester United captain picked up the honour at the PFA Awards on Tuesday instead of Rice.

‌



Fernandes' heroics last season saw him lead United to a third-place finish and unlikely Champions League qualification. He broke the all-time Premier League assist record with 21, one more than Kevin De Bruyne and Thierry Henry achieved in the 2019/20 and 2002/03 seasons, respectively.

‌



The 31-year-old was largely battling Rice for the award, with the Arsenal talisman having played a major role in his side's title triumph. However, it was the Portugal international who was crowned.

‌



Despite missing out on the trophy, the England midfielder's classy reaction was captured by cameras at the ceremony. Moments after Fernandes was announced as the winner, the camera panned to Rice in the audience and out of his Arsenal team-mates sitting next to him - Jurrien Timber, William Saliba, David Raya and Gabriel - he was by far the most enthusiastic in applause.

Delap's departure is more advanced, with the 23-year-old set to have a medical at Forest ahead of completing a move worth up to £50m. Sports.title: Chelsea ask fans to stop controversial chant after loud Fulham rendition
Sports.content:
Chelsea ask fans to stop controversial chant after loud Fulham rendition

A portion of Chelsea fans launched into a sectarian chant during their opening game of the Premier League season, as they watched Xabi Alonso's side beat Fulham 3-2

View 2 Images Chelsea have taken a stance (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Chelsea have written to their supporters warning them against singing a sectarian chant which was heard in the away end during their clash with Fulham. In Monday's 3-2 victory at Craven Cottage, some Chelsea fans belted out the song 'F lute for 50 Pence'.

‌



The opening verse of the song includes the line: "F*** the Pope and the IRA." Chelsea officials quickly became aware of the chant being sung and have acted.

‌



An email to supporters who travelled to the game read: "Dear supporter, Thank you for your fantastic support during our opening Premier League fixture of the season against Fulham. The whole team and manager recognised your contribution to helping secure our first win of the campaign.

‌



"The passion and backing from our fans are vital in achieving a successful season, and we encourage you to continue your vocal support for the team. Following the fixture, we have received multiple reports of sectarian chanting from a small portion of those in attendance at the match.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"We would like to strongly remind all supporters that the club does not condone any chants which discriminate against a protected characteristic. Any supporter found guilty of this will face the strongest possible action, which could include indefinite suspension from attending all Chelsea matches and ejection from the stadium.

"Following previous club fines and charges for chants of this nature, and to ensure that we create a welcoming matchday experience for all, we ask supporters to take collective responsibility and remain vigilant in helping us tackle discriminatory chanting.

"If you witness any discriminatory language or behaviour while supporting the team, please report it to us by notifying your nearest matchday steward whilst at the game or via our dedicated reporting form.

‌



"Thank you for your ongoing support throughout this season. Chelsea FC.

The use of the chant appears to reflect Chelsea's long-standing relationship with Scottish giants Rangers. It has been heard sung in relation to Glasgow rivals Celtic, who have a deep connection to the Roman Catholic Church.

The Football Association are also aware of the situation. In October 2025, the FA fined Lincoln £8,500 for twice chanting 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' towards former Wrexham and Republic of Ireland player James McClean. Chelsea could therefore face a similar punishment.

‌



View 2 Images Chelsea's fans enjoyed a 3-2 win (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

There was a charged atmosphere at Craven Cottage, with the Premier League unusually scheduling a West London derby for the opening matchday. It took Chelsea just one minute to take the lead, as Joao Pedro got Xabi Alonso's reign off to the perfect start.

Fulham equalised through Josh King before Morgan Rogers scored on his debut to restore Chelsea's advantage. Cole Palmer then gave the Blues breathing room shortly after half-time.

‌



Another debutant, Gonzalo Garcia, pulled a goal back for Fulham in the 54th minute. As the hosts pushed to drew level again, Chelsea held on to begin their season with a win.

Another moment of animosity came when Enzo Fernandez was subbed on by Alonso. Fulham fans heavily jeered the Argentine, who'd taunted England after beating them at the World Cup.

Alonso was pleased with how his side handled the encounter, saying post-match: "[It's important] to manage in difficult moments, not to lose this emotional control. We know the Premier League is fantastic because sometimes the games are out of your hands.

Article continues below

"You don't control them, so the players on the pitch need to know how to manage it - it's as important as the tactics being right. It's a process but today we went through good moments on that and we need to carry on that."

Sports.title: Match of the Day commentator fires back at Richard Keys in row over BBC programme
Sports.content:
Match of the Day commentator fires back at Richard Keys in row over BBC programme

Richard Keys has annoyed a Match of the Day commentator after sounding off about the BBC's iconic Premier League highlights programme on his new podcast

View 2 Images Richard Keys isn't a fan of Match of the Day (Image: YouTube/Keys & Gray Unleashed )

Richard Keys has been branded an "unemployable dinosaur" by a Match of the Day commentator after he slammed the BBC highlights programme.

‌



Keys and sidekick Andy Gray are embarking upon a new stage in their careers after leaving Qatar and their jobs with beIN SPORTS. The duo moved to the Middle East following their sacking by Sky Sports for making sexist comments in 2011, but are now back in England.

‌



After 13 years in Doha with beIN SPORTS, Keys and Gray have now entered the world of podcasting with a show called 'Keys & Gray Unleashed'. In the latest episode, Keys has voiced his opinion that the BBC's Premier League highlights show, Match of the Day, is unfit for purpose in the age of social media.

‌



He said: "When [Gary] Lineker left Match of the Day, there was a big fuss about who was going to present the programme going forward and my attitude then and remains 'who cares'? It doesn't matter. Match of the Day is a programme well past its sell by date. It was when Gary was presenting it. Who watches it?

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"By the time it goes to air everybody knows what's happened in the day. Highlights are available from 5.15 on most social media outlets. They even let commentators, in an eight-minute edit, do team news at the top. Why? What's the point of that?"

‌



He went on to lament the £390,000 to £394,999-a-year that Alan Shearer earned for his punditry role last year. "The BBC still think they cover football better than anyone else," he concluded before looking directly down the camera. "Not since 1992 guys."

Keys' not-so hot take has wound up commentator Dan O'Hagan, who has worked on Match of the Day, as well as other BBC sports highlights shows.

"So, this is to be their format then," O'Hagan wrote on X. "A pair of old, unemployable dinosaurs saying mildly controversial things for clicks. No better than the YouTubers or the s***-takes-for-likes influencers. Quite sad really, especially as Gray was genuinely the best co-commentator around."

‌



View 2 Images Mark Chapman, Gabby Logan and Kelly Cates took over as Match of the Day presenters in 2025 (Image: CREDIT LINE:BBC / Charlie Clift)

Lineker presented Match of the Day from 1999 to 2025 before stepping down last summer. Last season saw Kelly Cates, Mark Chapman and Gabby Logan come in to share presenting duties.

There have been reports of tensions behind the scenes recently due to BBC director of sport Alex Kay-Jelski's plans to take the iconic programme in a different direction. Reports that Shearer had decided to reduce his appearances on the show to once-a-month have been rejected by the corporation.

‌



"The suggestion that Alan is reducing his Match of the Day appearances because of the director of sport is untrue," a spokesperson said.

A statement from Shearer read: “Cutting back my MOTD appearances is something we’ve been discussing for some time and purely so I can have some weekends back. I've always had a positive relationship with everyone at the BBC and that continues to be the case.”

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and laughing gas possession after motorway crash
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and laughing gas possession after motorway crash

Raheem Sterling is due in court next month to face charges of dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen

View 2 Images Raheem Sterling is without a club after playing for Feyenoord last season (Image: Gabriel Calvino Alonso/Getty Images)

Former England star Raheem Sterling has been charged following a crash on the motorway in May.

The 31-year-old, who is currently without a club, was arrested on May 28 following a collision on the M3 involving his black 4x4 Lamborghini. He is now due at Basingstoke magistrates court on September 15 to face three charges.

A Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesman said: “A driver will appear in court next month to face charges following a collision on the M3.

“Raheem Sterling, 31, from Berkshire, has been charged for the following offences: dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen.

“The charges come following a single vehicle collision, involving a Lamborghini, on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange, on 28 May, 2026.

Article continues below

View 2 Images Raheem Sterling is currently without a club (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

“No other vehicles were involved and no injuries were reported. Mr Sterling is due to appear at Basingstoke magistrates court on 15 September.”

The ex-Liverpool, Manchester City, Arsenal and Chelsea forward had just finished his stint playing for Feyenoord at the time of the crash. After being frozen out of the first-team set-up, he terminated his contract with Chelsea in January in order to join the Dutch club.

Article continues below

He played under former Premier League striker Robin van Persie, but the short-term move didn't go to plan, with no goals or assists coming in his eight appearances for Feyenoord.

The four-time Premier League winner has spent the summer looking for a new club - a search which has so far proven unsuccessful. He has been keeping busy in the off-season by coaching at his own RS7 Academy.

Sports.title: Man Utd's dream end to transfer window with Lewis Hall U-turn and £40m deal struck
Sports.content:
Man Utd's dream end to transfer window with Lewis Hall U-turn and £40m deal struck

Manchester United have under a week to complete their summer transfer business

View 3 Images Manchester United are still extremely interested in Lewis Hall

Manchester United could offload a striker and sign their most desired target before the transfer window is over. Michael Carrick endured a nightmare start to the Premier League season after losing 2-0 to Hull City on Saturday.

‌



Despite this defeat, the United boss has insisted he saw positives and will not allow the team to be downtrodden by the result. He said: "It’s one game. It’s the first game of the season so it’s disappointing enough and it hurts, of course it does.

‌



"But it’s one game, it doesn’t change the whole course of the direction the team or the football club is going in. We’ll stay calm, stay in the bubble and focus on next week."

‌



Now, the manager will focus on bringing in new faces to boost the squad. Carlos Baleba is set to join from Brighton for a fee of £70million with the midfielder being sent for a medical at the weekend.

Paul Scholes lashes out at Bruno Fernandes after Man Utd skipper slated team-mates READ MORE :

Here, Mirror Football has examined how United could add to Baleba's arrival and end the transfer window on a high.

Lewis Hall U-turn

It is no secret that United are huge admirers of Newcastle's Lewis Hall. The defender has been targeted by the Red Devils all summer but Magpies manager Matthias Jaissle emphasised that he is not planning to let Hall go.

‌



When United icon Peter Schmeichel asked if the full-back could head to Old Trafford, Jaissle exclaimed: "No chance! No chance!"

Sky broadcasts more than 1,400 live matches across the Premier League, EFL and more with at least 215 live from the top flight alongside Formula 1, darts and golf.

View 3 Images Hall is very coveted by the Newcastle fans and their new manager (Image: Getty)

‌



However, stranger things have happened in previous transfer windows. Newcastle fans will still be feeling the pain of the Alexander Isak saga last summer, where the once-beloved striker was ordered to train separately from the team amid claims of "broken promises" and "misleading" words.

The Swede eventually joined Liverpool for £125m after missing multiple Premier League matches and causing a transfer drama that is still talked about one year on. Hall is a totally different player to his ex-teammate and may not consider trying a stake-out to force a move to United.

However, he could see this as a viable option with Jaissle shutting down any speculation despite United still holding a keen interest in the 21-year-old. Hall is valued at around £34m by Transfermarkt, but a £60m price tag has already been mentioned.

‌



£40m deal done

View 3 Images Joshua Zirkzee could be on his way out (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Joshua Zirkzee has been linked with a move away from United for some time. However, Carrick has no intentions of letting the Dutchman leave on the cheap.

The 25-year-old has attracted interest from Napoli, Aston Villa and Juventus. The Sun reports that United are demanding at least £40m before considering a permanent sale for the striker.

‌



Zirkzee could make a return to Serie A this summer after spending two seasons with Bologna before heading to Manchester. Football Italia claims that Juve have made enquiries with Napoli also keen.

However, both teams may need to make room in their squad before entertaining a move for Zirkzee. Villa were interested in the striker due to Ollie Watkins' impending exit to Saudi Arabia, but a move back to Italy could be more appealing to the 25-year-old.

With Benjamin Sesko, Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford all good options for Carrick, Zirkzee's Old Trafford exit could be on the horizon.

Sports.title: Man City sign Bouaddi in record-breaking deal
Sports.content:
Manchester City have completed the signing of midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi in a record-breaking £86m move from Lille.

Sky Sports News understands City are paying a fixed fee of £81.3m plus £4.3m in add-ons. Bouaddi has signed a five-year contract, keeping him at City until the summer of 2031.

The 18-year-old becomes the most expensive teenage signing in Premier League history, surpassing the £58.9m Manchester United committed to paying Lille for Leny Yoro in 2024.

Lille have secured the fee they were holding out for in negotiations for Bouaddi, who was one of the breakout stars of this summer's World Cup with Morocco.

City are working to rebuild their midfield after the departures of Rodri, Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders.

"Manchester City are, for me, the best club in the world," said Bouaddi. "It's a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan and Michael Bridge discuss whether Manchester City need to sign another midfielder alongside Elliot Anderson and Bouaddi

"I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game. I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football. And they have shown they are winners - this club feels like it's built to win.

"The squad is world-class and Enzo [Maresca] is a top manager. And I'm really looking forward to playing at the Etihad Stadium, in front of all the fans.

"I have plenty of improving to do. I am only 18. I am happy with the progress I have made so far, but I also know I can improve so much. This is undoubtedly the best place for me to do that.

"This club demands trophies and I will give everything to make sure we are challenging for every title."

Manchester City director of football Hugo Viana said: "Ayyoub's potential is extremely high - a player equipped with everything a top midfielder needs.

"At just 18, he already has outstanding football intelligence and that will only improve under the guidance of Enzo.

"We have watched him very closely and throughout that process we have become increasingly convinced he is a huge talent who will thrive at City.

"We are really happy he has joined us and our job now is to ensure we provide him with everything he needs to fulfil his potential."

What position will Bouaddi play at City?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Transfer Talk Podcast panel discuss Manchester City's links with Enzo Fernandez and Bouaddi, and if the two stars would fit City's style

Bouaddi revealed the role he is set to play at City - hinting that he's going to play as a defensive midfielder.

"I would say I am a player who plays for the team," Bouaddi says. "I am a really collective player. I try to put my team-mate in the best position and to give everything every time for the team.

"The most important aspect is to try to balance the team, help your team-mates.

"We know as a No 6 that you're not going to score 20 goals in a season, well it can happen but it's quite rare, so you know you have to balance the team and do everything for the team and do your job."

Those who followed Morocco's recent World Cup campaign will recognise the name Ayyoub Bouaddi. Perhaps those who only took a passing glance will remember him, too. He tends to stand out.

Aside from his throwback curly mop of hair, the way he dominated the big stage with effortless grace over the summer got people talking. The midfielder excelled in his fledgling role at his first major international tournament, particularly noticeable in a group-stage bout with Brazil.

But this was not the first time Carlo Ancelotti found himself ruminating over an opposition player who was "better in the duels" than his own.

Ancelotti's Brazilian midfield was composed of the experienced Casemiro and Bruno Guimaraes, and yet somehow it was Bouaddi that beamed brightest. It struck a familiar chord...

Sports.title: River Card and Cloud Forest clash at Newbury
Sports.content:
We have a busy day’s racing on Wednesday with flat action from Newbury and Wolverhampton, live on Sky Sports Racing...

6.30 Newbury - Cloud Forest and River Card headline feature handicap

Cloud Forest and River Card clash in an excellent renewal of the feature Gracelands Handicap at Newbury.

Saeed bin Suroor saddles Cloud Forest, who drops back to a mile as he makes his handicap debut after three starts this season. The form of his recent second at Kempton has been boosted and he can go well under Hector Crouch.

River Card claimed the notable scalp of Maltese Cross when winning an Ascot maiden last year but finished well beaten in a sales race over in Deauville next time. He makes appeal if fit enough on this seasonal return and handicap debut with Tom Marquand in the saddle for the first time.

Others to note include Haydock winner Home Hero, while the hat-trick seeking Accademia must be feared despite a six-pound penalty for her course and distance success last month.

3.30 Wolverhampton - In-form The Craftymaster faces Boilermaker

In-form The Craftymaster takes on six rivals in a trappy attheraces.com/Marketmovers Handicap at Wolverhampton.

Tony Carroll's charge has won three of his past four starts and seeks a hat-trick under new pilot Molly Gunn. A narrow winner at Lingfield and Newmarket the last twice, he switches back to the all-weather with obvious claims.

Boilermaker recorded a first career success at Sandown last month and, with confidence boosted, the sole three-year-old in the field ought to make his presence felt on just his third all-weather run.

Thomas Faulkner's V Power merits respect on the pick of his form, while Letmebetheboss and Fair Dinkum complete the shortlist.

Somers Isles and Bidsta clash in a hot edition of this IRE Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish Maiden Fillies' Stakes at 5.55pm.

The Andrew Balding-trained Somers Isle made a pleasing start to her career when runner-up at Newmarket last month and, with the yard in cracking form, she could go one better under Oisin Murphy.

Richard Spencer's Starburster showed ability when getting the hang of things late on debut at Windsor and granted natural progression she looks an each-way player.

George Boughey's Bidsta is a fascinating newcomer for Victorious Racing. A 380,000-guineas purchase at two, she is closely related to useful sprinter Ferrous and should be in the mix for a yard who have done well with juveniles this summer.

Sports.title: Mayer: I feel unbeatable - Cameron fight won't be close!
Sports.content:
Mikaela Mayer says she feels "unbeatable" and that her blockbuster unification fight against Chantelle Cameron for the world super welterweight titles won't be close.

British WBO title holder Cameron (22-1, 8 KOs) faces American Mayer (22-2, 5 KOs) at the bp pulse LIVE arena on Saturday - live on Sky Sports - with every bout on the MVPW-06 main card pitting a UK fighter against a US opponent.

WBA and WBC champion Mayer has no shortage of respect for Cameron - who has won her last four fights since a rematch defeat to Katie Taylor in 2023 - but has backed her own ability to unify the titles in front of what is set to be a hostile Birmingham crowd.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mikaela Mayer says she and Chantelle Cameron are at the peak of their powers and that the super welterweight showdown can only lead to 'an action-packed' fight.

"I feel better than ever," Mayer told Sky Sports. "I just know I just feel unbeatable right now. I feel in a great position and I can't wait to get out to the UK and do my thing.

"[Cameron] is good at what she does. She's an aggressive fighter. She lets her hands go.

"She fights at a fast pace and so do I. So that's going to make for a very exciting fight for the fans.

"But I just don't think it's going to be as close and as much of a war as everyone thinks.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chantelle Cameron can't wait for her unified world super welterweight title fight with Mikaela Mayer in Birmingham on 29 August.

"There's probably a handful of people who think I'm stupid for coming to the UK and going onto Chantelle's turf, but I'm just confident in myself right now.

"I'm fighting better than I've ever fought, smarter than I've ever been. And I just believe in myself.

"I feel like no matter where I go, I'm still going to kick butt. So it could be here. It could be there. I'm taking the win."

Mayer pointed to her "versatility" as a defining factor come Saturday, insisting nothing can prepare Cameron for the new and improved version of the 36-year-old that awaits.

"I'm really hard to train for because I've developed so much these last 10 months of being in the gym," Mayer told Sky Sports.

"I know I haven't fought since last October but the things I'm doing now, it's really impossible for Chantelle to have trained for me at this point.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mikaela Mayer, Chantelle Cameron, Caroline Dubois and Amelia Moore face off ahead of their MVP 06 clashes on Saturday.

"I'm going to do everything I can to make it a very obvious win, maybe a stoppage, we'll see, but I know I'm coming out with my hand raised.

"I've worked on making sure that my inside game and when I do press forward that my defence is tighter and I'm the one landing my shots. I'll definitely be using a little bit of everything I've got, but knowing mine and Chantelle's styles there will definitely be moments where it will be a dog fight."

Mayer vs Cameron - fighter records

Mikaela Mayer Wins 22 Losses 2

Chantelle Cameron Wins 22 Losses 1

'A win would be one of the best moments of my career'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mikaela Mayer is supremely confident she'll beat Chantelle Cameron when the pair clash on 29 August, live on Sky Sports.

The 35-year-old Cameron won the WBO super welterweight title - a belt Mayer had vacated just months after beating Mary Spencer for it - with a dominant victory over Michaela Kotaskova in April.

The significance of the chance to become unified world champion by reclaiming the WBO crown is not lost on Mayer, with the American describing the prospect of victory as a career-defining moment.

"[A win would be] definitely up there with one of the best [moments].

"I've had a pretty awesome career. Even though I've gone through some ups and downs, I think that's what makes my career even more special and what makes these big fights that are ahead of me extra special.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chantelle Cameron says she has been waiting a long time for a big name clash with Mikaela Mayer and put their super welterweight world titles on the line.

"I've had to go through trials and tribulations - I've had to adjust, I've had to make changes in my team and keep continuing to get better - and I've done that.

"Going in there and having a dominating performance against someone like Chantelle Cameron, who is very highly respected - the only person to beat Katie Taylor - that's going to definitely be one of the best moments of my career thus far."

The upcoming bout may not be the last between the two, with Mayer revealing that a rematch clause has been included in the contract of both fighters:

"Well, Chantelle and I do have a rematch clause on both of our ends, which is unique, but if it's the type of fight that everyone expects, then why not do a rematch?

"Why not give it to the world again? I have no problem giving a rematch when it's, when it's justified.

"Do I want to kick her butt so bad that she doesn't even want to activate that rematch clause? Of course. But if she does, we can go again."

Sports.title: Wolff 'not at all' disappointed by Verstappen's new Red Bull deal
Sports.content:
Mercedes chief Toto Wolff says he is "not at all" disappointed by Max Verstappen having committed to Red Bull with a new contract that runs until 2030.

Ahead of the Formula 1 season resuming with Verstappen's home Dutch Grand Prix over the weekend, Red Bull ended speculation over the four-time world champion's future by announcing the extension.

While Verstappen's previous deal was set to run until 2028, exit clauses in the agreement meant the 28-year-old would have been free to join another team in 2027, with possible switches to Mercedes and McLaren having been the subject of significant speculation.

Wolff made a very public pursuit of Verstappen after Lewis Hamilton announced in February 2024 that he was leaving Mercedes to join Ferrari in 2025, and the Mercedes boss appeared to still be interested in signing the Dutchman last season

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Verstappen admits that, with V8 engines' potential return in 2030, there may be another opportunity for him to reassess his future in F1

However, Wolff has insisted in recent months that he is happy with his driver pairing of Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, who sit first and second, respectively, at the top of the Drivers' Championship after Sunday's race in Zandvoort.

Asked about Verstappen's new contract in an interview with Sky Sports F1 on Saturday in Zandvoort, Wolff said: "Most important was that we had the clarity in the team since a long time.

"We're committed to George and Kimi, and in a way, that was just a logical consequence what happened now.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff had previously downplayed suggestions Verstappen could join his team

"Silly season is officially cancelled now, and everybody can concentrate on the racing."

Pushed on whether he felt any disappointment about the length of Verstappen's commitment to Red Bull, Wolff added: "No, not at all.

"We know each other well. With Kimi and George, it's the perfect set-up we have and the perfect line-up, so there is no disappointment."

Rosberg: I don't think Max had any options

The cooling of Wolff's interest in Verstappen appears as though it may have been influenced by the hugely impressive form that has put Antonelli in control of the championship.

The Italian, who turned 20 on Tuesday, has unexpectedly outperformed the far more experienced Russell to build a 59-point advantage over his team-mate at the top of the standings.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix

While Mercedes showed huge faith in Antonelli by fast-tracking him in as Hamilton's replacement as a teenager, an inconsistent rookie campaign left doubt over whether he would be able to live up to expectations.

However, his 2026 form, which saw him break countless records by winning five successive races after finishing second in the season opener, could potentially have made Wolff reconsider whether bringing Verstappen to Mercedes remained necessary.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A 360-degree look at Verstappen’s race-ending crash at the Dutch Grand Prix on Sunday

McLaren appeared to be similarly content with their current driver line-up of reigning world champion Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri, who have combined to lead the Woking squad to successive constructors' titles.

Sky Sports F1 pundit Nico Rosberg, who won the 2016 world championship with Mercedes, said: "It's fantastic news for Formula 1 because Max Verstappen is the greatest driver at the moment, and we want him to stay here. He's a phenomenal driver!

"He was thinking about taking some time off, or stopping F1 for a while, so that's great.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nico Rosberg discusses Verstappen's contract extension with Red Bull, saying it's a 'super important message' for the team

"I don't think he had any options. He was in talks with McLaren, but I think that was just to strengthen his position at Red Bull.

"Red Bull need stability so you offer him a bit more money, and the range is from £70-90m a year, so let's land on £80m - which is a lot of money!"

Sports.title: Uefa poised to lift boycott threat after Fifa promises no World Cup sale repeat
Sports.content:
Uefa is poised to drop its threatened boycott of Fifa competitions after receiving concrete guarantees that the global governing body will never attempt a repeat of Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in the World Cup.

The Guardian understands European teams are likely to be cleared for participation in the upcoming under-20 Women’s World Cup, along with subsequent tournaments, after Fifa provided the binding assurances that no equivalent of its president’s ill-fated scheme will be put on the table.

Uefa had threatened the boycott after Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal was revealed and doubled down after it was withdrawn, saying the condition that “such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again” had not been met.

Quick Guide How do I 

Despite exchanging barbs in public Uefa and Fifa are understood to have been having private discussions over the terms of removing the boycott threat for several weeks, with the European governing body finally getting the reassurances it required.

When Fifa confirmed its decision to abandon FFE four days after it became public it neglected to pledge that a similar privatisation plan would not be repeated, but has now done so in private correspondence.

A decision to drop the boycott will allow England, who named their squad for the under-20 tournament last week, to travel to Poland in time for the opening game against Canada on 5 September.

View image in fullscreen England’s under-20s are in line to go to the World Cup in Poland. Photograph: Carlos Rodrigues/The FA/Getty Images

France and Spain had also listed their travelling party in anticipation that the boycott would be lifted. Portugal, Italy and the host nation are the other European countries due to compete.

While the boycott is yet to be publicly dropped, it is among the topics that may arise in a meeting of Uefa’s executive committee and federation chiefs in Monte Carlo on Thursday.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The 55 heads of Uefa’s member associations will convene before the Champions League draw during what is traditionally a significant few days in the European football calendar.

Uefa’s position that Infantino must be replaced has not changed and further steps regarding its stance towards the Fifa leadership will also be discussed at Thursday’s meeting.

There will be relief in some quarters that younger players, in particular, will not become embroiled in the volatile battle for football’s future. But the fact Fifa has been forced to mitigate for its president’s actions is another humiliation for a persistently scandal-hit organisation.

Sports.title: Martin O’Neill puts Champions League collapse among most painful Celtic nights
Sports.content:
Martin O’Neill has admitted that Celtic’s Champions League qualifying collapse from 4-0 up ranks as one of his most painful nights as the club’s manager.

Celtic held a four-goal aggregate lead against Lask on Tuesday when Callum McGregor scored in the 21st minute in Austria, building on a 3-0 first-leg victory, and appeared to be cruising into the league stage. But they lost 5-1 on the night after extra time to go out in extraordinary fashion.

Defeat sends Celtic into the Europa League and delivers a damaging financial blow that will cost the club at least £20m. O’Neill, who has overseen more than 300 games as the club’s manager, said the loss on Tuesday was one of the most painful.

“I would say absolutely, yes,” the 74-year-old said. “I’d put it down before the disappointment of losing the Uefa Cup final in 2003, but it’s so, so disappointing.

“We should have been out of sight by half-time. We scored a goal, which was great, we missed two great, great opportunities. And then we give them a lifeline just before half-time and then one just after it. And they come roaring back. And obviously we conceded, from our viewpoint, not good goals at all. But that’s my team and that’s my responsibility.”

Asked whether his squad was strong enough, O’Neill said: “These are tough games. And it might only be a Champions League qualifying game, but it felt like a Champions League game. I thought they were a fine side. But that doesn’t matter. We should have been able to have seen it through. And we didn’t do. Talking about the squad, that’s for another day.”

McGregor, the captain, accepted there were no excuses. “We got what we deserved,” he told Amazon Prime. “I thought we were so passive. All night. We actually looked scared to go and win the game, and when you are 3-0 up it’s psychological.

“To be honest I didn’t think we were that good in the first leg, either. We scored at good times and kind of got away with it. You go 3-0 and you think you’ve got a real chance but when you play like that you can’t have any excuse whatsoever.

“We have to suck it up, apologise to the supporters and the club because there is no way that we should lose that game … Now you’ll see what kind of characters are in there.”

Sports.title: Manchester City confirm Bouaddi signing as Marmoush and González head out
Sports.content:
Manchester City have confirmed the signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for €95m (£81.4m) plus €5m, with the 18-year-old midfielder agreeing a five-year contract.

Bouaddi’s arrival comes after City struck deals to loan Omar Marmoush to Tottenham for the season, with an obligation to buy for an initial £50m, and sell Nico González to Newcastle for £52m.

Bouaddi has experienced a rapid rise after becoming Lille’s youngest player when featuring against KÍ Klaksvík on 5 October 2023, three days after his 16th birthday. The Morocco international played 96 times for Lille and becomes the most expensive teenager signed by an English club.
