He said: “I am happy with the progress I have made so far, but I also know I can improve so much. This is undoubtedly the best place for me to do that. This club demands trophies and I will give everything to make sure we are challenging for every title.”

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, said: “Ayyoub’s potential is extremely high – a player equipped with everything a top midfielder needs. At just 18, he already has outstanding football intelligence and that will only improve under the guidance of Enzo [Maresca].”

Bouaddi, who has played mainly as a No 6, continues City’s midfield rebuild. González is poised to become the fourth frontline central midfielder to depart this summer, after Rodri, Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders. City have added Bouaddi and Elliott Anderson, a £116m buy from Nottingham Forest, and are expected to firm up their interest in Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández by making a bid. The west London club value the midfielder at £120m.

Marmoush is to have a medical at Spurs, who have agreed to pay up to £10m in add-ons, with half of that guaranteed. Next summer the 27-year-old is to sign a four-year contract with a one-year option.

View image in fullscreen Omar Marmoush is to sign a four-year contract with Spurs next summer when his loan ends. Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty Images

City are not due to give a sell-on fee to Eintracht Frankfurt, from whom they bought the Egyptian in January 2025. Marmoush is following Sávio in leaving City for Spurs, who bought the Brazilian winger in a £75m plus £10m deal on Tuesday. City have agreed a £34m fee for Palmeiras’s Allan Elias, who is to be Sávio’s replacement as a wide forward.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Spurs manager, Roberto De Zerbi, has been keen to bolster his options at centre-forward and Marmoush represents an upgrade on Dominic Solanke and Richarlison, who have struggled for consistency and fitness.

De Zerbi said at the end of July that Spurs had a “bomba” attacking signing lined up, meaning a top-tier player, and Marmoush and Sávio fit the bill. They have taken rather longer to join than he would have liked; he revealed on Tuesday that the negotiations for Sávio started three days after the end of last season. He believes they will be worth the wait.

Spurs have spent £304.5m this summer on Jan Paul van Hecke, Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Sávio. They have added Martin Dubravka, Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi on free transfers.

Sports.title: De Zerbi hopes Sávio’s fresh start will help Spurs’ much-needed rebrand
Sports.content:
What’s in a name? Quite a bit, judging by the discussion at Roberto De Zerbi’s Tottenham press conference on Tuesday, shortly after the club had completed the £75m signing of Savinho from Manchester City and the Brazil winger had let everybody know that he wanted to be called Sávio from now on. He will have that name on his Spurs shirt above his No 17, which he has taken over from Cristian Romero, the former captain who has moved to Atlético Madrid.

The 22-year-old went by Sávio at various times before his two seasons at City but there was nonetheless speculation about the reasons for the reversion. Savinho translates roughly from the Portuguese as “little Sávio”. Was it him saying that he was now an older and more mature player?

On the subject of theories, there is one about the fee, which could rise to £85m in add-ons. Even at £75m, it represents a record sale for City, who paid £30.8m to take Sávio from Troyes. Spurs are pushing to sign another attacker from City – Omar Marmoush, whose previous club Eintracht Frankfurt have a sell-on clause. Are Spurs paying more for Sávio in order to pay potentially less to City for Marmoush, which could reduce the liabilities to Eintracht?

De Zerbi has plenty on his plate after Spurs’ dismal 3-0 defeat at Brentford on Saturday in their Premier League opener and before the Carabao Cup tie at home against Charlton on Wednesday night.

“Listen, I lost 3-0 in the first game in the Premier League … do you think for me it’s a problem if Savinho becomes Sávio?” he said, turning to face his interpreter. “If Enrico [the interpreter] becomes Savinho, it’s a problem. If Savinho stays Sávio, nothing changes for me.”

De Zerbi said the talks for Sávio had started three days after the end of last season. It has been a mini‑epic to get the deal over the line but well worth it, according to the Spurs manager, who rates Sávio as one of the best in the world for being able to get past his marker when one‑against‑one. The challenge for Sávio will be to improve his end product, particularly in terms of goals. He scored only seven for City in all competitions and only two in 53 Premier League appearances. Sávio is available for selection against Charlton, his paperwork having been completed in time.

De Zerbi did get around to accepting that Sávio’s rebrand was part of a fresh start for the player. What is not in doubt is Spurs’ need for one after Brentford, when all the excitement around a summer of heavy spending turned to frustration; a very familiar sinking feeling.

View image in fullscreen New Tottenham signings Jan Paul van Hecke (left) and Sandro Tonali (right) after Spurs conceded their second goal during their 3-0 defeat at Brentford. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

It is possible to explain away the shambles against Brentford, who were not only much more joined-up but appeared to want it more in the duels. De Zerbi has attempted to do so in that way beloved of managers, emphasising he is not making excuses, you understand, just stating facts.

He had a completely new back four compared with his preferred unit from the end of last season; a new midfield pair, too. Up front from right to left, Mikey Moore, Richarlison and Mathys Tel were nobody’s idea of a trio to drive the push for Champions League football. De Zerbi was missing a host of players because of fitness issues, including Pedro Porro, Micky van de Ven, Mateus Fernandes and Dominic Solanke. Some of the issues can be traced to the slog of a pre-season tour to New Zealand and Australia, which De Zerbi continues to reference in irritated tones.

These facts do not really wash. The performance against Brentford was unacceptable. There is the sense that it will work out for Spurs, mainly because they have De Zerbi and a collection of Premier League‑ready new signings. They have certainly put themselves under pressure for the visit of Charlton. A relevant statistic: Spurs have won one domestic home game in 2026 – against Everton on the final day of last season which enabled them to avoid relegation.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

De Zerbi made the point that he and the squad had “started the project right now, not last season”. Which was when he was parachuted in with seven games to go; he picked up 11 points to dodge the unthinkable. “Last season, we fought to stay up,” he said. The inference was that it would take rather more to become a proper team.

On the other hand, the experiences of the previous campaign do offer reassurance. “Maybe last season was a tougher challenge to stay up than this season,” De Zerbi said. “I said to the players: last season, in a worse situation, we showed character, we showed balls. We showed pride and quality. Now we have to stay calm and to analyse better the situation – not to have an emotional reaction. We have to be intelligent.”

What De Zerbi craves is consistency, which he defined as being five wins in a row. It seems a distant goal after Brentford but De Zerbi has faith. What it will take is a change to the collective mentality. “We have to get used to winning games and games and games – we have to change habits from the last two seasons,” he said.

“For me, the Carabao Cup is like the Premier League. We are not in the condition to make differences [between the competitions]. We have to play well and get used to winning – and winning matches, not a match. We have to change the mood. And we can.”

De Zerbi said that Porro and Van de Ven will return as substitutes against Charlton and Solanke may start. James Maddison is out for two weeks with a shoulder injury suffered against Brentford. De Zerbi has a decision to make on Sávio. Victory is non-negotiable.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 5: Charlton Athletic
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 14th (NB: this is not necessarily Sophie Downey’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 3rd (WSL2)

Prospects

Just under 20 years since Charlton’s successful women’s team were disbanded after the men’s team’s relegation from the Premier League, they are finally back in the limelight and ready to make a name for themselves again.

Karen Hills’s side impressed for much of last season, going on a 27-game unbeaten streak and possessing the meanest defence in WSL 2. A mid-season blip harmed their race for the title, however, and they lost out to Birmingham City on the final day of the season, ultimately going through a playoff to achieve their goal of promotion. Beating Leicester in that game will have given Hills and her players confidence that they can compete. There will be no complacency, however, having seen how newly promoted sides have fared in recent history.

Six players have departed since last season, including the influential Katie Bradley But they have been replaced with a blend of knowhow and exciting young talent. The arrival of Ashleigh Neville and Emily van Egmond will bring experience to Hills’s dressing room. Leah Davidson’s and Grace Johnston’s arrivals from Australia are intriguing moves. Meanwhile, Sophie Whitehouse was the hero of the previous campaign and Charlton will be looking to the goalkeeper to again lead from the back. It is the attacking side of the game that perhaps causes the most concern. Charlton managed only 31 goals last season, the lowest of the WSL2’s top six.

Preparations got under way with a pre-season trip to Cádiz, a chance for a new-look side to come together. There is no doubt that the task to stay up is a challenging one, but a club that have defied the odds on more than one occasion will believe they can do it again.

Off-field picture

A record-breaking partnership has seen haircare brand Sofnfree become the women’s team’s official sleeve partner. The branding will feature on all playing and replica shirts this season, while content creation will be a focus as Charlton hope to access new and existing audiences. The club have also launched their first women’s-centric TikTok channel. The news, however, that ownership group Global Football Partners have put the club up for sale could cause a bit of instability in the short term.

The manager

Reaching the Women’s Super League was part of the five-year plan Hills had when she was appointed in 2021, bringing a club close to her heart back into the limelight. The 51-year-old represented Chartlon for six years as a player, winning the FA Cup in 2005. This is the second time in Hills’s coaching career she has guided a team to the top flight, having previously done so with Tottenham in 2019, and watching Charlton walk out at the Valley against Liverpool on 6 September will inevitably be an emotional moment for her.

View image in fullscreen Karen Hills has guided a club into the top flight for the second time after have done so with Spurs in 2019. Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Alamy

Star signing

Only three months ago, Neville was lining up against Charlton in the promotion playoff. Now she is a fully fledged Addick, joining from Leicester on a two-year deal. The full-back brings with her a wealth of experience having made more than a century of appearances in the WSL. The majority of those were under Hills at Tottenham after arriving there from Coventry United. A tough-tackling, intuitive defender, Neville never shirks a challenge and has the ability to push forward. She will also be a strong leader in the dressing room.

Stat attack

Despite finishing third in WSL2, Charlton kept the joint-most clean sheets and conceded the fewest goals in the division. No club saved as high a percentage of their shots on target faced, with Whitehouse playing every minute. She saved four penalties in the playoff shootout, too.

Set for a breakthrough

Johnston was named Charlton’s first signing of the summer during a transfer window that has seen many A-League players depart for Europe. The versatile young full-back arrives at the Valley hoping to make her mark on English football after three seasons with Perth Glory. She impressed during her time with her home town club, played every minute of last season, winning the club’s 2026 best young player award. Johnston’s form led to her being called up to the Young Matildas in 2023, representing the under-20s and now the under-23s. She was an integral member of the squad that won the Asean Women’s Championship last year.

What they say …

“I know what Karen’s about and vice versa; she knows what I bring. I’m really looking forward to working with her again” – Ashleigh Neville

Where are they playing their home games?

Charlton will play their home games at the Valley for a third consecutive season. Season-ticket sales started almost immediately after their successful promotion push. Alcohol will also still be allowed in the stadium, with an alcohol-free section established. Other fan activations include giving supporters the opportunity to sponsor a player.

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and nitrous oxide possession
Sports.content:
The former England forward Raheem Sterling has been charged with dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after a crash involving a Lamborghini on the motorway, police have said.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight constabulary said the charges followed a single-vehicle collision on the M3 southbound, near Minley interchange, on 28 May. The 31-year-old is accused of dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen.

The force said that no other vehicles were involved in the collision and no injuries were reported. Sterling, from Berkshire, is due to appear at Basingstoke magistrates court for a hearing on 15 September.

Quick Guide How do I 

He scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate’s side to reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the Euro 2020 final. Sterling came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut and moved in 2015 to Manchester City, with whom he won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup.

Sterling left for Chelsea in 2022 but after falling out of favour he spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal. After leaving Stamford Bridge, he joined the Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of last season. He is now without a club.

In the 2021 Queen’s birthday honours, Sterling was made an MBE for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out strongly against racism on and off the pitch.

Sports.title: After Dom Ballard’s backheel, what is the earliest goal of the season? | The Knowledge
Sports.content:
“After watching Dom Ballard’s backheel volley for Bristol City against Birmingham in game week two of the Championship, it begs the question: what’s the earliest in a season a goal has gone on to win goal of the season?” asks Ricardio Sentulio.

There is no doubting Dom Ballard’s outrageous flick for Bristol City at Birmingham City should be a Puskás contender, especially with his finish kissing the crossbar on its way in, and has a very good chance of being the best goal scored in the 2026-27 Championship season, even though there is a long way to go.

Ballard’s wondergoal was scored on 22 August, on gameweek two. Eleven years ago to that day, Marco Matias notched this ridiculous effort for Sheffield Wednesday at Leeds United, although it should be said that Yorkshire derby was gameweek four, so technically later in the 2015-16 season than Ballard’s. Matias was given the goal of the season gong in April 2016.

The earliest Championship goal of the season we could find was the 2022-23 effort from Ismaïla Sarr for Watford. The Senegalese, now at Palace, scored from the halfway line to stun West Brom on the opening day (8 August). It doesn’t get much earlier, especially as Sarr’s strike was just 12 minutes into the match.

David Beckham’s famous goal for Manchester United against Wimbledon in 1996-97, lobbing Neil Sullivan from the halfway line – later voted the best of that Premier League campaign – was also on the opening day of the league season but came later in the year (11 days after Sarr) and also in the 87th minute (so 75 minutes later than Sarr in the match).

View image in fullscreen A 21-year-old David Beckham, there, on his way to superstardom. Photograph: Tony O’Brien/Action Images/Reuters

In Scotland, the 2017-18 SPFA goal of the season was given to Kieran Tierney for Celtic versus Kilmarnock, also on 8 August (2017) in the League Cup. Even though that is the same date as Sarr’s strike, the cup tie actually came three days after Celtic’s opening league game, a 4-1 win over Hearts on 5 August 2017. We could also mention that Celtic’s Jota once scored a goal of the month (for August even though the goal was in July) for Celtic against Aberdeen (31 July 2022, game one).

We finish with a goal that probably doesn’t quite fit into this category but is too good to ignore or forget. Schalke’s goal of the year (not season, it should be stated) in 2013 came as early as on 27 July but comes with three caveats: a) it was in a pre-season friendly; b) it was by a player that wasn’t even on Schalke’s books at the time of scoring; and c) it was a tap-in.

After two successful years at Schalke, Raúl had joined Al-Sadd, with a pre-season friendly arranged as part of the deal. So when Al-Sadd travelled to Gelsenkirchen on 27 July 2013, Raúl agreed to play the first half for his new side and the second half for Schalke. The Spaniard scored twice for the latter, the first of which was a textbook right-place-right-time finish from two yards out. To understand why it was voted Schalke’s goal of the year, you are going to have to check out the assist from a teenage Julian Draxler.

Have you any earlier examples from further afield? Mail us with your questions and answers.

Spinning plates

“Has a club’s player-manager ever been called up for an international cap, or travelled to play during an international break in the club season?” asks Frederick Sondheimer-Acosta.

Let’s start with a couple of famous examples from the Scotland team of the mid-1980s. “Kenny Dalglish became Liverpool player-manager in the summer of 1985 and subsequently played a few games for Scotland, including the first leg of their World Cup playoff win against Australia,” writes Dom Miller. “He won his 100th cap against Romania in March 1986 and was initially selected for the World Cup squad but withdrew due to a knee injury picked up in the FA Cup final (there has always been a suspicion he didn’t go because his mate Alan Hansen wasn’t picked). Dalglish won his last two caps in the autumn of 1986.”

View image in fullscreen Player-manager Kenny Dalglish (top right) and Liverpool celebrate winning the 1985-86 First Division at Stamford Bridge. Dalglish scored the winning goal to beat Chelsea and clinch the title. Photograph: David Cannon/Getty Images

Scotland, with Alex Ferguson in temporary charge after the tragic death of Jock Stein, did have a player-manager in their squad for the World Cup. Graeme Souness was appointed by Rangers in April and played the first two games at Mexico 86, when Scotland were a little unfortunate to lose to Denmark and West Germany. But Souness struggled with the altitude, saying he never felt worse on a football field than during the West Germany game, and Ferguson left him out of their final group match against Uruguay.

Another mighty, all-purpose midfielder, Johnny Giles, went one better than Souness. “Perhaps uniquely, Giles held player-manager positions for club and country simultaneously,” writes Bruce Mair. “He was player-manager of the Republic of Ireland, a part-time post, from May 1973 until March 1980 while playing for Leeds United (1973-75) and serving as player-manager of both West Bromwich Albion (1975-77) and Shamrock Rovers (1977-80). Giles selected himself for 24 of his 59 international appearances.”

Those are the most high-profile examples in Britain and Ireland, but there are dozens more cases – thanks to Bruce Mair, in particular, for doing so much work on this. We’ve picked some of the more interesting examples:

Andy Aitken “The earliest player-manager I can find,” writes Bruce. “Won three caps for Scotland while player-manager of Middlesbrough, 1907-08, and three more when player-manager/secretary at Leicester Fosse (now Leicester City), 1910-11.

Orvar Bergmark “Played 41 internationals for Sweden, including their run to the 1958 World Cup final, while player‑manager of Örebro between 1958 and 1961.”

Gunnar Gren “Seventeen caps for Sweden while player-manager of Örgryte IS, 1957-58. A teammate of Orvar Bergmark in the Swedish side that reached the 1958 World Cup final.”

Stuart Pearce “Capped twice for England in 1997 during his stint as caretaker player-manager at Nottingham Forest.”

Fanny Vágó “Hungary’s most‑capped women’s international made 19 appearances for her country while player‑manager of Ferencvárosi TC between 2021 and 2023.”

Elisha Scott “Liverpool legend won four caps for Northern Ireland while player-manager of Belfast Celtic at the tail end of his career, 1934-36.”

John Toshack “Six appearances for Wales as Swansea City player-manager in 1979.”

Jim Platt “Played twice for Northern Ireland in 1984 as player-manager of Ballymena United and made one further appearance as player-manager of Coleraine in 1986. Member of Northern Ireland’s 1986 World Cup squad.”

Knowledge archive

“Has there ever been an occasion where a major team has been disrupted by jury service, with either a manager or a player being called up during the season?” James Schofield asked back in May 2018.

“Plymouth’s Welsh international Carl Fletcher once tried to argue he couldn’t sit on a jury as he was too well known,” answered Andy Carswell. “According to reports in 2010, Judge Francis Gilbert told the midfielder that being Plymouth captain was not sufficient reason to excuse him, and that he had enough time to travel to Cheltenham for a Johnstone’s Paint Trophy tie after completing his duties. Fletcher argued that his position meant he was in a position of potentially being threatened, saying: ‘I don’t want anything to come back on me for sitting on a jury.’ His protests fell on deaf ears, with Judge Gilbert adding: ‘Lots of well-known people, some more famous than you, have been required to sit on juries.’”

James Perch had just helped Newcastle United to fifth place in 2012 but was also forced to cut short a holiday to Dubai after learning of his higher calling. “I’ve got jury service, unless I can be excused,” he told the club website. “It’s killed my holiday a bit, but at the minute I’m set to be in court at the end of May.”

Can you help?

“As someone who occasionally has to search for football stadiums to find directions and the like, I always enjoy that people take the time to rate their experience of visiting a football ground,” begins our own Will Unwin. “Hull City, for example, have 4.3 stars from 3,655 reviews. I therefore ponder … which ground has the highest and lowest Google rating?”

“I was surprised, staggered in fact, to see Nottingham Forest as the 18th team in the Guardian season previews,” writes Ross Connett. “I associate 18th place with the likes of Tottenham or West Ham, never a team beginning with N, just scraping over halfway into the alphabet. Has there ever been a more ‘early alphabet team’-dominated Premier League?”

“During Fulham v Chelsea, the previous jobs of both the opposing managers was coincidentally at the same club, Real Madrid,” notes Sarang Satish. “Are there other times this has happened?”

“Who has scored the highest percentage of their professional goals in hat-tricks?” asks Michael D.

“Last weekend every match in the Gibraltar league was a draw,” mails Stephen Hogg. “There are very few teams in the league, however. What’s the biggest league where this has happened?”

“This season Istanbul has six clubs in the Turkish top flight,” starts Vasco Wackrill. “What is the record number of top-flight clubs supplied in a season by a non-capital city?”

“Three of Kevin Lisbie’s sons are playing professionally; in the Championship (Kyrell, Millwall), in League One (Kyreece, Reading) and League Two (Kaion, Colchester United),” writes Stuart Willsher. “Have we ever had four brothers playing in all four top English divisions?”

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Jean-Philippe Mateta to Aston Villa?
Sports.content:
Liam Delap may not have broken any records during his time with Chelsea but he is setting one on his way out the door. The England youth international is thought to be breaking Nottingham Forest’s transfer fee record with Oliver Glasner bringing him in for an expected £50m. The fee comes despite a disappointing 2025-26 season with the 23-year-old striker scoring only one Premier League goal.

Injury problems with his shoulder and hamstring did not help but the lack of return means the Blues were open to selling the striker and Forest have taken the bait. If Delap does sell for £50m it also means Chelsea will make a £20m profit on the player after buying him from Ipswich for £30m in 2025.

Delap isn’t the last deal Forest want to get over the line before Monday’s deadline day either as they are interested in Corinthians and Brazil midfielder André.

One story that is gathering momentum like a ball in snow is Jean-Philippe Mateta moving to Aston Villa. The Villans have made Crystal Palace an offer for the France striker but it is a long way off what the London club would like.

A departure that could finance Mateta’s move could be that of Ollie Watkins, though it is one that has shocked Villa. It has been extensively reported the English international has interest from Saudi club Al-Hilal with his signature set to be worth about £59.8m. Villa are close to agreeing the move and it is understood Watkins would have an annual salary of £12m.

With deadline day approaching, last-minute signings will come out of the woodwork at every turn. Let’s rattle through some. Manchester United are interested in Stuttgart defender Finn Jeltsch, Newcastle have submitted a bid for Lille winger Matias Fernandez-Pardo, West Ham defender El Hadji Malick Diouf may play in the Premier League again with Brentford close to a deal for the Senegalese player, newly promoted Hull have agreed a move to sign Ilyas Ansah from Union Berlin in a deal worth £20m and Tottenham are pushing to sign Omar Marmoush from Manchester City.

If Spurs did get that move over the line for the Egypt forward then the club’s spend this summer would be close to £400m. It is no wonder fans looked lost for words at Tottenham’s 3-0 loss to Brentford last weekend.

We started with Chelsea so let’s end with the Blues. Enzo Fernández, who was met with a wall of boos when Chelsea played Fulham in their opening fixture, may not play in London for much longer. Manchester City will submit a bid for the Argentina midfielder before deadline day. If they do, it could be the biggest transfer of the summer so far with Chelsea reportedly wanting £120m for the 25-year-old.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

So Fernández may travel up the M1 and M6 but the boos are likely to follow him after he scored and showboated in England’s defeat to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final.

Sports.title: When is the Europa League draw? Premier League trio ready to make history
Sports.content:
When is the Europa League draw? Premier League trio ready to make history

The draw for the league phase of this season's Europa League takes place this week.

Sunderland, Bournemouth, and Crystal Palace will find out their fate in the initial stages of the continental competition.



3 Crystal Palace tasted European glory last season after beating Rayo Vallecano in the Conference League final Credit: Getty

The Cherries are set to play European football for the first time in their club's history.

The Black Cats make their return to continental football for the first time in 53 years after finishing seventh-place last season.

Additionally, the Eagles will also be in the competition following their success in the Conference League.



They could face various European giants such as Juventus, AC Milan, and Bayer Leverkusen who missed out on Champions League qualification.

However, the Premier League sides cannot go head-to-head in the league phase due to teams from the same country not being able to be drawn together.



Teams are also unable to play two teams from the same country in a single league phase campaign.

When is Europa League draw?

The Europa League draw will take place on Friday, August 28 at 12pm BST in Monaco.



Pots for the draw will be confirmed after the second leg of the Europa League play-off round on Thursday.

The Conference League draw will also take place on the same day.

The Conference League draw will feature the likes of last season’s losing Europa League finalists SC Freiburg, Dutch giants Ajax, and Serie A side Atalanta

3 The Europa League will once again follow a Swiss System for the draw Credit: AFP

How to watch Europa League draw?

The draw will be live on talkSPORT.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.



Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Additionally, talkSPORT's live blog will also be following the confirmed fixtures.



The Europa League draw will be broadcast on TNT Sports 4 and will be live streamed for free on Uefa.com.

The live broadcast of the draw will get underway at 12:00 BST.

3 Emery guided Aston Villa to the Europa League last season, and will now compete in the Champions League Credit: Getty

How does the league phase draw work?

The clubs will be split into four pots based on their Uefa club coefficient ranking, with 36 teams in the competition and the sides are set to play eight times.

Pot 1

Bayer Leverkusen

Juventus

AC Milan

AZ Alkmaar

Olympiacos

Real Sociedad

Marseilles

Pot 1 or 2

Union Saint-Gilloise

Pot 2

Celtic

Sparta Prague

Rennes

Pot 2 or 3

Sturm Graz

Crystal Palace

Sunderland

Bournemouth

Pot 3 or 4

Celta Vigo

TSG Hoffenheim

Torreense

Hapoel Be'er Sheva

NEC

The line-up for the competition includes 11 sides who qualified for the tournament automatically due to league position, as well as last years Conference League winners, Crystal Palace.



There will also be 12 clubs who progressed through qualifying and 12 teams who dropped down from the Champions League third qualifying round and play-offs, including Celtic.

Teams will play eight games in total in the Europa League - two teams from each pot, facing four sides at home and four away.

Sports.title: Omar Marmoush deal ‘certain’ to trigger instant exit for Tottenham star
Sports.content:
Omar Marmoush's imminent arrival at Tottenham Hotspur is bad news for one of the club's current forwards.

That is according to talkSPORT's Alan Brazil and Ally McCoist, who believe Richarlison is now a 'certainty' to leave Spurs this summer.

3 Richarlison is a 'certainty' to leave Spurs according to Brazil and McCoist Credit: Getty

Marmoush is on the verge of completing a move to north London from Manchester City.

The Egypt striker has been given permission to undergo a medical ahead of a season-long loan switch with an obligation to buy.

Once made permanent, Spurs will pay an initial £50million plus up to £10million in add-ons.

However, his arrival could spell the end of Richarlison's time at Tottenham with the transfer deadline fast approaching.

The 29-year-old is into the final year of his current contract having joined the club from Everton in 2022.

Premier League sides have until 11pm on Tuesday to conclude their summer transfer business.

Will Richarlison leave Spurs?

Brazil and McCoist reacted to Marmoush' move to Spurs live on Wednesday's talkSPORT Breakfast show.

The former believes it spells the end of Richarlison's time at the club, admitting: "I think Richarlison is a certainty to leave."

His co-host agreed, with McCoist replying: "Yes, I would guess that would be the case."

Brazil then added: "He looks a moody git doesn't he? He's really moody, like the whole world's against him.

3 Marmoush is set to join Spurs on loan from City with an obligation to buy Credit: Getty

"Sometimes he looks as if he's like, 'I don't care,' and then other times he can be brilliant, but he's gone."

Meanwhile, McCoist explained: "I think he's leaving. I don't think there's any doubt about that, I think he's going to go to pastures new."

Richarlison at Spurs

Richarlison has scored 32 goals in 134 appearances since joining Spurs four years ago.

He was part of the side which ended their 17-year wait for a trophy by winning the Europa League in 2025.

Speculation surrounding his future comes just days after he started their opening weekend defeat to Brentford.

Dominic Solanke replaced Richarlison in attack for Roberto De Zerbi's side during their 3-0 away loss on Saturday.

3 Richarlison has entered the final year of his current Spurs deal Credit: Getty

As for Marmoush, he has 10 goals and five assists in 37 Premier League outings for City.

Since arriving at the Etihad Stadium from Eintracht Frankfurt in January 2025, he has also won both the FA Cup and Carabao Cup.

Sports.title: Man City obliterate Premier League transfer record and give Ayyoub Bouaddi legend’s shirt number
Sports.content:
Manchester City have made Morocco star Ayyoub Bouaddi the most expensive teenager in Premier League history - by some distance.

The 18-year-old has officially joined City from Lille in a deal thought to be worth £86million.



2 Bouaddi caught the eye in North America over the summer Credit: Getty

It obliterates the previous record fee for a player under the age of 20 in England's top-flight, previously held by Romeo Lavia following his £58m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Bouaddi established himself as one of the hottest young players in Europe during the 2026 World Cup.

French football fans have known about his talents for some time after he burst onto the scene with Lille in 2023.



Most expensive Premier League teens Ayyoub Bouaddi— Lille to Manchester City (2026): £86.0m Romeo Lavia— Southampton to Chelsea (2023): £58.0m Leny Yoro— Lille to Manchester United (2024): £52.0m Anthony Martial— Monaco to Manchester United (2015): £49.8m Archie Gray— Leeds United to Tottenham Hotspur (2024): £40.0m

“I would say I am a player who plays for the team,” Bouaddi said upon signing for City.

“I am a really collective player.

“I try to put my teammate in the best position and to give everything every time for the team.



“I think the most important aspect is to try to balance the team, [to] help your teammates.

“We know as a No.6 that you’re not going to score 20 goals in a season; well it can happen but it’s quite rare.



“So, you know you have to balance the team and do everything for the team and do your job.”

The Moroccan was handed the No.32 shirt - made famous by City hero Carlos Tevez.

And he revealed now was the right time to make the step up in his career.

“I think it was the right time because I was good in Lille,” the 18-year-old added.



“I felt very good, but I felt it was the right moment to step over.

“I started playing really quite young at six-years-old.

“I was in Creil, a small city in France. Then I went in Lille when I was 14 years old. I played in the Academy and then I started playing with the First Team.

“Then I started playing Champions League, Europa League, Conference League, World Cup. And today I’m here.

2 The Moroccan star became the youngest Ligue 1 player since 1981 when he made his league debut for Lille Credit: Getty

“I am really, really happy – really proud to be here at one of the greatest clubs in the world and I hope everything is going to be right in the future.



“Coming to City I think was the right thing to do and I am really happy and proud to be here.”

Sports.title: EFL manager issues public apology to fanbase after ‘painful evening’ in Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
EFL manager issues public apology to fanbase after ‘painful evening’ in Carabao Cup

Chris Davies has issued a direct apology to Birmingham City fans after his side suffered a 6-1 defeat by Brentford.

Callum Wilson scored his first goal for the Bees on his debut after six minutes to begin the hammering.



3 Gray scored Birmingham's only goal of the match Credit: Getty

Although Demarai Gray brought the Blues level in the 28th minute, Keith Andrews' side restored their lead just six minutes later.

Brentford then tore the hosts apart, extending their advantage through goals from Aaron Hickey, Nathan Collins, Mikkel Damsgaard, and Igor Thiago.

The west London outfit began their Premier League campaign with a dominant victory over Tottenham on Sunday.



They now await the third round draw that takes place on Wednesday night following the conclusion of Preston vs Everton.

'A painful evening'

Following the match, the Birmingham City manager said: "My message to supporters tonight is 'sorry'. It's not very pleasant and I can understand how frustrating it is for them.



"It was a very tough evening for us, a painful evening, and incredibly disappointing to lose a game 6-1 at home.

"There were many situations where we were just not good enough to compete and I take ultimate responsibility for it - and the players will have to do it in their own minds.



"We were beaten by a team a long way ahead of us in every aspect. Was 6-1 a fair reflection? Probably."

Davies remains focused on achieving the club's target of promotion to the Premier League, though the Blues have endured a frustrating start to their Championship campaign.

3 Birmingham have high hopes in the Championship this season Credit: Getty

So far, they have logged two goalless draws against Sheffield United and Bristol City.



The Blues are among the favourites for a long awaited promotion to the top-flight after finishing 10th place last season.

They now are preparing for their next fixture at the Racecourse Ground against Wrexham on Friday night - just three days' time.

Due to the fixture being selected for live television broadcast, the Blues are forced to navigate two competitive matches inside a four-day window.

The Red Dragons are currently on equal points to Davies' side after only acquiring two points from the first two fixtures.



However, Phil Parkinson's men benefit from extended rest after being eliminated from the Carabao Cup first round by Middlesbrough earlier in August.

Meanwhile, Andrews was thoroughly impressed by how clinical his team was.

3 Andrews has enjoyed a fantastic start to the season Credit: Getty

The Bees boss said: "I didn't really blink an eyelid making so many changes.



"There is a huge narrative around cup games with coaches making changes but with the squad we have, there are fine margins between who plays and doesn't play.

"We needed to compete really hard to play the game we wanted. I thought overall we produced a really good performance."

Sports.title: Ange Postecoglou explains why he took furious Cristiano Ronaldo off before 10-man comeback
Sports.content:
Ange Postecoglou explains why he took furious Cristiano Ronaldo off before 10-man comeback

Cristiano Ronaldo stormed off the pitch at half-time before Al Nassr produced an improbable comeback in their latest outing.

The Saudi Pro League champions recovered from 2-0 down to beat Al Ettifaq away from home on Tuesday night.

3 Ronaldo was substituted at half-time after storming off the pitch against Al Ettifaq Credit: X

Their victory came despite playing over 75 minutes with 10 men after goalkeeper Bento was sent off.

A frustrating first half saw Ange Postecoglou's side trailing by two goals at the break.

Ronaldo was visibly angered as he left the field before being substituted ahead of the second half.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner threw his arms in the air and ripped off his captain's armband as he headed down the tunnel.

Postecoglou responded by withdrawing the veteran forward, who is planning to retire next summer, ahead of the restart.

In Ronaldo's absence, Al Nassr produced a late fightback with three goals in the final 20 minutes to snatch all three points.

A brace from Sadio Mane either side of Abdulelah Al Amri's equaliser was enough to see off a spirited Al Ettifaq.

The result maintains Al Nassr's 100 per cent record under Postecoglou as they remain top of the table after three matches.

Postecoglou explains Ronaldo substitution

Following the match, the former Tottenham Hotspur manager addressed his decision to take Ronaldo off.

Speaking to reporters, he admitted: "With Cristiano, we know he hasn't played a lot of football.

3 Postecoglou justified his decision to withdraw Ronaldo after Al Nassr's comeback win Credit: AFP

"So I think with 10 men to have him out there after 45 minutes, he did a great job for us in the first half.

"But we needed a different approach in the second half and I try and help them, but it's really the players.

"The players are the ones who out there have the belief and the courage to still play.

"You can see that in this humidity, how hard it is to run and keep having an effort and I thought the players were outstanding."

The match had been Ronaldo's first start of the campaign and only his second appearance since the World Cup.

He previously came off the bench to score against Al Riyadh on Friday.

However, the 41-year-old missed each of his side's opening two fixtures this term.

Al Nassr on form

Despite his absence, Al Nassr saw off both Al Fateh and Al Diriyah in the league and King's Cup, respectively.

Prior to Friday's win, Ronaldo had not played competitively since Portugal's round of 16 loss to Spain on July 6.

He could make his second start of the season as soon as this Friday as Al Nassr host Al Taawoun.

They currently sit two points clear at the summit of the Saudi Pro League, with four wins from four under Postecoglou in all competitions.

The Australian was appointed on a two-year deal by the reigning champions in July.

3 Ronaldo had made his first competitive start since July 6 on Tuesday night Credit: AFP

His arrival followed the departure of title-winning boss Jorge Jesus at the end of last season.

talkSPORT verdict

Alan Brazil and Ally McCoist gave their own reactions to Ronaldo's antics live on Wednesday's talkSPORT Breakfast show.

After hearing Postecoglou's comments, McCoist responded: "He's got to be like that, doesn't he? He doesn't want to slag off anybody."

However, Brazil saw the funny side, quipping: "Well, if he does slag him off then Cristiano just buys the club and sacks him."

McCoist then added: "The fact of the matter is, we're making a big deal out of this because it's Ronaldo.

"It wouldn't have mattered who he was taking off, if a person deserved to come off and you end up winning the game 3-2, it is the correct decision."

Sports.title: ‘Murder’ – Alan Brazil reveals night from hell immediately after Celtic horror show
Sports.content:
Alan Brazil endured the night from hell after watching Celtic crash out of the Champions League - before arriving late to work.

The talkSPORT co-host has been left in disbelief by the Hoops' 5-4 play-off defeat on aggregate to Austrian outfit LASK.



4 Celtic will be playing Europa League football after failing to qualify for the Champions League Credit: Getty

Martin O'Neill's side led 3-0 on aggregate having eased to victory last week in Glasgow, and they got off to the perfect start on Tuesday night after Callum McGregor's 23rd minute opener.

But they somehow blew a four-goal lead, with LASK taking the game to extra-time before scoring a winner through Samuel Adeniran's 109th minute long range effort.

It means that Celtic have now crashed out in the Champions League play-offs for a second successive season, with the Scottish giants set for another campaign of Europa League football.



If that wasn't bad enough for Brazil, he then struggled to get to sleep, leading him to head down to London from Ipswich early in the night.

Meanwhile, problems on the road led to him getting an even later night's sleep in the capital - leaving Rangers icon Ally McCoist to be on solo presenting duties on the Sports Breakfast show.



Why was Alan Brazil late for work?

With Brazil not in the talkSPORT studio McCoist quipped: "So the question is this, is Brazil late this morning after Celtic's embarrassment?"

Brazil would eventually arrive a few minutes later, where he would discuss his night from hell.



After a cheerful McCoist asked his colleague, 'How are you pal?,' the ex-Manchester United forward simply replied: "Murder."

Keen to get an excuse out of Brazil, McCoist then said: "Traffic? Tired? Slept in? Just depressed?"

To which Brazil remarked: "I'm not depressed, I'm not depressed, I cannot sleep."

4 Celtic boss O'Neill watched his side capitulate in real time against LASK Credit: Getty



He continued: "I was in Ipswich, at 11 o'clock [pm] I thought, 'This is ridiculous,' I went to bed at 7 [pm], could not sleep.

"I've got this... it's a long story... sciatica as well I've got... and then at 11 o'clock I said, 'Right, I'm going.'

"She [Jill Brazil, Alan's wife], didn't know [I left], so she's gone crazy this morning, woke up, 'Where am I?'

Brazil added: "And then coming into London, ahh, road shut, anyway, I got here, straight to bed, could not sleep.



"Up at 2 [am], 3 [am] and then I popped two aspirin plus or something - I suddenly woke up at 5.40 [am], I went, ' 'Ahh no!'"

He then proceeded to discuss Celtic's horror performance, remarking: "I said after the first game it's not over, but then when Celtic scored, I thought, 'Well that's it surely.'

4 Celtic have now failed to reach the Champions League group stage in the last two seasons Credit: Getty

"Unbelievable, it's unbelievable, the punters were going crazy at the board again, terrible.



"When McGregor scores, you think, 'Well, that's it, just lock up, keep the ball, slow it down,' they [LASK] were good at Parkhead though."

Where does Celtic's loss rank amongst their worst defeats in history?

Brazil then declared that the 5-1 loss on the night will go down as one of the Hoops' worst in European football.

He said: "In the importance of the game and the money side of it, probably the worst, I would suggest.

"I was screaming at the telly, the first leg, 'We need a third, we need a third, we need a third,' and we got it.



"And then when McGregor scores an away goal, you think, 'OK, done, it's going to be backs against the wall, but it should be enough,' shocking.

4 LASK have inflicted arguably Celtic's darkest day in European football Credit: Getty

"I don't want to be too harsh on players, because it's early on in the season, but if you got to look at some of the characters and say, 'Hold on a minute, do you want to play Champions League football? Do you want to play? Do you want it that much?'

"Or is it, 'A bit unlucky, they're a good side...'"

Celtic will now be looking to return to winning ways when they host Falkirk in the Scottish Premiership on Saturday.

Sports.title: Frank Lampard handed instant survival boost as new signing backed to make big Premier League impact
Sports.content:
Frank Lampard handed instant survival boost as new signing backed to make big Premier League impact

New Coventry signing Sidiki Cherif has been tipped to make a big impact in the Premier League this season.

Frank Lampard landed the 19-year-old striker from Fenerbahce for around £20m.

3 Cherif joined Coventry from Fenerbahce Credit: Getty

Cherif only joined Fener on a permanent deal this summer, with his loan from French side Angers including a mandatory purchase agreement.

He scored two goals in 12 Super Lig games after joining in January - but there is plenty of unrealised potential.

talkSPORT’s European football expert Andy Brassell said: “I personally think he will make a big, big impact in the Premier League. He was good when he arrived at Fenerbahce.

“Given that he was, because of their failure to sign any other senior strikers, immediately a senior striker, there's a lot to his game.

“He's really smart. But generally speaking, it's a big leap.”

Coventry have spent more than £100m this summer in a bid to stay in the Premier League after more than two decades away.

Their season got off to a tough start with a 3-0 defeat at defending champions Arsenal in what will likely be their hardest test of the campaign.

talkSPORT has been told that Lampard is not overly worried by that outing and there are plenty of positives to take.

Wrexham want Angers star

Another player who could be heading to English football via the Angers development route is Jacques Ekomie.

Wrexham are believed to have had a bid in the region of £8m for the left-back accepted, having faced competition from Championship rivals.

3 Ekomie is a target for Wrexham this summer Credit: AFP

The 23-year-old has made 36 Ligue 1 appearances since joining Angers from Bordeaux in July 2024.

Brassell warned there is a steep learning curve for all players joining from the French league as the traditional routes to step up are becoming increasingly tough.

He continued: “We've seen how difficult it is for defenders to adapt to the Premier League. We've seen how difficult it is from the very start.

“Angers is a bigger leap than Lyon. Ideally, Lyon are one of the better teams in the division.

I know the French League isn't as moneyed as it was. Not that it was ever replete with cash, but it's flat broke at the moment.

“Players going from Angers to hit that next level, that is a big ask. You are probably better off going to Marseille first, or Lyon or somewhere like that.

3 Lampard has signed a number of talented players this summer at Coventry Credit: Getty

“The problem being that Marseille and Lyon don't have the money to take you if you're a really good player at the moment.

“Angers are really, really good at developing players.”

Sports.title: Man United Confidential: Joshua Zirkzee will leave United with Aston Villa and Serie A duo circling, why Amazon documentary is doubling stars' workload and how club have slashed Old Trafford beer queues this season
Sports.content:
Joshua Zirkzee fully expects to leave Manchester United in the next week, Confidential understands.

While there is a feeling that United need more players through the door before Tuesday’s 11pm deadline following the shock opening-day defeat at newly promoted Hull City, there is an expectation that Zirkzee will go – most likely on loan.

A £36.5million signing from Bologna two years ago, Juventus have set their sights on taking Zirkzee back to Italy. There is interest from their Serie A rivals Napoli and Aston Villa have also enquired.

The 25-year-old Dutchman made just five starts in all competitions last season and was an unused substitute at the MKM Stadium on Saturday. Zirkzee is eager to get regular first-team minutes, and the sense around the player is that a compromise is required on all sides to facilitate a move.

Zirkzee is one of the most popular players in the dressing-room, but with his best position being as a No10 – the role occupied by captain Bruno Fernandes – opportunities to play are at a premium.

As for replacing Zirkzee, who has scored just nine times in 75 appearances for the club, United are prioritising a new left-back amid interest in Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde and 19-year-old Jorge Salinas of Racing Santander. But insiders are far from certain there will be any more incomings to add to £155million midfield trio Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba, and free-agent goalkeeper Karl Darlow.

Joshua Zirkzee is expected to leave Manchester United in the next week

After scoring on his United debut at home to Fulham two years ago, Zirkzee has added just eight more goals in 74 appearances

United announced the £70m signing of Carlos Baleba from Brighton on Tuesday but are not currently close to adding any more arrivals before the window closes next week

Double or Nothing!

Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary has doubled United’s broadcast commitments this season.

Filming began during the club’s pre-season camp in Dublin earlier this month and hit full flow last week, with crew working on the access-all-areas documentary now part of the furniture at Carrington and Old Trafford. The demands of producing the programme have dawned on those at a club which is already the biggest media draw in the Premier League for players and staff.

The Amazon documentary may be earning the club more than £10million, but it means United face twice the broadcasting demands as before, representing a real challenge in a season that could bring as many as 15 extra games following a return to Europe.

It’s understood that all the United stars have had to sign waivers giving permission to be filmed behind the scenes, and journalists covering the club have done likewise so that footage from Michael Carrick’s press conferences can be included.

MUTV’s studio boost

As much as Amazon are demanding a significant amount of United’s time, Confidential understands the new Snapdragon Studio at Carrington has been installed for the benefit of MUTV rather than the streaming giant.

The editing suite on the first floor of the training ground will be used by the club’s in-house TV station to produce the increasing amount of content United broadcast on their own channels. The equipment there is powered by Snapdragon as part of United’s £60million-a-year shirt sponsorship deal with California-based tech firm Qualcomm which is currently due to run until 2029.

Amazon will have to use their own facilities to produce the highly-anticipated docuseries on United which is due to air in the summer of 2027.

Sleeve it out

With Snapdragon on board as shirt sponsor for at least another three years, and Betway having recently agreed a record deal to have their name on United’s training kit, the club are now looking for a new sleeve sponsor.

United’s £20million-a-year partnership with DXC Technology ran out in May after four seasons, and they kicked off the new campaign at Hull on Saturday without branding on their sleeve for the first time in eight years.

The club were prepared to be patient last season when they went without a training-kit sponsor after the deal with Tezos lapsed, before cashing in on their return to the Champions League this season by signing the multi-year agreement with Betway. The deal, also believed to be worth £20m-a-year, is said to be the biggest standalone training kit or playing shirt sleeve deal in world football.

Reds escape rail chaos

United avoided the rail chaos that affected many of their 2,400 fans at Hull on Saturday by travelling back from Humberside on the team bus – although some players returned under their own steam.

United stars trudge off the pitch at the MKM Stadium after the 2-0 defeat at Hull City last Saturday

The Reds routinely take the train to games in London, and usually fly further afield, but the 200-mile round trip between Manchester and Hull meant that Carrick and his squad went there and back by bus.

It was just as well after the matchday announcer at the MKM Stadium appeared to take great pleasure in informing the United fans that the trains scheduled to depart from Hull for Manchester at 3.30pm and 5.03pm had been cancelled – much to the delight of the Hull supporters.

The team bus got away on time, but not before Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw were spotted walking across the car park towards their own transport. Confidential understands that several other United players did the same because they had plans for their day off on Sunday.

OT is pitch perfect

United may have requested to kick off the new season away from home so they could complete a major upgrade of the pitch at Old Trafford, but Confidential understands that the stadium would comfortably have been ready to host a game last weekend.

The turf has been relaid for the first time in 14 years – complete with new foundations and drainage system – and United have also taken steps to protect the players from injury by safeguarding the perimeter of the pitch.

The club confirmed earlier this summer that ‘the grass is being extended to provide a consistent surface at pitchside, and a layer of protection is being added to the brickwork at the foot of Old Trafford’s famous slope’.

There had been concerns over the ditch and perimeter wall that were created when the pitch was elevated in the 1990s, with players at risk of injury if they came off the grass at speed and collided with the advertising hoardings. Most recently, Benjamin Sesko hurt his shin in the victory over Liverpool in May, with the Slovenian only returning to action at Hull on Saturday.

United have also upgraded the home and away dugouts to increase the number of seats for substitutes and coaching staff from 16 to 20, in keeping with UEFA criteria ahead of the club’s return to the Champions League.

Benjamin Sesko hurt his shin after colliding with an advertising hoarding in the victory over Liverpool in May, with the Slovenian only returning to action at Hull on Saturday

All the work was completed in advance of United’s trip to Humberside, meaning the club could have played at Old Trafford last weekend after all, although insiders say the extra week will give the new turf – which is made up of 96 per cent natural grass and four per cent artificial fibres – more time to mature before Sunday’s home opener against Ipswich Town.

United have made the improvements despite pressing ahead with plans to build a new stadium to replace Old Trafford, hopefully by 2035.

The club have also improved the stadium experience for fans as part of new partnership with Levy, the sports and entertainment hospitality specialists. It aims to provide a better quality, faster service for supporters which has seen new draught beer taps installed around Old Trafford. There will be more self-service bars which will enable fans to tap their payment card and grab a beer, which should reduce queues and improve flow.

There will also be a wider range of dining options outside the ground, including a number of kiosks featuring independent Manchester vendors selling street food.

JJ passes Under 21s audition

Confidential was in position at Leigh Sports Village on Monday night to witness JJ Gabriel’s stunning competitive debut for the Under 21s.

Gabriel, still only 15, scored a sublime goal when he chipped Ipswich Town goalkeeper Woody Williamson from outside the area, and also added two assists for Victor Musa and Jaydan Kamason.

Michael Carrick and his assistant Steve Holland were among the small crowd in Leigh, and it was hard not to marvel at Gabriel’s display as he thrived in a No10 role.

The Under-21s played in a 4-2-3-1 system to mirror the first team, even playing without a recognised No9, much like Carrick did at Hull by using Matheus Cunha through the middle. That allowed Gabriel to play the Bruno Fernandes role. The expectation is that Gabriel will train regularly with the first team throughout the season while also playing a starring role in the Under 21s.

JJ Gabriel, still only 15, scores a sublime chip from the edge of the area against Ipswich Town Under 21s

He scored 29 times across 32 appearances last season, helping his team reach the FA Youth Cup and Premier League Under 18s Cup finals

He was outstanding for the Under 18s under Darren Fletcher last season despite starting it as a 14-year-old. He scored 29 times across 32 appearances, helping his team reach the FA Youth Cup and Premier League Under 18s Cup finals.

Carrick and Holland were beaming by full time. With a star like Gabriel on their hands, who could blame them?

Scouts flock to see Under 21s

It was noticeable just how many EFL scouts were there on Monday night to watch an Under 21s team that is still ripe for picking before next week’s deadline.

Kamason and Harry Amass, who started at right-back and left-back in the 5-0 win, are both expected to draw interest. Confidential understands that both are expected to leave, with permanent exits not being ruled out as both players draw significant interest in the Championship, with nothing left for either to gain in academy football.

United have cashed in on several young players this summer as Radek Vitek, Tyler Fredricson and Ethan Williams left the club permanently, with buy-back clauses and matching rights included as part of their exit packages.

Jaydan Kamason celebrates scoring the third goal in United Under 21s' 5-0 win over Ipswich

Harry Amass, who started at left-back on Monday against Ipswich, is also likely to leave United in the next week

New cyber threat warning

News that Premier League teams face a fine of up to £100,000 if they fail to follow new cybersecurity rules coming into effect this season revived memories of the attack on United in November 2020, which paralysed the club’s computer network.

Staff were forced to communicate by WhatsApp for several weeks after the ransomware attack crippled United’s email accounts and other systems, forcing the club to call in the National Cyber Security Centre for help.

It was never revealed how much the hackers demanded as a ransom – or if United paid up – but the NCSC said at the time that the biggest single loss to a sports organisation from cyber-crime was £4million. United are believed to have upgraded their cybersecurity since then in an attempt to prevent another breach. The new rules will be implemented in three phases through April 2029.

Jamie Akhtar, CEO and co-founder of CyberSmart, said: ‘This is an important shift for the Premier League. Cyber security is moving from being viewed primarily as an IT responsibility to becoming an enforceable element of club governance.

‘Football clubs hold significant volumes of sensitive supporter, employee and player data, while also relying on systems for ticketing, payments, stadium access and matchday operations.’

Wes & Pally at Salford

Given that United host Ipswich Town on Sunday, those at a loose end on Saturday need look no further than Salford Lads & Girls Club.

United are teaming up with the iconic club to host an open day where former players Wes Brown and Gary Pallister will be in attendance. The pair are hosting a Q&A at the event which will give fans the chance to buy limited edition adidas third shirts, which have been designed to celebrate the Salford club’s centenary year.

A football fun day, which starts at midday, for those after a football fix on Saturday.

Sports.title: It is an utter disgrace that Joe Root is left to unpick the deeply ugly booze and banter culture of denial and victimhood that Ben Stokes and Brendon McCullum have stitched into this England team: IAN HERBERT
Sports.content:
It is an utter disgrace that Joe Root is left to unpick the deeply ugly booze and banter culture of denial and victimhood that Ben Stokes and Brendon McCullum have stitched into this England team: IAN HERBERT

Unlock more of the best of our cricket coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

The spectral figure of Ben Stokes, lurking on the fringes of the latest tedious embarrassment for English cricket - Brydon Carse’s arrest at a Derby nightclub - said everything about the risible sense of denial and victimhood we were asked to stomach amid his walking away from the national team.

After the sulk-fest in which Stokes complained that media duties were stalling ‘a proper drink with the boys’ before a late-night altercation at a Chelsea nightclub, we were treated to a 140-minute soft focus PR interview with him on the For the Love of Cricket podcast, which Kevin Pietersen declared to be a terribly clever example of him choosing a player-owned business to open his heart to.

It was a safe space for Stokes to dissemble on the question of whether England had a drinking culture. ‘No, that's such an extreme thing to put on a team,’ he complained, before going on to discuss his own ‘bad relationships with alcohol’ in that thoroughly modern way, where you can infer it’s a two-way relationship and the alcohol is somehow partly to blame.

The depth of the drinking culture was spelt out to me two years ago by an individual whose partner had left the England set-up for another international sports side because she loathed the boys’ club air of entitlement so much. The depth of that culture needs no elaboration now. Ben Duckett at Noosa in Australia last December, Harry Brook in Wellington, New Zealand, in January, Stokes and Gus Atkinson at Chelsea’s Rex Rooms in June and now Carse at Molly Malone’s in Derby.

If Stokes had an iota of care for the England team he once led - or for his friend Joe Root, left to pick up the pieces - then he would have moved heaven and earth to ensure that his Durham team-mate Carse was nowhere near that nightclub on Saturday night.

An adult approach to Carse after Durham had just beaten Derbyshire would have gone along the lines of ‘Get yourself home. You’re in the England squad for a Test against Pakistan on Thursday.’

A 'hacked off' Joe Root has to discuss the latest ugly off-field incident involving one of his England players

Brydon Carse is put in handcuffs outside a Derby nightclub on Saturday night - five days before a Test match he could have been involved in

But the nightclub it had to be. Another evening’s ‘relationship with alcohol’ which concluded with Carse in handcuffs, Stokes skulking at the pillar and Matthew Potts, a third of the laughing boys, also adjacent. Prepare yourselves for another sugar-coated podcast on how it was all someone else’s fault, quite soon.

It’s been rather unfashionable to argue, as I have done for several years now, that there is something deeply unattractive about the booze and banter scene which Stokes gave full rein to as England captain.

The brilliance of his cricket seems to render him untouchable in the eyes of the majority on the social media channels, where all the power resides nowadays. We have to stomach a hagiographic narrative about Stokes’ ‘bravery’ and ‘courage’ - as if laying off the ales, making adequate preparations for a Test match and treating journalistic questions with a modicum of respect don’t even enter the equation.

Root’s return to the helm has served as a beautiful antidote to all that. A refreshing reminder that English cricket does not need a creed of boorish, alpha male entitlement to somehow ‘save’ it and give it a contemporary relevance. When Root first sat down to discuss his captaincy a few weeks back, you simply thanked God for the restoration of basic common sense.

His vocabulary felt like a return to the real world - the use of the words like ‘adult’ and ‘grown up’ speaking to the fact that neither is such a huge ask in an elite professional environment where South Africa and Australia lie up the road.

The need of a curfew to bring some decent behaviour was a dreadful look and Root immediately removed it. This felt like the recovery of a lost kind of Englishness. Proof to those of us who hated the way the national team we loved had been hijacked that we’d been entitled to make our argument.

Root also addressed the problem without appearing to lecture anyone. We were witnessing humility again. That first press conference, taken with the comfortable innings victory over Pakistan at Leeds, seemed like the start of an unpicking of the booze and banter culture stitched into England by Stokes and Brendon McCullum.

If Ben Stokes had an iota of care for the England team he would have ensured that his Durham teammate Carse was nowhere near that nightclub on Saturday night

Root also addressed the problem of Carse without appearing to lecture anyone. We were witnessing humility again

Molly Malone’s has taken him right back to square one and the fact that Root, who has never put a foot wrong off the pitch, found himself having to deal with the same old questions this week is nothing less than a disgrace.

Stokes, who never seems to be far away when trouble starts, will no doubt not see it that way. Some public contrition from him for not steering Carse away would have been appropriate. The silence has been deafening. Stokes is above all that sort of thing.

Root has declared himself ‘hacked off’ with the situation, which must be putting it mildly. In another necessary balancing act, he has made his displeasure with Carse quite clear, whilst being mindful to ask Stokes about ‘the emotional state’ of the bowler.

Carse has been emblematic of the worst of modern England. The player who had a three-month ban from cricket for betting on the sport in breach of regulations before he’d even bowled a ball in Test cricket.

The player who, sitting at a Perth cafe with Zak Crawley and Brook the morning after England lost the first Ashes Test inside two days last winter, put his hand in his pocket and sent thousands of dollars in cash flying into the air. Bystanders, including English cricket journalists in the place for a coffee, scrambled to grab the cash and return it to him.

As England head into their second Test under Root, the formidable on-field challenges of the future begin to loom large. Victory at Lord’s, to wrap up the series, would create the potential to experiment with the bowling lineup at Edgbaston with South Africa in mind.

Carse, with his flagrant disregard of Root’s words when he took the captaincy again, has no place in this team, either now or at any time in the future

Root and England managing director Rob Key in talks at Lord's - where cricket may not have been top of the agenda

If Root is to thrive against a competitive Test nation like that, then the virus of booze-related indiscipline must be expunged and players lacking the fundamental respect which ought to come with Test selection must have no place. Carse, with his flagrant disregard of Root’s words, has no place in this team, either now or at any time in the future.

Stokes, the man standing at the pillar, declared a wish to coach England in the future during that self-aggrandizing podcast appearance. To which the response must be, ‘Heaven help us.’

A cricketing force of nature he might be, yet the bombast and braggadocio which has diminished England will never be punctured if he returns with his current offended perspective.

Discipline, intelligence and rigour must be recovered if England are to remotely aspire to reclaim the Ashes. They need a new world, expunged of the rogue elements which have brought them here.

Sports.title: Brentford get their £35m man from West Ham, Villa expect Al Hilal to pay £50m asking price for Watkins, Liverpool explore other options with Brighton wanting £80m for Minteh and all options remain open for Grealish: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:

Sports.title: Man United's kit clanger: Club's rule-breaking shirt falls foul of Premier League laws on first game of season
Sports.content:
Man United's kit clanger: Club's rule-breaking shirt falls foul of Premier League laws on first game of season

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United have fallen foul of Premier League kit rules after one game of the season.

The Old Trafford outfit went into the current campaign without a sleeve sponsor, following the expiration of a £20m per year deal with DXC Technology which dates back to 2022.

However, Premier League rules dictate that clubs without a sleeve sponsor should display the competition’s badge on both arms.

And eagle-eyed observers have pointed out that United did not comply during their opening day defeat at Hull City, with one sleeve left blank.

While both the Premier League and United declined to comment, Daily Mail Sport understands that the club was given a polite reminder of the rule.

Premier League rules dictate clubs without a sleeve sponsor should display the competition’s badge on both arms - but Manchester United did not

The Premier League badge was shown on the other arm of United's shirts

It is also understood that the top-flight badge will be on both sleeves when United return to action against Ipswich at Old Trafford on Sunday.

United are seeking a new shirt sleeve sponsor, having had one for the past eight seasons.

The rule-break came on a chaotic opening day for United and manager Michael Carrick, with the surprise defeat by Hull drawing plenty of criticism - including from captain Bruno Fernandes.

After the match, the United captain complained to the media that his side had made the 'same mistakes as we did last season (in away matches)'. The Portugal midfielder added: 'Every away game we give too much of the ball to them. In the first 20 minutes, the goalkeeper was the one with the most touches.

'We needed to press more, be more aggressive, and then again we need to work on set plays and not concede these types of goals. Against these types of teams, they are waiting for that moment.'

Club legend Paul Scholes, however, took issue with Fernandes' comments on his podcast The Good, The Bad & The Football.

'I'd be interested to know what he means by them. What mistakes were they giving away?' the 51-year-old former player said.

'Especially when you perform the way he did as well, I think it's probably best to keep your mouth shut. He didn't have his best performance either.'

Scholes and former United forward Dion Dublin went further, suggesting that Fernandes, alongside team-mate Luke Shaw, who also claimed after the match that United went into the fixture underprepared, had undermined manager Michael Carrick.

Bruno Fernandes - pictured without the Premier League logo - was left disappointed

Shaw had said after the match: 'It’s not us and we knew it was coming. I think as a whole, as a group, collectively, we could prepare better. Especially knowing how good they are at set plays and what their dangers are.'

Reacting to the left-back's comments, Scholes said: 'Luke Shaw always says something. And that's a slight on your staff. That's a slight on your manager. If one of your players is saying that you'd be like f***ing hell, you'd have them in on Monday morning.'

Dublin said: 'You want silence. If your skipper has to speak then he has to speak, but then you make sure he says the things that don't open a can of worms. You just don't give anyone any ammunition because the ammunition is there from your performance.'

Scholes added: 'Those comments are not so much about respect but you speak about fear of managers and the things they've said, they're a slight on the manager and staff. As a player if we did that about Sir Alex, "we weren't prepared", f***ing hell, you'd be right in and he'd probably single you out in front of the full team.'
