Sports.title: Leeds co-owner Jed York escapes further action from UK football regulator - after arrest in Ohio prostitution sting when he tried to pay $140 for sex at trailer park
Sports.content:
Leeds co-owner Jed York escapes further action from UK football regulator - after arrest in Ohio prostitution sting when he tried to pay $140 for sex at trailer park

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York will not face action from the football regulator after being caught attempting to pay for sex.

The 46-year-old American spent a day in jail and was fined $1,150 (£844) after he was exposed in a police sting operation at a US trailer park.

Criminal convictions can lead to those involved being disqualified by the regulator and Premier League under the owners and directors’ test, which has recently been strengthened.

However, Daily Mail Sport understands that officials are aware of the development, but feel it does not meet the threshold for further investigation and potential action.

Under the test, offences which would trigger action include those resulting in a prison sentence of 12 months upwards and convictions for fraud and corruption.

Leeds are owned by 49ers Enterprises, of which York and Paraag Marathe, who takes a more hands on role in the running of the Yorkshire club, own more than 10 per cent.

Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York will not face action from the football regulator after being caught attempting to pay for sex

York, 46, was arrested on Sunday, spent a day in jail and was fined $1,150 (£844) after he was exposed in a police sting operation at a US trailer park in Ohio

According to the New York Post, court documents say York, who filed for divorce months before the arrest, ‘arranged to have sexual activity with [a] female in exchange for $140 (£103)’.

He replied to an advert but was arrested at the trailer park, in his native Ohio, by an agent from a human trafficking task force.

Initially, York was charged with engaging in prostitution, which was subsequently amended to disorderly conduct.

He was handed a one-day prison sentence, a $1,150 (£844) fine and agreed to complete an online course after pleading no contest. Such a plea is not an admission of guilt, rather an acceptance of the punishment.

York is the principal owner of the NFL’s San Francisco 49ers and chief executive. 49ers Enterprises acquired a 51 per cent stake in Rangers last year.

‘As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time,’ the 49ers said.

Leeds declined to comment.

Sports.title: The bitter battle of non-League's record transfer - which could collapse: 'Held hostage' club owner calls out 'tools downing' £1.5m star striker in 1,000-word programme notes rant
Sports.content:
The bitter battle of non-League's record transfer - which could collapse: 'Held hostage' club owner calls out 'tools downing' £1.5m star striker in 1,000-word programme notes rant

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The biggest transfer in non-League history is in jeopardy amid a public row between the Boreham Wood chairman and his star man Abdul Abdulmalik.

Abdulmalik, who scored and assisted in last season's National League play-off final defeat by Rochdale, is currently on strike at Boreham Wood as he tries to force an astonishing £1million-plus move to Swedish top-flight club Djurgarden.

Daily Mail Sport understands there is no agreement between the two clubs, despite Boreham Wood clearly outlining their demands.

Boreham Wood's valuation for the 23-year-old is thought to be over £1.5m plus significant add-ons. Djurgarden's latest bid reached £1.5m but was rejected.

In the programme for Thursday evening's match against Boston United, circulated to season ticket holders and obtained by Daily Mail Sport, Boreham Wood chairman Danny Hunter has said the transfer fee is agreed while add-ons are to be determined.

But it appears that while Boreham Wood may have agreed their own asking price internally, a club-to-club agreement has not been reached with Djurgarden having had multiple bids turned down and Boreham Wood unwilling to budge.

Seven-figure deals in the National League are extremely rare, with Jamie Vardy's £1m move from Fleetwood Town to Leicester City in 2012 the biggest initial fee received by a non-League club. Should Abdulmalik depart, he would become the most expensive non-league transfer.

Meanwhile, Hunter also accused Djurgarden of tapping up Abdulmalik, which can result in a transfer embargo.

Abdul Abdulmalik had a stellar 2025-26 season, scoring 17 goals and providing 10 assists as Boreham Wood reached the National League play-off final

The 23-year-old is trying to force an exit from Boreham Wood - refusing to train and play

In extensive programme notes - in which he devoted over 1000 words to the issue - the Boreham Wood chief went on to suggest there is every chance Abdulmalik remains at the club beyond the September 1 transfer deadline.

'At 64 years of age and having enjoyed 28 seasons here in the Chair, I know our supporters want an experienced owner to stand up to outside noise, to see passive-aggressiveness for what it is and not allow anything, except my own good conscience, to dictate what's right for our football club,' Hunter's notes read.

'I, of course, understand the new agent, player, family and advisors are not happy, as they are only thinking about Abdul and themselves, but that is very much their concern.

'I've now watched the behaviour of those concerned up close over the last three weeks. I've seen the constant leaks to Sky Sports and the press, but that's out of my control.

'I do understand that some people will think those press leaks will put me under pressure (they don't), but what I will say is that these things are unhelpful to all concerned, as they unsettle the player unnecessarily and just add to the noise, the me, me, me culture and poor behaviour.

'I'm old school and always believe that a transparent transfer negotiation must firstly begin with the interested (buying) club making contact with the parent club (us) in good faith. Only if those initial conversations between the clubs are positive can a deal further down the line be done.

'If a transfer is being initiated at the start by an agent or by a buying club using an agent, then one club (us), in this case, is usually kept in the dark before an offer is suddenly sent through. Remember, at that point the agent and the player have already agreed their deals, even though NO deal at that point has been struck between the two clubs.

'To be even clearer, if a potentially interested club knowingly contacts a contracted player through an agent, without his parent club's permission, and negotiates his deal, that could constitute an unauthorised approach under the relevant football regulations.

'If that happens, a player on most occasions has already had his head turned long before the parent club (us) even knows that the player has accepted his deal and long before a low-ball offer is on its way to the parent club.

'I now feel I'm being made out to be the bad guy here and slightly held hostage, as it's very late in the transfer window and I'm now forced into negotiating a transfer because the said player, on advice from others, has downed tools.

Boreham Wood chairman Danny Hunter feels he is being held 'hostage' by Abdulmalik

Hunter went on to accuse Djurgarden of tapping up Abdulmalik while making contradictory statements on negotations

Boreham Wood claim they have already dropped their asking price by £350,000 - their initial valuation was believed to be £2m

'In truth, I'm not happy with that, nor the silly press leaks after we stayed respectfully quiet and agreed to negotiate in good faith.

'However, with Abdul now once again downing tools, I'm slightly backed into a corner and feel I need to set the record straight to our loyal supporters by being very honest, while still not airing too much of our dirty washing in public.

'I'm making it crystal clear that we have negotiated in good faith with a club, but we will not relent on the present asking price, as we have already lowered our asking price by £350k.

'When the time is right, I might go into more detail about the real truths behind these press leaks, the downing of tools, the player's conduct, the nonsense and the behaviour of some characters within this transfer saga.

'But for now, 'least said, best mended' is my stance. That said, until the window has closed, the ball is now firmly in the buying club's, player's, agent's and advisors' court because if our valuation is met, then Abdul can go.

'As far as I'm concerned, the transfer fee is agreed. It's now simply about reaching agreement on some add-ons based on the buying club's league and UEFA success while Abdul is at their club.

'There are some appearance add-ons, a simple international clause should Abdul become an international (which would increase his worth tenfold) and a fair sell-on. That's pretty much the saga/story in a nutshell.

'At the moment, Abdul is refusing to train with us or play, though he is still very much our player and has two years left on his contract. My gut feeling is the buying club might decide not to come back to the table, but of course I might be wrong?

'If I was a betting man, and I'm not, I would expect, when the transfer window closes next Tuesday, that an unhappy Abdul will still be with us, but what do I know?

'It's now a very simple equation. If the buying club wants to agree the add-ons and finalise a transfer agreement, then let's get on with it, as I'm ready and waiting. If not, trust me, I'll be even happier as the window will be closed, and we'll still have Abdul.

'For clarity, Abdul, in his position, is the best in this division and the division above by a country mile, hence why he is valued highly. If he stays, he will of course help us enormously with our promotion push and EFL ambition.'

Abdulmalik could become the most expensive non-league player - eclipsing the £1m Leicester City paid Fleetwood Town for Jamie Vardy in 2012

Abdulmalik, meanwhile, released a statement via Instagram on Tuesday night expressing his desire to leave.

'I'm ready to prove to myself and those around me that I'm capable of reaching the top,' he said. 'Opportunities like this are rare, especially within the National League where some of the hardest working talent is overlooked.

'The game of football is forever changing and decisions are fast paced. There's no guarantee that the same chances come knocking twice. I owe it to myself and the kids growing up just like me to fight for this one I've been offered.'

Abdulmalik played for Millwall's academy and represented England at under-17 level before being released in 2024 and joining Boreham Wood as a free agent.

The tricky attacker had a stellar 2025-26 season, scoring 17 goals and providing 10 assists as Boreham Wood reached the National League play-off final.

Daily Mail Sport has contacted Boreham Wood for comment.

Sports.title: Joe Root's five biggest headaches ahead of second Pakistan Test - from the hangover effects of another England drinking scandal to the two struggling players fighting for their place
Sports.content:
England’s first-Test victory over Pakistan at Headingley last week was a welcome win after only two in the previous ten games.

Returning captain Joe Root's side now head to Lord's for the second Test, starting Thursday, with the chance to secure a first series win since the end of 2024.

But after another drink-related fiasco and with a constant search for the right batting lineup, they still have questions to answer going into Lord’s.

Here, Daily Mail Sport looks at five of the most urgent.

Just when Joe Root was starting to inject positivity - and victories - back into the England Test team, more headaches have arisen

Can they put the Carse incident behind them?

Recent precedent is not encouraging. After Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson visited the Rex Rooms in Chelsea following the first-Test win over New Zealand at Lord’s in June, England disintegrated, for the first time ever losing a three-match home series from 1-0 up.

Now, two days before returning to the Home of Cricket, Joe Root spent almost the entirety of his 24-minute press conference addressing Brydon Carse’s arrest in Derby on Saturday night. He spoke for the whole of the ECB when he said he was ‘hacked off’.

Two factors are in England’s favour as they seek to avoid another meltdown. First, the latest shenanigans will not deprive them of any first-choice players. Against New Zealand at The Oval, by contrast, Stokes and Atkinson were stood down and they fielded a side including five players with a combined total of two caps.

Second, Pakistan are weaker than New Zealand, having lost nine of their last ten Tests away from home. Sections of their media have taken offence at the suggestion that this is the weakest Pakistan team to visit here for 50 years, but no one has yet come up with an alternative answer.

Brydon Carse and Ben Stokes' night out in Derby has caused yet more problems for the ECB - now Root's team must respond better than England have to previous incidents

Has Emilio Gay nailed down his spot yet?

Gay made an impressive start as Zak Crawley’s replacement as opener, making 57 – the highest innings of the match – as England won a low-scoring first Test against New Zealand at Lord’s, then adding 53 in the first innings at The Oval.

Three failures were followed by a good-looking 33 off 31 balls against Pakistan at Headingley, but his dismissal there – squared up by Mohammad Ali before edging to second slip – hinted at a technical weakness outside off stump.

Six of his seven dismissals have ended with catches in the cordon. And while one of them was a leg-side strangle, a pattern is in danger of emerging.

Gay deserves the chance to build on those two fifties, but his Durham team-mate Ben McKinney lies in wait.

Emilio Gay (left) has been caught behind six times out of seven dismissals in his Test career

Gay's 6ft 7in Durham team-mate Ben McKinney looms large in the background if England need a replacement opener

Can Jordan Cox make life difficult for the selectors?

Initially chosen as a stand-in No3 while Jacob Bethell recovers from a knee injury, Cox began with 73 last week against Pakistan, batting with the swagger that earned him an Indian Premier League contract with Royal Challengers Bengaluru. He later chastised himself for spurning a maiden Test hundred – music to England’s ears.

It seems inconceivable that England won’t return to Bethell for their next Test series, starting in South Africa in December, but Cox could yet stake a claim at No6, currently occupied by Dan Lawrence, or even for the wicketkeeper’s gloves.

It was behind the stumps that he would have made his Test debut in New Zealand in late 2024, only to break a thumb shortly before the series began. The option remains on England’s table.

Jordan Cox made an impressive 73 in England's lone innings at Headingley but admitted he let a maiden Test hundred slip through his fingers

Does that mean Jamie Smith is under pressure?

Smith is among a group of players whose reputation is yet to recover from the disastrous Ashes last winter.

The 26-year-old has had his moments this summer, making a crucial 39 in the Lord’s shootout against New Zealand, and top-scoring with 60 in the second innings at Trent Bridge – though by then the game and the series were gone.

But he missed a chance to impose himself on the Pakistan bowling at Headingley, tamely miscuing a pull to mid-on, and has now made 364 runs at 20 since scoring 51 against India at Lord’s last summer.

Smith recently told Daily Mail Sport he has found it painful watching his batting average slump: it has just fallen below 40 for the first time since his second Test. His glovework remains fine, but he needs to prove he has ironed out his technical flaws, especially against the short ball and the nipbacker.

Jamie Smith needs to prove he has ironed out his technical flaws, especially against the short ball and the nipbacker

Are they any closer to solving their spin-bowling problem?

Not really. Shoaib Bashir is in the squad, but – with apologies to Lawrence – the lack of a genuine all-rounder means England can’t squeeze him in. And his chances of playing in the third Test at Edgbaston have been damaged by a season-ending groin injury to Sam Curran, whose presence and batting ability would have balanced the side.

England still seem lukewarm about the leg-spin of Rehan Ahmed, even though the 22-year-old who bats at the top of Leicestershire's lineup would strengthen the lower order, but they will also argue there is no great urgency to resolve the issue.

Spin bowling is unlikely to play a central role in South Africa at the turn of the year, nor in next summer’s Ashes. It will be an issue in the two-Test series in Bangladesh in between, but those games are low on England’s list of priorities.

Sports.title: Rory McIlroy wish granted as PGA Tour confirm major rule change that gets seal of approval
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy wish granted as PGA Tour confirm major rule change that gets seal of approval

Rory McIlroy is on board with big changes that will be introduced in 2028

View 3 Images Rory McIlroy has welcomed the upcoming changes to the PGA Tour (Image: Getty Images)

Rory McIlroy's demands have been heeded after the PGA Tour confirmed big changes to the play-off series. The Masters champion has been a critic of the end-of-season FedEx Cup series, which comprises the St Jude Championship, the BMW Championship and the deciding Tour Championship.

‌



Therefore, he has welcomed the changes, which will see the season conclude with a two-week matchplay event held across two different venues. The new format will be introduced from 2028.

‌



McIlroy has hailed the revamp as a positive step and believes it shows fans are being listened to. Speaking ahead of the Tour Championship at East Lake in Atlanta, the 37-year-old said: "I think the PGA Tour and the Future Competition Committee and Brian and everyone involved have really taken on board what the fans have been calling for and have wanted, which is matchplay.

‌



"Brian [Rolapp, PGA Tour CEO] took me through the plan last week for the first time. I didn't really know anything about it. It's certainly different. But it's cool. I think they've taken a big swing, and conceptually, I think I really like it."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

The new season-ending structure will begin with a 90-player, 72-hole stroke play event. The points leader at the conclusion of that tournament will be crowned the season-long champion, while the top 32 in the standings will secure their place in the Tour Championship.

‌



Rory McIlroy blows chance to pocket £1.64m as he reacts to BMW Championship collapse READ MORE :

Those 32 players will be divided into eight groups of four, with each player facing the other three in their group. The top two from each group progress to the second week.

The final 16 will then battle it out over four rounds of matchplay, with their records determining the overall standings and the two unbeaten players squaring off for the title.

View 3 Images McIlroy was back on form at the BMW Championship (Image: Getty Images)

‌



McIlroy believes the changes would be welcomed by his peers. He added: "I think they've been great for players. Obviously, we play for a ton of money, and it's sort of like the culmination of the entire season.

"The players have been rewarded. I think what the Tour are really trying to do is listen to the fans and what they want, and I think this idea of matchplay over two weeks is something that came mostly from what the people that watch golf wanted, so I think that's a really good thing."

View 3 Images Brian Rolapp took McIlroy through the changes (Image: Orlando Ramirez, Getty Images)

Article continues below

McIlroy should head to the Tour Championship in high spirits after a strong showing at the BMW Championship. The Northern Irishman started the final round five shots behind overnight leader Wyndham Clark, but was level after 15 holes.

While McIlroy bogeyed the 17th, Clark maintained his composure to birdie the 16th, 17th and 18th holes to wrest back control and finish the tournament on 17 under par. The two-time US Open champion ended the tournament three shots clear of Patrick Cantlay, who edged McIlroy for second.

Sports.title: Man City to make £100m Enzo Fernandez transfer bid despite missing Chelsea's deadline
Sports.content:
Man City to make £100m Enzo Fernandez transfer bid despite missing Chelsea's deadline

EXCLUSIVE: Enzo Fernandez remains a Chelsea player with five days until the summer transfer window closes, but Manchester City are preparing to finally make an opening bid worth £100million

View 2 Images Manchester City will test Chelsea's resolve for Enzo Fernandez (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Manchester City will make an opening bid of £100million for Chelsea star Enzo Fernandez. Etihad bosses remain keen on signing the Argentine midfielder, despite talks between the two clubs having stalled.

‌



Chelsea had set City a deadline of 5pm on August 13 to meet the asking price of £120m and get a deal done. But City know the World Cup winner is desperate to join them before the transfer window closes.

‌



And chairman Khaldoon-Al-Mubarak is poised to tempt Chelsea with an offer of £100m, in the hope of landing the 25-year-old. Fernandez has become an unpopular figure at Stamford Bridge, where he has been booed by his own fans.

‌



He was left out of Xabi Alonso's starting line-up for the win at Fulham this week, before playing the final 30 minutes at Craven Cottage. New City boss Enzo Maresca had a good relationship with Fernandez when he managed him at Chelsea.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



And he made it clear to City bosses when he accepted the job of replacing Pep Guardiola he would love to have him in his team again. City have seen Bernardo Silva and Rodri leave the Etihad this summer, while fellow midfielder Nico Gonzalez is poised to join Newcastle in a £50m deal.

The final straw for Gonzalez came last weekend, when Maresca selected defender Marc Guehi ahead of him in a holding midfield role for the 2-1 win over Bournemouth. Maresca would like to have Fernandez operating in tandem with record signing Elliot Anderson.

But it remains to be seen if City, who have kept in close contact with Fernandez's agent Javier Pastore, can strike a deal with Chelsea. Earlier this week, Alonso made it clear that he wants the midfielder's future to be decided quickly.

‌



How much is Enzo Fernandez worth? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso wants the Enzo Fernandez saga to be over (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

The Chelsea boss told BBC Radio 5 Live: "In football, I am not surprised by anything. We will see. My wish is that we know what will happen for the future but we will see this week."

‌



Maresca, meanwhile, has been tight-lipped on City's pursuit of Fernandez, who's seen as the ideal replacement for Rodri after he recently joined Barcelona.

"Enzo is a Chelsea player and I'm not going to talk about players that are not with us," the Italian said last week. "First of all, because I think it's a lack of respect, and second because I don't like when different managers talk about our players."

Sports.title: Arsenal set to announce striker transfer as target sends farewell message
Sports.content:
Arsenal set to announce striker transfer as target sends farewell message

Arsenal are on the verge of confirming the arrival of a young striker to their academy after his farewell message on social media

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal are edging closer to confirming a new signing (Image: (Photo by David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

Arsenal appear set to announce the signing of Igor Tyjon after he sent a farewell message to Blackburn Rovers. The 18-year-old striker has been targeted by the Gunners for much of this year and made the goodbye post on Tuesday before later deleting it.

‌



Several approaches from north London for Tyjon have been rebuffed but a breakthrough was achieved last week with Arsenal set to pay an initial £1million, with a further £2million potentially available in add-ons. Following that, Tyjon all but confirmed his departure in a now-deleted Instagram post.

‌



In an Instagram post, which was later deleted on Tuesday, he said: "I would like to thank (Blackburn) Rovers for the last 3 years. Thank you to all my teammates and staff throughout the years. I've made friendships for life and memories I won't forget. Lots of ups and downs and learning on the way.

‌



"The last couple of months have been tough due to certain people and reasons I can't say but I will never forget the good times at this club [blue heart emoji]."

The latter portion of his statement suggests criticism towards individuals at the club following several approaches from Arsenal being rejected. The youngster has made his senior bow for Blackburn but has chosen not to sign professional terms at Ewood Park

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

He has clocked up 69 first-team minutes across three appearances, with the bulk of his action coming in Premier League 2, where he has notched 10 goals and contributed two assists from 20 outings. Tyjon has yet to feature in any capacity this season as his transfer to Arsenal edges closer, and his social media farewell strongly suggests the deal is nearly done, having reportedly undergone a medical last week.

‌



Tyjon is anticipated to begin in Arsenal's under-21s but may appear for the senior squad in some capacity later this season. His forthcoming arrival provides additional evidence that Arsenal are once more concentrating on strengthening their youth academy after some prospects chose to depart elsewhere due to concerns that their route into the first-team was obstructed.

View 2 Images Igor Tyjon is set to join Arsenal from Blackburn Rovers

Manchester United succeeded in luring both Ayden Heaven and Chido Obi with both players receiving some first-team chances. The former has actually been a regular under Michael Carrick.

‌



In their efforts to attract the finest young players to London Colney, Arsenal have agreed to recruit James Scanlon and Habeeb Ogunneye from Old Trafford.

Arsenal are acquiring the pair on free transfers but substantial sell-on clauses are anticipated to be included with Ogunneye having already completed a medical.

Sports.title: Dylan Browne McMonagle 'out for a number of weeks' after Bellewstown fall injury
Sports.content:
Dylan Browne McMonagle 'out for a number of weeks' after Bellewstown fall injury

Irish champion jockey Dylan Browne McMonagle was taken to hospital after a fall at Bellewstown on Tuesday, with the first day of the track's 300th anniversary fixture ultimately abandoned following further fallers

View 2 Images Dylan Browne McMonagle" taken to hospital after fall (Image: Getty Images)

Dylan Browne McMonagle is facing a period on the sidelines following a fall at Bellewstown on Tuesday, with the opening day of the course's 300th anniversary meeting eventually called off after additional fallers.

‌



The Irish champion jockey was rushed to hospital in Drogheda after being thrown to the ground when his mount Mosel stumbled while launching a challenge a furlong out in the day's opener, the Irish Stallion Farms EBF Median Auction Maiden.

‌



While confirmed to be conscious upon departing the racecourse and subsequently described as recovering well with a full recovery anticipated, early examinations indicate the 23 year old "will be out for a number of weeks".

‌



Race meeting abandoned after Dylan Browne McMonagle taken to hospital following fall READ MORE :

Nicky Henderson announces decision on Constitution Hill Windsor appearance READ MORE :

Irish Horseracing Regulatory Board chief medical officer Jennifer Pugh said on X: "Following his fall in the first race at Bellewstown, Dylan Browne McMonagle was transferred to Our Lady of Lourdes Hospital, Drogheda.

"Dylan was conscious when leaving the racecourse and is recovering well in hospital this evening. He is very appreciative of the goodwill messages he has received since this afternoon.

"Dylan will be kept in Our Lady of Lourdes Hospital overnight for further assessment and observation and will be out for a number of weeks but will make a full recovery."

‌



View 2 Images Dr Jennifer Pugh issued an update

Browne McMonagle has experienced a remarkable year, with Classic triumphs on both sides of the Irish Sea enabling him to secure an Oaks double at Epsom and the Curragh aboard Thundering On and Johanna Walsh respectively.

As recently as Saturday he notched up a remarkable 723-1 five-timer at the Curragh, while he secured one victory with Limestone (Queen's Vase) and two runner-up finishes at Royal Ascot this year. He also captured the Chester Cup aboard A Piece Of Heaven.

‌



After his fall, the second race was delayed by 30 minutes so groundstaff could apply sand to problematic areas.

Sports.title: Man Utd's financial reality bites in chase for final piece of Michael Carrick's jigsaw
Sports.content:
It remains an oddity that Manchester United's record transfer fee came a decade ago.

Back in August 2016, the £89million United paid Juventus to bring Paul Pogba back was truly blockbuster, a fee from the future. It sent shockwaves across the football landscape.

The fact it hasn't been eclipsed in the 20 transfer windows since is telling. It reflects the fact that United haven't won the Premier League since Sir Alex Ferguson's departure in 2013 and the austerity with which owners the Glazers have run things.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe's arrival in February 2024 was followed by a drastic cost-cutting effort which still hasn't had the desired effect. This summer's transfer window has shown where United lag behind their Premier League rivals.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

To United, the signing of Carlos Baleba for an initial fee of £65m plus £5m in add-ons is a hugely significant one. But right across the Premier League such a fee is now almost run-of-the-mill, as United have noted internally after pulling out of the race for Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, who both moved to Tottenham for a combined £185m.

Premier League sides have cumulatively splashed out over £2bn this summer and there is plenty more to come, with some colossal transfers in the pipeline ahead of the September 1 deadline. Liverpool are in negotiations with Paris Saint-Germain for Bradley Barcola, Manchester City want Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea, Arsenal are eyeing Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez.

‌



United, meanwhile, are trying to bring in a left-back to compete with Luke Shaw. And they are trying to do so on the cheap.

View 3 Images Lewis Hall appears to be out of reach for Manchester United (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

They are unwilling to pay Barcelona's asking price for Alejandro Balde and have reportedly asked for a loan deal. Jorge Salinas, a 19-year-old from Racing Santander, is another option for a release clause of €16m (£13.6m).

Lewis Hall was always United's first-choice target. But Newcastle's reluctance to sell stopped United dead in their tracks, because unlike some of their rivals, they are unable to throw their financial weight around.

‌



United's most recent financial accounts showed they owe £405.75m in outstanding transfer fees, of which £171.14m is due after more than one year. The other heavy weight around their neck is the wage bill.

The £325,000-a-week contract handed to Marcus Rashford in July 2023 is a much-publicised problem. But, as Ratcliffe has publicly stated, the club are over-paying several other players.

View 3 Images Manchester United are still trying to sell Joshua Zirkzee (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manuel Ugarte cost £50m two years ago from PSG, has offered very little on the pitch and is paid £150,000 per week. Now injured, he is the sort of drain on finances the club will seek to avoid in future.

‌



The return to the Champions League was a huge boost for the club - worth an estimated £50m to £100m in additional revenue - but came with a sting in the tail, with a handful of players, including Mason Mount and Andre Onana, automatically getting a 25 per cent wage increase.

United have now changed the clause, meaning players have to feature in 60 per cent of the team's minutes to qualify. But for the time being they are still feeling the effects of past decisions.

Joshua Zirkzee wasn't among the players to get the wage uplift, but United have still so far been unable to find a buyer for the unwanted striker. He is emblematic of the club's current situation and why Michael Carrick will have to be understanding if his desire for a top-level left-back isn't fulfilled in the coming days.

Sports.title: Celtic's Champions League bottle job costs £40MILLION after horror LASK defeat
Sports.content:
Celtic's Champions League bottle job costs £40MILLION after horror LASK defeat

Celtic remarkably missed out on this season's Champions League after blowing a massive four-goal lead on aggregate away to Austrian side LASK in the final qualifying round

View 3 Images Celtic's defeat has hit them in the pocket (Image: Christian Bruna/Getty Images)

Celtic's catastrophic failure to qualify for the Champions League has seen the club miss out on a whopping £40million. Martin O'Neill's side will compete in the Europa League this season after falling at the final hurdle in qualifying on Tuesday.

‌



After romping to a 3-0 victory over Austrian opponents LASK at Parkhead last week, Celtic were the favourites to advance when they made the trip to Linz for the return leg. The Scottish champions even got off to a dream start, with Callum McGregor extending their lead on aggregate to four goals when he scored in the 22nd minute.

‌



But then it fell all apart. LASK's two goals before half-time followed by another just shy of the hour mark meant that it was game on.

‌



And in the 90th minute, substitute Florian Flecker scored to send the match to extra-time. Although Celtic looked to have steadied the ship and with penalties looming, Luke McCowan was robbed of possession on the egde of their box, allowing LASK striker Samuel Adeniran to tuck home what proved to be the decisive goal in the rollercoaster tie.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Adeniran missed a penalty six minutes later to give Celtic an inkling of hope. But the visitors couldn't recover and bowed out in embarrassing fashion.

Aside from the ignominy of having to compete in Europe's second-rate competition when they were minutes away from sitting at the top table, the loss also hits them financially. Celtic have gone from looking at a £40m jackpot to less than a quarter of that.

The Bhoys' failure will likely affect their transfer business, too, with former Celtic goalkeeper Kasper Schmeichel pointing out on commentary that certain targets may've only considered a move to Glasgow had they been able to offer Champions League football. Celtic captain McGregor admitted that his team 'looked scared' during the collapse, apologising to fans.

‌



Will Tuesday go down as Celtic's worst night in European football? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images LASK scored five unanswered goals (Image: Christian Bruna/Getty Images)

"We got what we deserved," the 33-year-old told Prime Video Sport. "We were passive all night. We looked scared to go and win the game.

‌



"I didn't think we were that good in the first leg either. We scored at good times and got away with it. We have to suck it up. We apologise to our supporters and the club because there's no way we should lose that game.

"It's as much on the players as everyone else. You can't look for excuses elsewhere. You'll now see what people are made of."

View 3 Images Martin O'Neill shouldered the blame (Image: Christian Bruna/Getty Images)

‌



Meanwhile, O'Neil took responsibility for the crushing defeat. "We should have the game out of sight," the Celtic boss said. "We missed some glorious chances and we gave them a lifeline just before half-time and then just after half-time again.

"So it gave them momentum and they carried that momentum for some time. I thought we were going to see it through. We didn't do it at the end and that's my responsibility. It's the most disappointing night I've had in a long, long time."

Sports.title: Carlos Baleba earns Roy Keane comparison but grew up idolising another ex-Man Utd star
Sports.content:
Carlos Baleba earns Roy Keane comparison but grew up idolising another ex-Man Utd star

Manchester United have invested in one of the best young midfielders in Europe in Carlos Baleba - now he must prove he can deliver on one of the most demanding stages of all

View 3 Images Carlos Baleba is now officially a Manchester United player (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Carlos Baleba has admitted he hates being compered to other footballers of his ilk.

‌



So he won't be impressed to learn that senior figures inside Manchester United believe the club has just signed someone who can have the same impact at Old Trafford as Roy Keane once did.

‌



That's quite a compliment - whether Baleba likes it or not. Because Keane remains one of United's all-time greats. One of the best midfielders of his generation. A rampaging enforcer who controlled games on his own. And won quite a few of them, too.

‌



Those in charge of recruitment at Old Trafford, including Christopher Vivell and head of senior scouting Kyle Macauley, have spent months watching Baleba's development on the south coast, while pouring over video footage of his performances.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

And these two have seen qualities in the Cameroon international which remind them of Keane in his pomp. Why United have been persuaded to spend £70m on someone who Michael Carrick can go on to build his team around.

‌



A bundle of pace, power and stamina, complimented with excellent passing and dribbling skills and that rare ability to anticipate what is going to happen in a game's engine room.

Baleba grew up idolising Paul Pogba and has a long-held ambition to win the Ballon d'Or. He is not lacking in ambition.

View 3 Images Baleba has been compared to Man Utd legend Roy Keane (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



View 3 Images Carlos Baleba has completed a dream move to Manchester United (Image: Crystal Pix/MB Media/Getty Images)

"Everyone talking about you, singing your name? That just doesn't do it for me. It's not something that gets me running. I just prefer getting my head down and working on the pitch."

If Baleba proves a success at United, he won't have a choice in the matter when it comes to being hero worshipped and revered.

‌



He will have to accept his life has changed. "At the end of my career, I want to have an individual title, to play and mark a little bit of history like the great midfielders have done before," he went on. "And then win trophies, lots of trophies, with my club and my country."

United will now be keeping everything crossed he goes on to achieve his ambitions.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
