Sports.title: Verstappen to race 100 drivers at once in karts at Silverstone | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen will take on 100 drivers in a special go-kart race at Silverstone, Red Bull has announced.

The four-times world champion will start at the back of the grid with 100 rivals ahead of him.

“In go-karts you learn all the basics: starts, defending, overtaking,” said Verstappen. “Of course, I spent a long period of my life go-karting, so it’s always nice to return.

“It’s about understanding the grip of the go-kart. I’ve done so many years in go-karting that you quite naturally get back into things. I will be looking forward to just seeing the carnage unfold in front of me.”

Red Bull say Verstappen’s rivals will be drawn “from every corner of sport and culture: from Red Bull athletes and celebrities to content creators, personalities and everyday fans invited from around the world.”

The event will take place on September 16th, three days after the Spanish Grand Prix, at a specially designed track at the home of the British Grand Prix.

“Creating a track for 100 drivers at the same time has never been done, never been seen,” said circuit designer and race director David Terrien. “So it’s very exciting.

“When you have Max Verstappen chasing everyone, I think that’s going to be the experience of a lifetime for all the drivers. You’re going to have Max showcasing all these skills of looking through the traffic, trying to prepare and plan where he can overtake people, and going through the traffic at the fastest speed he can because he doesn’t want to let the drivers at the front pull away.”

The event will be broadcast in some territories on Disney Plus and the ESPN app.

Sports.title: McLaren’s car is still “horrible to drive” despite consecutive wins, says Norris | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris may have won the last two grands prix in a row but he says McLaren’s car is still a handful to drive.

The world champion believes this is partly a consequence of the 2026 regulations.

“It’s tough to say, but I do think it’s a trickier car to drive this year in some ways,” said Norris. “I think you can see that because the gaps between team mates are often bigger this year, I would say, than it was last year.”

However Norris says he is doing better at communicating his needs to his team.

“I do believe I’m able to understand situations better, to understand the car in a better way,” he explained. “It’s still just horrible to drive, but I’m doing a better job at just understanding this, relaying this to my team, figuring stuff out.

“So, it’s not just that I’m driving better on track. I’m certainly eliminating my weaknesses on track, and I don’t have so many, but it’s also how I work off the track.”

He said the changes he made on his car between the sprint race and qualifying session in the Netherlands “is a perfect example of [how] the work we put in overnight transformed our race and gave me the opportunity to win.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Norris’s team mate Oscar Piastri also appeared to struggle with his car at times during Sunday’s race, where he finished sixth. At one stage he asked his race engineer Tom Stallard: “Please give me some help on how to drive this thing.”

Despite his wins in the last two rounds, Norris says McLaren must make significant improvements in their car’s low-speed cornering.

“We have a strong car in certain areas,” he said. “It’s not like last year where we were pretty good everywhere.

“We’re very, very strong in high speed, and that’s the place we’ve improved the car the most, is high-speed performance. No one matches us in high-speed, and that’s a good thing. My pace advantage to Mercedes in turn seven and eight was crazy, but the advantage that they have to us in slow speed is also crazy.

“Therefore, I don’t have the confidence to say, ‘Yeah, I can easily fight for a championship for the rest of the season.’ I know I’ve just won two races in a row and had two poles in a row, but at the minute I don’t have the car I need to fight for a championship.

“I know that’s quite a big comment, but I think last year I understood what is needed from a car and what was needed for myself. And I know the level that I am now and what I know I can perform at, and I know just what I need from the car and I know what tracks we have coming up where we’re going to certainly struggle more, and I don’t want to struggle more.

“So I’m just doing my part to make sure, as a team, we don’t relax, we don’t get complacent in any way, and we work more than we’ve ever done before, even more than the last two years when we’ve won championships. I need the guys and girls to work and focus better than ever before to improve on these areas. If we can improve on these slow speeds, I’m confident that I can win every race this season. If we don’t, then it’s much more difficult to believe so.”

Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc was in no doubt Ferrari wanted him to pit when he was holding his team mate up during the Dutch Grand Prix.

The team originally hoped to bring Leclerc in on lap 41 but did not want him to follow George Russell’s Mercedes into the pit lane. Ferrari told their driver to pit “opposite” Russell, so when the Mercedes came in Leclerc followed his team’s order and did not pit as well.

Meanwhile Hamilton was gaining on Leclerc and becoming concerned his team mate would hold him up. Early on lap 42 Ferrari told Leclerc to come in.

However Leclerc disputed the order, telling Ferrari it would put him at a disadvantage to Russell, who had pitted earlier. After a period of silence, which was long enough for Leclerc to prompt his race engineer Bryan Bozzi for a reply, Ferrari gave the driver a second instruction to pit. But Leclerc did not come in.

Hamilton was becoming increasingly infuriated, telling the team “we’re just losing time.” After Leclerc finally pitted on the next lap, following another instruction from Ferrari, Hamilton sarcastically commented: “Big waste of time guys, good job.”

The Ferrari drivers finished the race behind Russell, with Hamilton fourth ahead of Leclerc.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Sees Frank Sanchez Testing Itauma
Sports.content:
That performance showed why Sanchez is dangerous for Itauma. He is not another aging heavyweight brought in to stand directly in front of the 21-year-old and disappear after absorbing the first clean combination. His movement, counterpunching and durability may keep him in the fight long enough to test Itauma’s chin more than once.

“He’s very clever, and he’s old,” Tony Bellew said.

Officially, Sanchez is 34, the same age as Hrgovic, making the repeated references to him being old strange unless Hearn and Bellew doubt his listed age.

Hearn considers Hrgovic’s upright style a better tactical fit for Itauma. The Croatian is easier to locate and more likely to exchange at close range. Sanchez creates different questions by changing distance, moving laterally and waiting for an opponent to overcommit.

Queensberry has spent years presenting Itauma as 24-karat gold while matching him with aging heavyweights whose styles advertise his best qualities. They have generally lacked the foot speed and defensive movement to escape his combinations. Hrgovic is considerably better than those opponents, but his upright stance and willingness to exchange still give Itauma a stationary target.

A Sanchez upset would begin with surviving the first four rounds, moving laterally and forcing Itauma to reset before launching his left hand. Rather than trying to overpower him, the Cuban can draw out the initial attack, step away and counter while Itauma is recovering his position. Every missed rush would make the younger fighter expend energy without getting the spectacular finish his promoters and the crowd anticipate.

Itauma has never been forced to think under pressure against a puncher with Sanchez’s power, defend against counters or manage his pace deep into a championship fight. If he becomes impatient, Sanchez has the timing and single-shot power to make him pay. Itauma may have the answers, but nothing he has done in the ring has shown them yet.

Under the IBF arrangement, Queensberry has little room to continue the same matchmaking formula. The winner must face Sanchez within six months without an intervening bout unless the organization grants an exception. If Itauma wins Saturday, his team must either accept the most complicated stylistic opponent of his career, seek another delay or surrender the belt.

The repeated effort to label Sanchez “old” is worth challenging. He and Hrgovic are both officially 34, yet Hrgovic is promoted as Itauma’s first legitimate test while Sanchez is discussed as a fading veteran. The difference is not age. Sanchez simply presents a more difficult style for the type of opponents Queensberry has matched Itauma against.

Sports.title: Oba Carr Had the Tools to Beat Spence
Sports.content:
Speed was not Carr’s only weapon in this hypothetical matchup. In the second round of his December 1994 title fight with Trinidad, he timed a quick right hand that dropped the dangerous champion. Trinidad recovered and stopped Carr in the eighth, but the knockdown showed Carr’s ability to identify an opening and punish an elite puncher ahead of the return fire.

That straight right would be especially important against the southpaw Spence. Carr had the hand speed to fire between Spence’s deliberate advances, then follow with combinations that prevented Spence from establishing his body attack. Crawford used different footwork and possessed a far broader offensive arsenal, but Carr owned enough of the necessary tools to exploit the same declining reactions.

Further evidence came during Carr’s 12 rounds with Quartey, whose stiff jab was faster and more punishing than Spence’s. Two judges had Quartey well ahead, so the majority decision was not as close as the official result suggests. Carr still handled that jab for the full distance and continued returning fire against a powerful natural welterweight.

The 2019 car crash, retinal injury and years of forcing his body down to 147 gradually removed Spence’s best qualities. He defeated Yordenis Ugas, but no longer possessed the reactions or physical condition of his earlier years. By the Crawford fight, he looked depleted and was taken apart in nine rounds.

Prime Spence would make it a much closer contest. His size, body punching and physical pressure would test Carr, who was dropped twice by former lightweight champion Livingstone Bramble before escaping with a disputed split decision in 1991. The damaged Spence seen later in his career would struggle to impose those advantages early enough to stop Carr’s speed from taking control.

The depth of the 1990s placed Trinidad, Quartey, De La Hoya and Pernell Whitaker at the top of the division. Missing out on a belt against those champions did not place Carr below championship level. In Spence’s fragmented era, he would have found several opportunities to collect one.

An empty championship column hides Carr’s quality. He had the speed, power and experience to beat the diminished Spence, even if Crawford remained a level beyond him.

Sports.title: Boxing’s Biggest Stars Were Never Universally Loved
Sports.content:
Joe Louis reached an even broader audience. His 25 consecutive heavyweight title defenses remain a division record, but his importance extended beyond the ring. Louis conducted exhibitions during World War II and served in the Army, becoming a national figure at a time when Black athletes faced severe racial barriers.

Sugar Ray Robinson followed as one of boxing’s most admired performers. His speed, combination punching and long career helped establish the standard by which later pound-for-pound greats were judged. Henry Armstrong defeated 16 world champions and once held the featherweight, lightweight and welterweight titles at the same time. His nonstop attacking style made him a fan favorite.

Rocky Marciano finished his career at 49-0 with 43 stoppages. His knockout victory over an aging Joe Louis was one of the best-known wins on his record.. Manny Pacquiao later became an international attraction, winning titles across eight divisions and carrying the expectations of the Philippines whenever he fought.

Not every major attraction was universally liked. Jack Johnson became heavyweight champion during an era of open racial hostility. Much of the opposition to him came from white Americans who resented seeing a Black champion defeat white challengers. The search for a “Great White Hope” revealed more about the country than it did about Johnson’s popularity. He was a hero to many Black fans while being vilified elsewhere.

Pernell Whitaker never generated the same commercial following as several less-accomplished fighters. His defensive style required viewers to appreciate positioning, timing, and subtle movement rather than constant exchanges. When I once asked him to name his toughest opponent, he replied, “All of them!”

Larry Holmes also struggled to receive the appreciation his ability deserved. He followed Muhammad Ali, defeated an aging version of him, and later angered Marciano supporters by saying, “Rocky couldn’t carry my jockstrap” after losing to Michael Spinks. That bitterness overshadowed a heavyweight reign that included 20 successful title defenses.

Ali demonstrated how hostility itself could be turned into business. His boasting encouraged some spectators to adore him and others to pay in hopes of watching him lose. I met him at his Cherry Hill, New Jersey, home in 1973 and again at his Deer Lake, Pennsylvania, training camp in 1977. Away from the cameras, he was far different from the confrontational character used to sell fights.

Ricky Hatton, Mike Tyson, Marvin Hagler, Sugar Ray Leonard, Willie Pep and Alexis Arguello also built devoted followings through different combinations of personality, nationality and fighting style. I met all except Hatton and found each of them to be a gentleman.

The history shows why ranking boxers only as “popular” or “unpopular” is too simple. Some were loved, some were resented, and a select few became enormous attractions by giving audiences reasons to feel both.

Sports.title: Ade Oladipo Misreads George Foreman’s Place in History
Sports.content:
“That’s horrendous,” Ade said. “What? Because he can sell grills, all of a sudden he can fight?”

He then assigned almost all the Rumble in the Jungle’s importance to Muhammad Ali, arguing that Ali could have faced someone else and produced the same event.

“I’d never heard anything about Foreman,” Oladipo said. “That is all Muhammad Ali.”

During his interview with Helwani, Oladipo first claimed the clip had been taken out of context. He described the original exchange as a light argument over the most famous boxer ever, with Gough bringing up the Foreman grill while Oladipo defended Ali. That account softened the substance of his own remarks.

“It wasn’t necessarily anti-George Foreman. I think it was so pro-Ali that I was like, ‘No, no, my guy,’” Oladipo told Ariel Helwani. “I was just saying my guy is numero uno, and by defending my guy kind of shot down others… I certainly didn’t mean to be disrespectful to the late, great George Foreman… I was just trying to back my guy, and I think maybe I batted a bit too hard.”

That is closer to an admission than a defense. Oladipo knew while recording the segment that his remarks might generate criticism. He now accepts that Foreman was one of the greatest heavyweights ever and that he unfairly diminished him while arguing for Ali.

Before making that concession, Oladipo spent several minutes attacking his critics. He called them jealous, dismissed some as “minions” and suggested members of the boxing media were using the clip to pursue his broadcasting position. He also complained that boxing expects commentators to possess the equivalent of a university doctorate in the sport’s history.

Born in 1981, Oladipo was not around for Foreman’s rise. He never experienced the sequence of an Olympic gold medalist developing into boxing’s most destructive heavyweight, wiping out established champions and arriving in Zaire with the aura of an unbeatable force.

Foreman’s 1973 destruction of Joe Frazier remains among boxing’s most memorable title changes. Howard Cosell’s repeated cry of “Down goes Frazier” entered American sports culture as Foreman dropped the champion six times in two rounds.

Frazier had defeated Ali two years earlier. Ken Norton had broken Ali’s jaw and beaten him in 1973. Foreman needed only two rounds to destroy Norton, then later stopped Frazier for a second time.

He was the Mike Tyson of an earlier generation. Spectators watched because Foreman’s knockouts carried a frightening inevitability. Ali supplied unmatched personality and global celebrity in Zaire, while the champion across from him represented terrifying physical danger.

Claiming that Ali could have fought anyone in Kinshasa and created the same spectacle also reduces Ali’s accomplishment. The Rumble in the Jungle achieved immortality because Ali conquered the undefeated destroyer whom many believed might seriously hurt him. Replace Foreman with a routine contender and the event becomes another Ali title fight rather than a defining moment in sports history. Foreman’s reputation was not incidental to the legend. It was the obstacle that made Ali’s victory extraordinary.

The grill argument reverses the cause and effect. Foreman’s fame did not originate with kitchen appliances. Their enormous commercial success relied on a recognizable former heavyweight champion with an extraordinary personal story. Modern casual fans may associate the older, smiling Foreman with television commercials, but audiences in the 1970s knew him as an intimidating knockout artist.

His second career further weakens Oladipo’s dismissal. Foreman returned after a decade away, rebuilt himself in public and knocked out Michael Moorer in 1994 to regain the heavyweight championship at age 45. That accomplishment introduced him to another generation and completed a remarkable reinvention. His popularity rested on the combination of his terrifying first reign, historic comeback, and transformed personality. The grill capitalized on that story; it did not create it.

A broadcaster does not need personal memories of every boxing era. Curiosity is supposed to fill that absence. Foreman’s rise is not obscure material from 1922, as Oladipo’s comparison suggested. The heavyweight era containing Ali, Foreman, Frazier and Norton is foundational knowledge for anyone paid to discuss boxing professionally.

Calling critics jealous avoids that distinction. They were not demanding expertise in forgotten bare-knuckle champions. The criticism followed because a prominent broadcaster showed limited preparation on one of the sport’s central figures, then treated the reaction as an attempt to take his job.

The mistake was not choosing Ali as the more famous man. It was mistaking the older George Foreman Oladipo knew for the young fighter the world feared. Blaming the reaction on missing context and professional jealousy does not correct that historical blind spot.

Sports.title: Richardson Hitchins Blames “Higher Ups” for Avoiding Norman
Sports.content:
“You not it the higher ups don’t care to see me whoop you #Facts,” Hitchins posted on X. “It would be bullying lil ni**a only thing that’s gone beat you up is ya ballz I’ll spank you from 1 to 12 bum.”

The contradiction could not be more obvious. If Norman truly offers zero resistance, Hitchins should jump at the chance to fight him. Dominating a recognizable name would solidify his status at welterweight, generate valuable highlight reels, plus give instant credibility to his claim that he belongs among the elite.

Instead, Hitchins dismisses Norman as unworthy while refusing to back up the insult. That is an ancient boxing trick, giving a fighter an easy exit from a dangerous matchup without having to confess to the hesitation underneath.

Nothing on his record justifies that kind of arrogance. His crowning moments came against Liam Paro and an undersized George Kambosos Jr. Hitchins edged Paro by a narrow split decision in late 2024 before stopping Kambosos in the eighth round half a year later. Kambosos was a lightweight moving up to junior welterweight who had already dropped three of his last five ring appearances. Bragging about bullying legitimate welterweights sounds absurd when your biggest triumph came against a faded, outsized opponent.

Norman brings power, real physical size, plus elite speed. He is entering his prime at his natural weight class, representing a completely different tier of danger. Gustavo Lemos brought relentless pressure. Jose Zepeda brought veteran craft. Neither man carried the firepower to punish mistakes the way Norman can.

Shutting out Ricardo Salas in July proved nothing about competing with the elite. Salas provided a gentle introduction to 147 pounds. That easy win offered zero evidence that Hitchins can handle a destructive puncher who will force real exchanges.

The tough talk collapses under any honest examination of his ring identity. Hitchins postures like a vicious finisher online, yet inside the ropes he operates strictly as a cautious technician who controls distance, avoids messy trades, and collects decision wins. He possesses real boxing skill, but his safety-first style looks nothing like the beatdown he advertised.

Belittling Norman looks especially weak after Hitchins pulled out of the Oscar Duarte bout on the day of the event in February. Instead of rebooking a dangerous assignment, he sat idle for months before returning against a harmless opponent in Salas. Choosing the soft path in matchmaking makes his loud talk impossible to take seriously.

Elite fighters who actually want an opponent take control of the situation. They order their teams to send contracts, call out rivals directly on camera, and force the other side to say no publicly.

Hitchins has done none of that. He mentions no specific promoters, points to zero failed talks, and produces not a single rejected contract. His vague talk about unnamed suits is simply a convenient hiding spot, letting him posture online without ever having to back up his words in the ring.

Until Hitchins tells his team to put real paper in front of Norman, dismissing the matchup as bullying remains pure theater. It is the cheap talk of a fighter whose matchmaking stays safe while his mouth makes promises his ring choices refuse to keep.

Sports.title: Mannix: Teofimo Lopez Knows Ryan Garcia Is Next
Sports.content:
Losing to Benn would remove that justification. Garcia would no longer bring the WBC belt, leaving Lopez to choose a commercially valuable voluntary defense over a mandated consolidation. Allowing it would amount to the WBA discarding its order because Lopez found a more profitable opponent.

Catterall is not merely a contender waiting after winning an eliminator. He captured the WBA Regular welterweight title by defeating Shakhram Giyasov and was promised a fight against the primary champion within 180 days. Lopez inherited that obligation when he took the WBA title from Rolando Romero.

The sanctioning body must now decide how much its own order is worth. A Garcia unification would produce greater attention and a larger sanctioning fee, but another postponement would further reduce the value of holding its Regular title. Fighters are asked to compete for that belt, pay sanctioning fees and trust that victory will lead to the primary champion.

Lopez’s apparent freedom to plan around Catterall shows that commercial appeal may defeat enforcement. If the WBA permits Garcia to go first, especially after a loss to Benn, it will make itself look second-rate by showing that its orders apply only when champions have nothing richer available.

Matchroom Presses WBA To Force Teofimo Lopez vs. Jack Catterall

Jack Catterall confirmed Tuesday that Eddie Hearn and Matchroom sent a letter to the WBA in an attempt to get his title fight with Teofimo Lopez enforced.

“Letter was sent to them yesterday by Eddie and Matchroom,” Catterall posted on X in response to a supporter asking his team to act.

Catterall also revealed that WBA president Gilberto Mendoza personally promised him that the 180-day commitment would remain in place regardless of who held the Super title.

“When I met Gilberto Mendoza in Egypt, I shook his hand and he gave me his word if I beat Giyasov, someone who was avoided and waited for his shot for two years, I will get my shot within 180 days regardless who has the belt. So I believe the WBA will do the correct thing,” Catterall posted.

That account removes much of the uncertainty about what the WBA intended. Its published resolution named Rolando Romero, but its president allegedly told Catterall that the commitment followed the title. Lopez still has a technical argument based on the written wording, yet the WBA would have to break Mendoza’s personal promise to let him move on.

The dispute began after Lopez openly denied that Catterall was his mandatory during Monday’s Inside the Ring show. Lopez plans to pursue the three additional titles he needs to become the undisputed welterweight champion, beginning with the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn on September 12.

That pursuit leaves no place for Catterall, but the secondary WBA champion has rejected the easiest negotiated solution.

“There’s not $1 that can persuade me to step aside to allow a unification bout to happen. I’m here to fight,” Catterall said.

His refusal means Matchroom cannot be paid to wait while Lopez pursues the Garcia vs. Benn winner. The WBA must enforce the consolidation fight, permit a unification first, or allow its two welterweight champions to remain separated.

The 180-day period expires on November 19, based on Catterall’s May 23 victory over Shakhram Giyasov. That leaves less than three months to settle the dispute. The cut Lopez suffered over his right eyebrow against Rolando Romero places more strain on the schedule, although there has been no indication that it will keep him out for an extended period.

Teofimo may believe the WBA will permit a unification to take priority over its internal consolidation fight. Sanctioning bodies regularly move mandatory obligations aside when champions pursue another belt, giving his team a stronger argument than the wording omission alone.

Catterall brings tactical risk with little financial reward. His awkward southpaw style and sharp counterpunching deny opponents clean offensive opportunities. Ryan Garcia, Conor Benn and Devin Haney generate massive paydays. Catterall brings no comparable commercial appeal, only a genuine threat to expose Lopez inside the ring.

WBA Loophole Gives Teofimo Lopez Easy Out On Jack Catterall

A review of the WBA’s published rulings supports part of Teofimo Lopez’s argument. No public order currently names Jack Catterall as the mandatory challenger for Lopez’s newly acquired Super welterweight title.

The May 21 ruling required Rolando Romero to face the Catterall-Shakhram Giyasov winner within 180 days. Its language named Romero specifically. It did not say the obligation would transfer to Romero’s successor if the title changed hands.

That omission gives Lopez a technical basis for denying that Catterall has been formally assigned to him. The WBA would need to issue another ruling, clarify that the original order followed the championship, or designate Catterall as Lopez’s challenger.

Teofimo still goes too far by claiming Catterall was lied to. The WBA sanctioned the Giyasov bout and publicly stated that its winner would receive Romero within 180 days. Catterall’s expectation came directly from the organization, not from an invented promise by his team.

The real issue is poor wording from the WBA. It created two champions and ordered them to meet, yet attached the obligation to Romero by name rather than clearly attaching it to the Super title. Lopez is now using that opening to pursue the Garcia-Benn winner while Catterall waits for the WBA to explain what its own ruling means.

Teofimo Lopez Denies Jack Catterall Mandatory Status

Teofimo Lopez claims Jack Catterall is not his WBA mandatory and says the British contender was lied to about his right to challenge for the welterweight title.

During today’s Inside the Ring show, Catterall confronted the new WBA champion after Lopez discussed facing the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn winner and eventually meeting Devin Haney for the undisputed championship.

“He’s not. He’s not my mandatory,” Lopez said when Catterall was identified as next in line. “By the sanctioning rules, he’s not my mandatory, and I think they lied. I think they lied to him.”

“It’s in the contract,” Catterall answered.

Teofimo’s denial conflicts with the WBA’s own published ruling. When the organization elevated Rolando Romero to Super champion in May, it sanctioned Catterall’s bout with Shakhram Giyasov for the vacant secondary title and stated that Romero had to face the winner within 180 days.

Catterall defeated Giyasov and now holds that belt. Lopez may argue that the ruling named Romero rather than whoever defeated him, or that no separate order has been issued since Saturday. Neither explanation supports his claim that Catterall was lied to. The WBA publicly connected the two titles and imposed a deadline for bringing them together.

The exchange became entertaining because Lopez tried to rewrite the situation while Catterall was on the screen looking directly at him. Rather than explain the supposed sanctioning rule, Teofimo declared that the obligation did not exist and blamed unnamed people for misleading Catterall.

After making that denial, the new champion returned to the familiar claim that he will face anyone.

“I’m always willing to fight anybody and everybody,” Lopez said.

“I’m glad you won on the weekend because I know you don’t duck nobody,” Catterall replied. “It would have been more difficult to get Rolly into the ring. I’m happy for you, but we’ve got to get it on.”

Catterall played the interaction perfectly. He congratulated Lopez, reminded him that Romero would have been harder to bring into the ring and declined to turn the conversation into a shouting match. That left Teofimo arguing against a contract he had not seen while Catterall calmly insisted the terms were already written down.

There was also some clever pressure inside Catterall’s praise. Telling Lopez, “I know you don’t duck nobody,” gave the champion little room to reject the fight without contradicting the reputation Catterall had just assigned to him.

The WBA now needs to explain the status of its own ruling. It can grant Lopez permission to pursue a unification, arrange a step-aside payment or order the title consolidation. What it cannot credibly do is remain silent while its new champion claims the other titleholder was fooled.

Lopez is clearly trying to look past the mandatory to chase the massive paydays against the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn winner or a unification with Devin Haney. Catterall holds the regular belt after beating Shakhram Giyasov, which, in standard WBA procedure, makes him the direct mandatory to unify the titles.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Expects Fury-Joshua Fight in America
Sports.content:
“I genuinely think it will happen. His Excellency, Turki Alalshikh, he will announce that fairly soon. I know there’s been some issues with contracts with Matchroom and AJ; I believe they will iron all those out. In the meantime, Tyson has flown off to the States. He’s in Miami, and he’s preparing for the fight,” said Warren to Sky Sports News.

Fury recently placed the fight in “serious doubt” and accused Joshua of wanting more money after plans moved away from a British stadium. Eddie Hearn has argued that Joshua signed for a UK event and that staging it in America would reduce his earnings after taxes while adding obligations to the contract.

That account undercuts the suggestion that Joshua alone wants to keep the event in Britain. Warren said Fury also prefers Wembley, but the broadcaster and financial backers have chosen America.

“They could refuse to fight. We don’t get the fight we want to see,” Warren said. “I think because of the amount of money involved, I hope I’m wrong, but I think it will go on in America.”

Much depends on how determined Joshua and Hearn are to increase his purse or force a return to the original terms. Hearn has openly rejected the venue change without amendments to Joshua’s contract, added payment and other demands from Alalshikh’s side.

Those public complaints may also have irritated Alalshikh, Sela and TKO Boxing. Joshua has lost the ability to negotiate the way he did during his prime. He has no world title, lost twice to Oleksandr Usyk and was knocked out by Daniel Dubois.

His last fight further weakened his position. Kristian Prenga was brought in for a showcase tune-up, but the second-tier heavyweight dropped Joshua twice in the opening round. Joshua was saved by the bell before returning to stop Prenga in the second.

Hearn can demand more money for moving the event, but the organizers have far less reason to agree to it than they would have had six years ago. The Prenga scare gave them another reason not to treat Joshua like one of the best heavyweights in the division.

This matchup is roughly six years past the point when it carried its greatest sporting value. Fury and Joshua once held every major heavyweight title between them, but repeated negotiations never brought them into the same ring. Usyk eventually beat both men and took away the argument over which one was the best heavyweight of their generation.

Fury has declined as well. He lost twice to Usyk before retiring and returning when another enormous payday became available. Training in Miami does not change what has happened to him or Joshua.

No longer a contest to determine Britain’s best heavyweight or the leading fighter in the division, it is now a nostalgia event for supporters who followed both men during their primes. The fight still makes money because of who Fury and Joshua used to be, not because of what either man has left.

Joshua may have the contractual right to reject America, but using it risks losing a payday that may never return. Hearn can continue pressing for revised terms, although his case weakens if the financial backers decide the price is too high for a fight between two heavyweights who are shot to pieces.

Eddie Hearn: Nobody Can Stop Fury-Joshua Fight

Eddie Hearn insists Anthony Joshua’s fight with Tyson Fury remains legally binding and can only collapse if Sela breaches the signed agreement.

Fury claimed Friday that the fight no longer looked likely, blaming Joshua and Hearn for seeking more money. Hearn has now rejected that account, maintaining that both fighters are signed and Joshua’s side is only waiting for Sela to provide a date.

“The update is quite simple. We’ve signed the contract. We’re waiting for a date. You saw Tyson Fury on the elliptical trainer, shouting and screaming. There’s nothing to shout about. The fight’s done, the fight’s signed,” Hearn told DAZN Boxing. “No one can pull out of the fight. You can’t just pull out of a contract. So, we’re waiting on the date.”

The dispute remains tied to the location. Joshua’s agreement calls for the fight to take place in the UK, while Sela, Netflix and the other parties involved favor New York. Hearn has submitted separate terms that would allow Joshua to accept Madison Square Garden, but he made clear that his preference remains a British stadium.

If Sela rejects those changes, Hearn expects the company to follow the existing contract and deliver the event in the UK.

“If they deliver on the contract, which they have to legally, the fight’s happening in the UK, and we’ll be very, very happy,” Hearn said. “The only way it can stop from happening is if they actually breach the contract.”

That line leaves Sela with two direct options: honor the UK agreement or meet Joshua’s terms for America. Sela can still abandon the event in practice, but doing so may expose the company to a costly legal claim. The possible damages cannot be calculated without seeing the cancellation and breach provisions.

Hearn’s claim is legally forceful but practically overstated. Sela cannot withdraw without risking financial penalties, but it can still refuse to finance the event. A contract creates legal consequences for breaking an agreement; it does not guarantee that a boxing match reaches the ring.

The greater issue may come after the lawyers finish. Joshua has received some of his largest purses through Turki Alalshikh and Sela. Hearn can use the UK clause to secure better terms for New York, but pushing too far risks damaging the relationship that makes paydays of this size possible. Few other backers can offer Joshua comparable money at this stage of his career.

Ghana News.title: TrafficTech cameras to target motorists speeding above 50km/h in school zones — Police
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Police Service has indicated that the deployment of TrafficTech cameras and other technological devices will be used to detect motorists who exceed speed limits in school zones and densely populated areas.

Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Alexander Kwaku Obeng said the initiative would strengthen enforcement and address dangerous driving practices that contribute to preventable road crashes.

He said the system would target offences including “excessive speed above the limits of certain instances, above 50 kilometres per hour in school zone areas and above 50 kilometres per hour in built-up, crowded areas”.

ACP Obeng, who disclosed this on JoyFM's Super Morning Show on Wednesday, August 26, added that the technology would also monitor speeding on highways, roads connecting communities and motorways, where some drivers exceed the prescribed limits and endanger other road users.

“The police are required to deploy traffic devices that are technological. Those hardware devices include cameras and other devices, whether they are independently working on their own, handheld, left on tripods or mounted permanently on poles,” he explained.

According to him, the required equipment has been procured and is currently being tested, while the software and back-office infrastructure needed to operate the system are also ready.

“That capability has been procured and is being tested, with the back office built, the hardware ready and the software application that will run on this police technology also available,” he said.

ACP Obeng indicated that the Ministry of Transport, supported by agencies within the road safety management sub-sector, would oversee the certification process ahead of the system’s rollout.

He said evidence collected through the devices would allow the police to take action against vehicle owners and drivers, including issuing court notices to those found to have violated speed limits.

Ghana News.title: “We may be down, but we are not out” — Boakye Agyarko vows to revive NPP as he files for National Chairman
Ghana News.content:
Former Energy Minister Boakye Agyarko has declared that the New Patriotic Party (NPP) will recover from its current challenges and return to political power.

Mr Agyarko arrived at the NPP headquarters in the company of prominent party figures, Henry Quartey, Gyapa Mercer, Alhassan Tampuli, Matthew Nyindam, and supporters to file his nomination to contest as National Chairman.

Speaking after receiving a call from about 50 NPP constituency chairpersons to offer himself for the party’s leadership, Mr Agyarko said he had accepted the challenge as part of efforts to revive the party.

He stressed that his decision was not motivated by privilege or the powers associated with political office, but by what he described as a responsibility to help restore the NPP.

“I respond to a call to revive our party from its current doldrums. It is not a call I respond to lightly,” Mr. Agyarko said.

He urged party members not to lose hope despite the NPP’s current difficulties, insisting that the party still had the capacity to bounce back.

“We may be down, but we are not out. NPP shall rise again,” he declared.

Mr Agyarko drew on religious teachings to encourage party supporters, saying periods of difficulty would eventually give way to better times.

“After every hardship, there is ease,” he said, expressing confidence that the NPP would overcome its present challenges and return to government.

He said his ultimate objective was to help the party regain power and support the presidential ambitions of former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia.

“I believe that this, our NPP, will see its period of ease. And that period will be when we win power, make Dr Mahamudu Bawumia the President,” he stated.

According to Mr Agyarko, an NPP government under Dr Bawumia would implement policies aimed at improving governance and creating conditions for peace and development in Ghana.

He said his team had presented themselves to the party and the wider public with the hope of earning the confidence of NPP delegates.

He concluded with a direct appeal to delegates to support his bid, saying: “NPP delegates, give me your votes, and we will finish the job that is ahead of you.”

Ghana News.title: TrafficTech to reduce roadside encounters between police and motorists — Police
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Police Service says the planned deployment of its TrafficTech system will reduce direct encounters between officers and motorists during the enforcement of road traffic regulations.

Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Alexander Kwaku Obeng said the technology would enable officers to gather evidence of traffic offences using cameras, smartphones and other digital devices.

“The law requires that, under the regulation I referred to, which has over 49 automated offences, the police are supposed to gather evidence with devices for vehicle owners and drivers to be forthcoming, rather than being stopped and taken to police stations,” he said on JoyFM's Super Morning Show on Wednesday, August 26, while discussing the services of the new technology.

According to ACP Obeng, the initiative represents a significant departure from the existing approach to traffic enforcement, which largely involves officers stopping suspected offenders on the road.

“It is a complete departure from how we are going to deliver our service, such that the police are required to deploy traffic devices that are technological,” he explained.

He said the devices would include independently operated cameras, handheld equipment and systems mounted permanently on poles or placed on tripods.

The police are also developing a mobile application that will enable officers to use personal digital assistants, Android devices and smartphones to record offences committed on the roads.

“We are building our capacity and developing fast a software application that will also allow police to have other PDA or Android devices and smartphones,” ACP Obeng stated.

He said the necessary TrafficTech hardware and software had already been procured and were undergoing testing, while the supporting back-office infrastructure had been established.

The system is expected to capture evidence that could be used to trace offending motorists, issue court notices and pursue prosecution without immediately taking drivers to police stations.

Ghana News.title: Study links unofficial Ghana border crossings to documentation gaps, financial hardship
Ghana News.content:
Alleged extortion at Ghana’s official border posts, coupled with financial difficulties and inadequate travel documentation, is pushing some immigrants to enter the country through unapproved routes, a study has found.

The research argues that efforts to strengthen border security must extend beyond surveillance and address the underlying challenges that discourage travellers from using authorised entry points.

The study, titled “Cross-Border Migration of Itinerant Immigrant Retailers in Ghana”, was conducted by Professor Elijah Yendaw, a professor of Population and Migration Studies at the University of Business and Integrated Development Studies (UBIDS) in Wa.

READ ALSO: Albert Kuzor writes: My recent trip to Togo and why ECOWAS must sit up

Its findings were outlined in a policy brief titled “Free Movement, Unapproved Routes: Closing Ghana’s Documentation, Trust and Border-Governance Gaps for West African Itinerant Traders”.

Using data collected from 779 itinerant retailers from West African countries in the Accra Metropolis, the study found that 58.2 per cent entered Ghana through unapproved routes, while 41.8 per cent used recognised border crossings.

All respondents reportedly travelled by land, with 71.9 per cent using buses or other vehicles and the remaining 28.1 per cent making the journey on foot.

The findings established a strong link between access to travel documents and migrants’ choice of entry route. All respondents who cited a lack of documentation as a factor in their decision said they used unapproved routes. In contrast, 98.4 per cent of those with travel documents entered through official crossing points.

Financial hardship was also identified as a significant factor, with 95.8 per cent of respondents who struggled to fund their journeys choosing unapproved routes.

The policy brief also documented participants’ allegations of harassment and demands for unofficial payments at some authorised border posts. However, it cautioned that the claims reflected the experiences reported by participants and should not be treated as independently verified estimates of misconduct.

According to the report, effective migration management requires improved border governance rather than an exclusive focus on tightening controls. It called for official crossing points to be made safer, more transparent, easier to navigate and more appealing than irregular alternatives.

The study proposed six policy interventions, including simplifying the use of approved routes, improving access to travel documents and pre-departure information, and establishing credible mechanisms for reporting extortion.

It also recommended evidence-led surveillance along specific migration corridors, stronger databases on mobile immigrant traders and cross-border movements, and closer collaboration with migrant associations and border communities.

The report said travellers should receive clear information about required documents, authorised fees, expected processing times and available complaint or support channels at border posts.

It further proposed working with consulates, transport unions, migrant associations, community leaders and other stakeholders to educate travellers about documentation requirements and their rights and responsibilities under ECOWAS free-movement protocols.

Such information, it said, should be communicated in widely spoken regional languages through radio, transport terminals, visual materials and other accessible platforms.

The study also urged authorities to regard border communities as partners in orderly migration. It said their involvement could support route mapping, public education and the early identification of changing migration patterns.

Ghana News.title: TrafficTech to issue court notices to speeding motorists based on camera evidence — Police
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Police Service says motorists caught exceeding prescribed speed limits under its planned TrafficTech system could be issued court notices based on evidence captured by automated devices.

Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Alexander Kwaku Obeng said the system would use cameras and other technological devices to detect and document road traffic offences.

“We hope to issue court notices to those who may be violating speed limits in their vehicles,” he said in an interview on JoyFM's Super Morning Show on Wednesday, August 26.

ACP Obeng explained that the initiative was supported by Regulation 242 of the Road Traffic Regulations, 2020 (L.I. 2519), which provides for automated road traffic offences and fines.

“The police are required to deploy traffic devices that are technological. Those hardware devices, including cameras and other devices, whether they are independently working on their own, handheld, left on tripods or mounted permanently on poles,” he stated.

According to him, the system will particularly target motorists who exceed speed limits in school zones, densely populated areas, highways and motorways.

He disclosed that the necessary hardware and software had been procured and were being tested, while a back-office system had also been established to facilitate enforcement.

“That capability has been procured and is being tested, with the back office built, the hardware ready and the software application that will run on this police technology also available,” ACP Obeng said.

He added that the Ministry of Transport, supported by agencies within the road safety management sub-sector, would lead the certification process before the technology becomes fully operational.

ACP Obeng said evidence captured by the devices would enable the police to pursue vehicle owners and drivers without necessarily stopping them and taking them to police stations.

Ghana News.title: Tricycle, motorcycle operators face arrest after August deadline for reflective stickers
Ghana News.content:
Tricycle and motorcycle operators in the Greater Accra Region who fail to affix reflective stickers to their vehicles by the end of August risk arrest as authorities step up enforcement of road safety measures.

The directive is part of a joint effort by the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA) and the Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) to improve the visibility of motorcycles and tricycles, particularly at night, and reduce road crashes.

Speaking on Tuesday, August 25, Accra Regional Manager of the DVLA, Justice Cudjoe, said reflective stickers, helmets and reflective jackets would form part of the safety requirements for operators.

“For safety purposes and to be able to identify you, especially when you are moving in the night, we need to fix these reflective substances on the motorbike,” he said.

Justice Cudjoe said the reflective stickers should cost operators no more than GH¢100.

“Maximum 100 Cedis should be enough to affix this reflective on your tricycle,” he stated.

He warned that operators who fail to comply with the directive by the end of August would be arrested.

“The mayor has given a deadline of the end of August. Any user of such equipment who has not complied with the policy or the directive, motorbike or tricycle, will be arrested,” he cautioned.

The enforcement follows growing concerns over the use of motorcycles and tricycles on Ghanaian roads, including concerns about visibility, compliance with safety regulations and road crashes.

Preliminary police investigations into a recent fatal crash on the Accra-Nsawam highway have also reportedly linked a tricycle operator to the incident.

Authorities say they are decentralising the exercise to make it easier for operators to comply before the August 31 deadline.

Greater Accra Regional Minister Linda Ocloo said operators would not have to travel to the DVLA headquarters in Accra to access the service.

She said the exercise would be available through district offices and assemblies across the region.

“We have offices, I would say we have all the 29 districts. I mean, I’m referring to Greater Accra. We have our district offices around, so not necessarily leaving Pokuase to come to Accra,” she said.

According to the Regional Minister, operators can visit their respective assemblies to access the necessary services.

The reflective stickers are expected to make motorcycles and tricycles more visible to other road users, particularly at night, while also making the vehicles easier to identify.

The authorities are urging operators to comply with the directive before the August 31 deadline to avoid enforcement action.

The exercise forms part of broader efforts to improve road safety in the Greater Accra Region amid concerns over road crashes and compliance with traffic regulations.

Ghana News.title: Ambassador Quartey highlights Ghana’s sustainable cocoa sector at Cocoa Connect Seminar in Rimini
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s Ambassador to Italy, H.E. Mona Quartey

Ghana’s Ambassador to Italy, H.E. Mona Quartey, has led a diplomatic delegation to the prestigious Meeting di Rimini to participate in the seminar "Cacao Connect: The Italian Way to the Sustainable Cocoa Supply Chain in Africa." She was accompanied by Mr. Kwesi Amuzu-Kpene, Head of Chancery of the Ghanaian Embassy in Rome.

During the event, Ambassador Quartey held exhaustive interactions with key global stakeholders, Italian institutional bodies (including MAECI and CDP), and major industry leaders like Ferrero and ICAM. Her discussions focused on promoting Ghana's exceptional quality standards, fostering public-private partnerships, and advancing climate-resilient, fair-trade practices within the cocoa supply chain.

Ambassador Quartey also shared vital updates on the Ghana Cocoa Board Bill 2026, which is expected to gain Presidential assent and soon to be passed into Law. She emphasized that this new Bill represents an asset for the sector - not only by improving the fortunes of local cocoa farmers but also by creating a highly attractive framework for investors focused on local value addition.

This active participation underscores the Embassy's firm commitment to economic diplomacy - positioning Ghana as a leading strategic partner for sustainable development and agro-processing in Europe.

Ghana News.title: World Bank calls for far-reaching reforms to COCOBOD Act
Ghana News.content:
The World Bank is calling for far-reaching reforms to the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) Act to promote market-based principles and reduce the financial risks associated with the cocoa sector.

The World Bank Division Director for Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone, Robert R. Taliercio , said financial and operational inefficiencies within COCOBOD were placing a strain on farmers and the country’s public finances.

Speaking at the launch of the World Bank’s Tenth Ghana Economic Update in Accra, Mr Taliercio said reforms to the legal and operational framework governing COCOBOD were necessary to ensure the sustainability of the cocoa sector.

“We welcome continued discussion and debate on the Cocoa Board Act, and we suggest that far-reaching reforms of the Act are needed to promote market-based principles and minimise quasi-fiscal risks,” he said.

He said without decisive reforms in the cocoa and energy sectors, some of the fiscal gains achieved under Ghana’s economic reform programme could quickly be eroded.

The World Bank’s call comes amid concerns over the financial position of COCOBOD and the impact of its operations on the government’s finances.

Mr Taliercio said the cocoa sector’s challenges were among the key domestic risks that could undermine Ghana’s economic recovery if not addressed.

He further stressed the need for Ghana to strengthen its fiscal position and reduce reliance on measures that could create additional pressure on public finances.

The World Bank official said Ghana’s economic recovery remained “structurally incomplete” despite significant improvements in key macroeconomic indicators.

He noted that the country’s heavy dependence on cocoa and gold exports also exposes the economy to fluctuations in international commodity prices.

According to him, diversifying Ghana’s export base and implementing reforms that support market-based economic activity would be critical to building a more resilient economy.

The World Bank therefore urged the government to sustain the reform momentum and address structural weaknesses in the cocoa sector to protect fiscal gains and support long-term economic growth.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
