World.title: America unites in mourning for Dolly Parton
World.content:
Los Angeles – Americans of all stripes united to grieve the death of country music legend Dolly Parton, offering a rare moment of agreement as presidents of both parties joined entertainment and business giants in paying her tribute.

The singer, who was 80, was long heralded as one of the few celebrities that everybody loved.

President Donald Trump announced the lowering of flags across the United States for a week, calling Parton’s death a “true loss for millions of people.”

“Very sad to report that Dolly Parton, one of the greatest Country singers, and far beyond, EVER, has just passed away,” Trump posted on his Truth Social network. “There has never been anyone like her, and never will.”

His predecessor Joe Biden called Parton “an American original” who “treated everyone with kindness and respect.”

Republican George W. Bush praised “her work to promote literacy, advance health, and strengthen communities,” while Democratic former president Bill Clinton called her “one of a kind.”

New York’s mayor, Zohran Mamdani, praised Parton as “an irreplaceable champion of the working class.”

“We are a better country because of her,” he said.

– ‘Devastating day for humanity’ –

Singer Miley Cyrus took to X to mourn the passing of Parton, who was her godmother.

“So many evil people in this world and we had to lose a pure heart like Dolly Parton,” Cyrus said. “Devastating day for humanity.”

Popstar Taylor Swift, who got her start in country music, said a world without Parton “doesn’t feel possible, real, or right.”

“Her legacy will be an everlasting one,” Swift said in a statement shared with Variety and The Hollywood Reporter.

Beyonce, who collaborated with Parton for her Grammy-winning album “Cowboy Carter,” also paid tribute to the star.

“Bold and brilliant. Talented and tenacious. You taught so many lessons on how to be uniquely oneself,” Beyonce said on her website.

Rocker Jack White, who covered one of Parton’s most famous hits “Jolene,” called for her “instant sainthood” on Instagram.

Rapper Kid Rock, who worked with Parton, called her “quite simply” the greatest of all time.

“Thanks for the songs, the laughs, the humility and grace. Without a doubt a woman who God truly has his hands on.”

– ‘Magical and joyous’ –

Across the world of entertainment there was a palpable sense of loss, but also one of gratefulness for a person whose life was filled with joy and compassion.

Country music star Carrie Underwood said Parton “was probably the one person on planet Earth that everyone loved and could agree on”.

Popstar Sabrina Carpenter, who collaborated with Parton in 2024, recalled meeting Parton for the first time, describing her as “an angel walking the earth.”

“Your light will be something the world will search forever to find again,” Carpenter said on Instagram.

Actress Jane Fonda, who performed opposite Parton in “9 to 5” mourned Parton’s loss.

“Dolly will always be with us because she was so present, so powerful, so generous and playful that she is woven into all our lives and hearts forever,” Fonda said on Instagram.

Parton’s “Steel Magnolias” co-star Julia Roberts called her “a magical and joyous human.”

Country music star Jason Aldean said he was grateful to have been in Parton’s company a few times over the years.

“She was truly a bright light that shined just a little brighter than anyone else in the room,” he wrote on X.

– Apple, Amazon and a Beatle –

Beatle Paul McCartney posted on Instagram about meeting Parton early in her career, adding “she was so bubbly and full of life it is difficult to take in the news that she has passed.”

Even rapper Eminem praised Parton, sharing a letter she had written him after he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

“She definitely didn’t have to take the time to do it. Even for a kid who mostly listened to rap music, she was an icon. A superstar in every sense,” he wrote on X.

Business titans also paid tribute to the Grammy winner.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos said he and wife Lauren Sanchez Bezos were “so grateful to have known her.”

Apple’s Tim Cook said called Parton a “brilliant songwriter, cultural icon and dedicated philanthropist” whose music “helped light up the world.”

World.title: Meta and US states discuss settlement in landmark social media trial: report
World.content:
San Francisco – Social media giant Meta has been in discussions with multiple US states to settle a major child privacy and consumer protection case out of court, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday.

With more than three billion users around the world, Meta is fending off accusations by a coalition of 29 states that it deliberately designed its products to hook children and gather their data while misleading the public.

The states are claiming that Meta violated both state-level and federal laws, though the exact allegations vary by state.

If Meta loses the case, the states could ask for around $200 billion in penalties, in addition to forcing the tech company to make changes to its products.

“Meta Platforms Inc. and state attorneys general have discussed a possible mid-trial settlement,” Bloomberg reported, citing anonymous sources familiar with the matter.

California, Colorado, New Jersey and Kentucky are leading the prosecution of Meta from a courtroom in Oakland, just a short drive from San Francisco.

Multiple state attorneys general sent out media advisories late Tuesday that they would hold press conferences on Wednesday regarding consumer protections and tech-related announcements.

Colorado said it would announce “a major update in a Big Tech case.”

Nevada, which is not involved with the trial in California, said it would make an announcement Wednesday regarding a “settlement” with “a leading technology company.”

Representatives for Meta and California Attorney General Rob Bonta did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Instagram boss Adam Mosseri took the stand on Tuesday as the trial entered its second week.

Mosseri admitted he touted newly launched safety tools for teens without disclosing low adoption rates from early testing several years ago.

Other witnesses have testified over the past week that Meta knew these tools were not effective and even that they were “designed to fail.”

Meta founder and chief executive Mark Zuckerberg was expected to testify at some point, as well.

World.title: Pakistan hospital fire kills 14 infants
World.content:
Islamabad – A fire erupted in a hospital’s maternity ward in Islamabad on Wednesday, killing 14 infants, Pakistani authorities said, with the prime minister calling for an investigation.

The fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Health Ward at the public Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), the Islamabad district office said in a statement.

The statement gave a death toll of 14, who according to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif were all infants.

Sharif and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi expressed “deep grief and sorrow over the deaths of 14 infants” in separate statements.

“Such a situation involving children is irreparable,” the prime minister said.

“The circumstances that led to the incident should be thoroughly reviewed, those responsible should be identified, and the strictest possible action should be taken.”

Authorities have not identified the cause of the fire.

Sohail Ashraf, the Islamabad chief commissioner, said the emergency call was made just before 7:00 am (0200 GMT), with rescue and police teams reaching the scene “immediately” and bringing the fire under control.

Outside the hospital, an AFP reporter saw a woman in tears and a man clear glass from two broken windows, as security guards stood at the entrance to the leading medical facility.

Fires in large buildings are frequent in Pakistan, often due to poor safety laws and building codes as well as lax enforcement.

In January, more than 65 people were killed in a shopping centre fire in the port city of Karachi.

At least 11 people were killed in another shopping mall fire in Karachi in 2023.

In 2021, at least 16 workers died after a factory fire in the same city.

In 2012, at least 250 labourers died at a garment factory in Baldia Town, in western Karachi, when a fire engulfed the facility. The building had no fire escape.

World.title: Nepal floods: PM Modi speaks to Balen Shah, offers support
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday expressed condolences over the loss of lives in devastating floods in Nepal and offered Indiaâs assistance for rescue and relief efforts.

âSpoke to Prime Minister Balendra Shah and conveyed condolences on the loss of lives due to the floods in Nepal,â

wrote on X. âThe people of India stand in solidarity with their sisters and brothers in Nepal at this difficult time.â

PM Modi added that India was prepared to support Nepal as the country dealt with the disaster. âIndia is ready to provide all possible humanitarian assistance to Nepal. Our teams are coordinating closely on rescue and relief efforts,â he said.

The floods swept through northern Nepal on Wednesday morning after the Bhote Koshi River surged, reportedly from the direction of Tibet. Timure in Rasuwa district and nearby Syafrubesi suffered extensive damage, with vehicles, goods and other property washed away.

105 Indians among hundreds missing after deadly flash flood

Floods battered Nepal on Wednesday after a sudden flash flood swept through Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, leaving at least eight people dead and hundreds missing, including 105 Indians.





The Bhote Koshi River surged through the Rasuwagadhi-Timure area at around 9am, affecting parts of Rasuwa as well as neighbouring Nuwakot and Dhading districts. Vehicles, bridges, goods and other infrastructure were washed away, while several hydropower projects were damaged.

World.title: Madras Crocodile Bank turns 50: How does this reptilian zoo run?
World.content:
Zai Whitaker distinctly remembers Madras Crocodile Bank Trust’s (MCBT) first-ever gharial.

As incredulous as it sounds, it arrived in a box.

The small zoo dedicated to reptiles on what was once a desolate East Coast Road in Tamil Nadu had been up and running since 1976 when among the rarest crocodilians on Earth, made its way to Chennai from somewhere in Central/ North India. A pen was dug up in the late 1980s with some water to accommodate this river guardian that was most critically endangered because human activities had destroyed its freshwater river habitat. Down South was certainly one way to go.

“The gharial came in a box… I think the carrier was from Kukrail, Uttar Pradesh, but I’m not sure. We [co-founder Rom and a few animal handlers] were all standing around it. Of course, when the animal is released from the box, you don’t know what it’s going to do, where it’s going to go. We were waiting and watching. Fortunately, it was very well behaved. It ran straight into the water, and since then there has been no looking back,” she says.

Fifty years since it first began, over 47 gharials (out of 395 crocs) have made the MCBT their home. This is besides the 32 other reptile species including the three Indian crocodilians, turtles, snakes, and lizards, across the eight and a half acre campus. Hundreds of animal handlers, educators, volunteers, staff members, and researchers make Croc Bank the institution it continues to be. Rom and Zai, who made this small piece of land in Vadanamelli village their home, have gone on to commission and pioneer a number of marquee programmes including the Snake Bite Mitigation Project, benefitting and aiding reptilian research essential reading in India. At the Croc Bank today, where Zai sits near a hatchery to write and oversee operations, a certain quiet enthusiasm takes over the space. As we walk through the quieter parts of the campus, amidst trees that the duo planted, half a century ago, Zai says that the years both seem to shrink and expand. Time is, after all, relative.

Pothole portal

The story unfortunately began during a point of infliction: a crisis. By the 1960s, hunting crocodiles for their skin had pushed their population into decline. Indian crocs like the mugger crocodile, saltwater crocodile, and gharials, faced massive existential threats. The Indian Government decided that it was time to protect the three species under the Wildlife Protection Act of 1972.

Zai says that by then, herpetologist Romulus ‘Rom’ Whitaker was already a well-known conservationist in India. He had been conducting several crocodile surveys besides setting up and running the Snake Park at Guindy. The idea for the croc bank came to him while he was sitting atop a truck, hitching a ride back home from a crocodile survey in 1972 all the way from Odisha.

“I think he was coming back from a survey because he’d run out of money. It was just everyday stuff for us. This wonderful truck driver gave him a free ride all the way from Orissa to the gate of the Snake Park in Chennai, which is where he was headed. So he wrote me this letter, which I should still have somewhere, saying why don’t we start a croc-breeding facility, and then rewild them with the help of the Forest Department. ‘People could come to visit and look at the animals, so maybe we could charge a ticket, and the future Mrs Whitaker’ — because by then we were talking about getting married — would have some daily income for food and other necessities. That was actually how it started,” Zai says.

The Madras Crocodile Bank was formally established on August 26, 1976 by Rom, Zai, and a group of like-minded conservationists, funded initially by wedding gifts; steady family support (including contributions by Zai’s father conservationist Zafar Rashid Futehally, who started the World Wildlife Fund-India, and Zai’s uncle decorated ornithologist Salim Ali); and the sale of a few possessions including a trusty old tape recorder (priceless back in the day). They bought their first plot of coastal land near Chennai for about ₹5,000 an acre even though the initial price was ₹4,500. “He increased it seeing how enthusiastic we got about the land,” Zai says.

Over the years, besides breeding crocs, turtles, tortoises at the bank, commissioning research about crocodile-human conflict, and devising educational programmes, they have set up the Andaman and Nicobar Environmental Team (ANET) in 1990, and the Irula Snake Catchers’ Industrial Cooperative Society which has helped the Irulas (left without jobs after the Wildlife Act banned snakeskin trade) earn a livelihood extracting snake venom for anti-venom production.

Zai says that they have been intent on building a passionate team. One that is enthusiastic about saying yes to the most unlikely of circumstances. Zai particularly remembers the likes of researchers who recently passed, including Jagannathan Vijaya, Satish Bhaskar, and D Basu. “We would tell them ‘There are dacoits there, and you’ll spend the night sleeping on the sand banks with pythons’. It was always the response of these three people, ‘oh yeah, that’s great, I would love to do that.’ We might have thought that we were doing them a favour. But these were three people who created the space in India to conserve sea turtles, freshwater turtles, and the gharial. Their initial studies were what took that whole conservation movement forward. I hope that continues,” she says.

When we meet 38-year-old second generation animal handler G Gowrishankar, we realise what Zai means. The crocs recognise his voice and amble towards him. Someone in the crowd who watches him call to the muggers in the pit next to us, remarks, “Who is this guy? He’s herding them like they are goats”.

Gowrishankar says that some of these beasts have become his favourites. Over time, he has learnt to enter the pits, feed specific crocs, assess their health, and even catch and quarantine them in case of ailments. This is strenuous work that requires brute strength, tactic, and a genuine understanding of the animal.

What it takes

Vaibhavi Bhardwaj, who grew up loving animals and wanting snakes for pets, is now a zoo educator at MCBT. She is a big proponent of the volunteer programme and says that it is a great jump-off point for those who wish to seriously enter the conservation space. She says that besides the public interactions she does during feed timings, where she tells people about the reptiles, and debunks myths about specific species, she conducts reptile awareness programmes for schools, and snake bite mitigation campaigns. She also helps educate volunteers and tells them how a zoo runs.

“One of the things volunteers participate in is husbandry activities: maintenance and constant checking on the reptiles. Reptiles are animals that are really hard to catch illness in, because they’re very good at masking anything that’s wrong — it’s a survival instinct for them. So our keepers are trained to observe small abnormalities in behaviour, which they do every morning,” she says, speaking about how a zoo runs.

“Apart from that, our vet constantly checks what supplements need to be added to their feed, which the volunteers help with, along with the bedding. There’s constant screening of things like faeces to check for illness, especially worms. Then the education department is mostly involved in breaking the barrier between an animal behind a pen and the people who come to observe them — building a connection by making people realise these animals are important, that they’re an integral keystone species maintaining the ecosystem, and bringing about the value they play in the wild,” she adds.

Today, as part of the 50th year celebrations, Ganesh Muthiah, trustee, MCBT, says that he will embark on a 15,000 kilometre journey across 20 Indian states over 120 days. The idea is to educate people about a Save the Reptiles Campaign that they are launching. This is besides a number of activities including photography contests and educating people about reptiles in their midst. “We are excited about the undertaking,” says this long-term-volunteer-turned-trustee, who is ever enthusiastic to speak about the days of yore. “Rom is like our Indiana Jones,” he says, speaking about the founder, who is scheduled to participate in the celebrations despite his advanced age.

Besides elaborating on everything that the Croc Bank does, everyone seems to have only one piece of information for anyone who walks in. “They may seem like they are still, and aren’t doing much. They may not seem cute and cuddly. But do not forget — they are definitely wild creatures. No going too close to the pen,” Vaibhavi says.

Madras Crocodile Bank Trust is at 4, East Coast Road, Vadanamelli Village, Mahabalipuram. The bank is closed on Mondays. Entry is priced at ₹110 for adults and ₹50 for children.

World.title: Centre examining proposal to tweak mining rules for Meghalaya: CM
World.content:
Meghalaya Chief Minister Conrad K. Sangma said that the Centre was examining the State government’s proposal to tweak the mining rules to suit local conditions.

He told the 60-member Assembly on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) that the Ministry of Coal acknowledged Meghalaya’s unique mining conditions and the need for a separate approach.

Replying to a short-duration discussion raised by Ardent Miller Basaiawmoit, the president of the regional Voice of the People Party (VPP), Mr. Sangma said authorised coal production began in three coal blocks after the Ministry of Coal granted mining leases for 12 blocks.

He said the National Green Tribunal (NGT) banned the hazardous practice of rat-hole coal mining in Meghalaya in April 2014. However, the Supreme Court allowed scientific mining in 2019, subject to compliance with the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, or MMDR Act; the Mines Act, 1952; and the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

Land ownership issues

The Chief Minister said implementing scientific mining has been difficult because coal-bearing areas in Meghalaya are largely under traditional land ownership and the State’s steep coal seams make open-cast mining impractical in several locations.

“The Ministry of Coal views Meghalaya’s case differently, and it understands that a framework to balance safety and livelihood is necessary,” he said.

He reminded the House of his recent meeting with Coal Minister G. Kishan Reddy in New Delhi along with the MLA of a coal-bearing area to discuss the difficulties associated with the transition to scientific mining. “The Union Minister told officials to examine the issue and find a workable solution,” he said.

Granting mining leases

Mr. Sangma said one of the key challenges in expanding scientific coal mining in Meghalaya was the regulatory requirement of a minimum 100-hectare area for granting mining leases. “This requirement poses significant difficulties for small miners, many of whom do not possess landholdings of the prescribed size,” he said.

The Chief Minister said that he urged the Centre to consider reducing the minimum concession area from 100 hectares, set up a unit to monitor mining activity in the State, and delegate powers under Section 26 of the MMDR Act to the State government to handle all aspects of mining.

He further said that the scale of mining in East Jaintia Hills district has added to the challenge of implementing scientific operations. “The district has about 22,000 coal mines, which makes it difficult for the officials to ensure the operations are carried out according to the law,” he said.

Mr. Sangma said illegal mining led to the closure of coal mines in Meghalaya, affecting the livelihood of thousands of people. “Our government’s objective is to allow mining within a legal framework, while cracking down on illegal operations,” he said.

A committee constituted by the High Court of Meghalaya has repeatedly slammed the State government for failing to curb illegal coal mining and transportation.

World.title: AM Intelligence orders 9,000 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs for AI factory in Hyderabad

AI infrastructure company AM Intelligence on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) said it has placed a firm and binding order for 9,000 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs for its first AI factory in Hyderabad.

The 9,000 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs, with their delivery slated in Q1 2027, are to be deployed as Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale systems at the 30 MW AI factory, making the facility one of the first frontier AI compute clusters in Asia.

AM Intelligence, which has been set up by the promoters of Greenko, said Hyderabad facility is the first tranche of AMI’s planned 1 GW global compute-as-a-service capacity. Initially, AMI plans to bring 200 megawatts (MW) of capacity to market in the near term, involving capital expenditure of more than $8 billion.

It is developing 5 GW of powered AI data centres across India, the U.S. and Europe, integrating energy and next-generation compute to deliver competitive electron-to-token economics for hyperscalers, sovereign AI initiatives, frontier labs and AI-native companies, the company said in a release.

By integrating NVIDIA Vera Rubin architecture with high-throughput RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE) networking for fast, efficient data movement and advanced storage systems, the Hyderabad AI Factory is being designed to run some of the world’s largest and most sophisticated AI models, including trillion-parameter models and next-generation agentic AI applications, Chairman Anil Chalamalasetty said.

NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 introduces NVFP4, a new low-precision computing format designed to run AI workloads more efficiently, alongside next-generation High Bandwidth Memory (HBM4). AMI said the Hyderabad AI Factory is being engineered to deliver approximately 450 exaFLOPS of NVFP4 inference compute, providing massive computing capacity for running advanced AI models at scale.

World.title: IIT Delhi constitutes external panel to probe student’s death; stir on campus continues
World.content:
IIT Delhi has constituted a seven-member external committee to probe the circumstances leading to the death of the 31-year-old MSc student, the institute Director, Rangan Banerjee, stated in an e-mail addressed to all students on Tuesday.

IIT Delhi constitutes external panel to probe student’s death; stir on campus continues

The death of the student, allegedly by suicide on the campus on August 22, has sparked uproar among several student bodies. Students at the institute have been protesting since Monday against “systemic issues”, which they claim have led to the deaths of eight students by suicide over the past 30 months.

Student well-being in India declines sharply through senior school years, finds study

On Tuesday, they submitted a collective note to the administration, demanding that the deceased’s family be paid ₹1 crore in compensation.

Later in the day, Aam Aadmi Party chief and former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal and the Cockroach Janta Party issued statements, expressing solidarity with the protesting students.

Review of protocols

The external panel will comprise former Uttarakhand police chief Ashok Kumar, AIIMS Delhi Psychiatry Department head Professor Pratap Sharma, four student representatives and the institute’s Registrar. Mr. Banerjee said the committee will hold talks with students, faculty members and officials concerned and review existing protocols and processes, adding that it will be requested to complete its report within two weeks.

The quiet crisis of adolescent mental health in India

The IIT Director said the institute would provide financial support to the family of the deceased, though he did not specify the amount. As per the e-mail, the student, who had a good academic record, developed mental health issues in March and was advised to stay under “continuous parental supervision”, following which he moved off campus with his parents. When he returned in July after a break, his medical records were checked and he was again advised to stay under parental supervision.

Objection to panel member

Students objected to the inclusion of Mr. Kumar in the panel, citing his purported comments on recent youth-led agitations, linking the protesters with “radicalisation”. They also condemned the administration’s view that students with mental health issues need parental support.

“As students, they need access to peers, fair academic opportunities, and a supportive, empathetic campus. Without a clear undertaking on the aforementioned points, an additional support system of a faculty and student mentor seems like a band-aid solution in a broken system,” read the note submitted by the IIT Delhi students.

The students added that “disparaging comments” had been made by faculty members against the protesting students and asked that no action be taken against students protesting peacefully.

(Those in distress can contact Tele MANAS at 14416 to seek help.)

World.title: BJP’s promise of ‘achche din’ has wrecked the common man’s kitchen budget, says Kharge
World.content:
Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge on Wednesday (August 26, 2026) targeted the Narendra Modi government over the rising prices of essential commodities, saying the “achche din” (good times) promised by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) had instead left the common person’s household budget battered by food inflation.

In a post on X, Mr. Kharge said the BJP was attempting to evade accountability through “distracting stunts and nonsensical talk”, but the Congress and the public would continue to raise questions over inflation.

“Take a look at the state of the common man’s kitchen during festivals — onion prices have risen by up to 59% in a year, ₹50-60 a kg in many cities; sugar ₹60-70 a kg, up to ₹72 a kg in some places; mustard oil over ₹200 a litre; food inflation 5.52%; wholesale inflation 9.78%,” Mr. Kharge said.

He said that after 12 years of BJP rule, “sometimes lentils, sometimes vegetables, sometimes oil, sometimes sugar” continued to put pressure on household budgets.

The Congress chief cited a comparison of retail prices in May 2013 and August 2026, based on figures attributed to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation and newspaper reports.

The comparison showed steep increases across several kitchen staples. Tomatoes recorded the sharpest rise, from ₹17.50 a kg in May 2013 to ₹120 now — an increase of 585.71%. Onion prices rose from ₹23 to ₹73 a kg, or 217.39%, while atta increased from ₹21 to ₹69 a kg, a rise of 228.57%.

Among pulses, tur dal rose from ₹75 to ₹180 a kg, urad dal from ₹71 to ₹180 and chana dal from ₹50 to ₹125 — increases of 140%, 153.52% and 150%, respectively. Mustard oil rose from ₹102 to ₹263 a kg, while groundnut oil increased from ₹165 to ₹286. Milk prices rose from ₹36 to ₹85 a litre. Rice increased from ₹29 to ₹71 a kg, sugar from ₹37 to ₹84 and potato from ₹24 to ₹51. The Congress said several essential commodities had thus recorded price increases of more than 100% over the period.

The comparison comes amid the Congress’s continuing attack on the government over inflation and the cost of living.

The Opposition party has accused the Modi government of failing to contain prices of essential commodities and said voters would “remember this and will not forgive”.

World.title: 14 infants killed in fire at Pims' gynae ward in Islamabad
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Fourteen infants were killed in a fire that broke out in the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) early on Wednesday.

Footage aired on television showed rescue workers using ladders to reach broken windows to access the affected area. Outside the hospital, an AFP reporter saw a woman in tears and a man clear glass from two broken windows, as security guards stood at the entrance to the medical facility.

Several witnesses, their hands and faces blackened from the smoke, told AFP they waited hours for help from the emergency services. They were forced to smash through windows to try and get to the neonatal intensive care unit.

Others said they came across locked doors and alleged guards prevented those inside the building from leaving as the fire raged.

In a statement, the Islamabad administration said that the fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Hospital’s ward. It said that rescue teams rushed to the scene, with six fire brigade vehicles and four ambulances taking part in the rescue operation.

“The fire was immediately brought under control and the children were immediately shifted to the intensive care unit,” it said, adding that 14 children “were completely burnt”.

Pims Spokesperson Dr Aneeza Jalil told Dawn that 15 babies were in the ward. “At least one baby was saved by a doctor,” she said.

Speaking to Geo News, Health Minister Mustafa Kamal said that the infants in the ward were either in incubators or on oxygen. He said the incident occurred at 6:45am due to a “blast in the air conditioner” inside the ward.

He said that the blast caused the fire, which was exacerbated due to the presence of the oxygen tanks. He confirmed that 14 infants had been killed, adding that law enforcement agencies were on the ground.

Later, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry insisted that there had not been any delay in the arrival of rescue teams and defended the district administration.

“After receiving information in the control room, they reached the hospital within six minutes,” the state minister said while speaking to the media in Islamabad.

He added that once the rescue teams assessed the situation, 19 people were rescued, including seven children, 1o mothers and two men.

He also said that administration officials “from the assistant commissioner to commissioner to the Islamabad IG” reached the hospital to monitor the situation. “Not only did they monitor but also assisted in the rescue operation,” he said.

Chaudhry said that the bodies of all 14 infants had been handed over to their families.

He added that a report of the incident had been sent to the prime minister and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who he said had been monitoring the situation.

An inquiry committee has been formed for a “high-powered” investigation into the incident, Chaudhry added. He said the committee will collect evidence — CCTV footage, presence of flammable equipment, why the door was locked, the number of doctors and nurses present — and present its findings.

Reiterating that rescue teams reached the site within six minutes, the state minister said, “There appears to be no negligence on the part of rescue services”.

However, he added, only the hospital administration could answer for the arrangements present within the hospital.

On being asked if Pims met the Capital Development Authority’s fire safety protocols, with the journalist also pointing out that his ministry had been issuing notices to the hospital for the past seven years, he acknowledged that notices had been issued.

“It is a huge institution, and notices were issued […] but what was complied with and what was not — as there are multiple buildings; we cannot conclude anything today, and an inquiry committee has been formed”.

Asked why the administration had not been active on the fire safety issue before, he said, “If there has been any negligence, the inquiry committee will find out.”

‘We ran for our lives’

Malik Israr, whose niece was admitted to the gynae ward, told Dawn that it was unfortunate the nursery was housed in a building in which repair and renovation work was ongoing.

“After the fire erupted, they told patients to vacate the building. Women who had just given birth had to rush down the stairs from the second floor,” he said.

Khurram Mehmood, 40, told AFP he lost his three-day-old daughter in the blaze and that rescuers took hours to arrive.

“I lost my daughter. She was only three days old,” he said. “My wife was in the ward. They took everyone out. We were sitting on the road waiting for help.”

He added, “Rescue teams arrived too late. Police arrived after four hours and said they were here to investigate.

“To hell with you, rescue team and police. Babies burnt to death there, but nobody could save them.”

Mehmood said the fire erupted at 6am, and rescue and authorities reached at 9am. “People were helping themselves.”

A mother with black residue from the smoke on her hands stood crying outside the hospital as she held her 10-day-old baby in her arms.

“People were screaming. There was black smoke. We ran for our lives. Thank god my baby is safe,” Shagufta Parveen told AFP.

“Give me my child,” Javeria, who lost her newborn, said outside the hospital, where ambulances had gathered. “I want justice.”

Mudasir, another parent who also lost his child, said all doors of the ward, except one, were shut and that there was “no fire security” in the ward.

Pims, established in 1985, is Islamabad’s biggest public sector hospital. It is one of two of the oldest health facilities in the federal capital and comprises several hospitals and teaching institutes.

Fires in large buildings are frequent in Pakistan, often due to poor safety laws and building codes as well as lax enforcement.

Federal health secretary removed

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice of the incident and directed the relevant authorities to investigate the incident. According to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), he expressed deep sorrow and grief at the incident and offered his condolences to the bereaved families.

“Such a situation involving children is unbearable,” the statement quoted him as saying.

“The circumstances that led to the incident should be thoroughly reviewed, those responsible should be identified, and the strictest possible action should be taken,” he said.

In a second statement, the PMO said the prime minister had suspended and removed federal Health Secretary Muhammad Aslam Ghauri.

The premier chaired a high-level meeting on the incident, where he expressed his anger and issued directives for “strict action”, the PMO said in another statement.

It too stated that the prime minister suspended the federal health secretary and asked him to leave the meeting, it said.

The statement quoted the prime minister as saying: “I am heartbroken at this tragic incident and share the parents’ grief.”

Subsequently, Captain (retired) Muhammad Mahmood, a BS-21 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), was appointed to the post of health secretary for three months “or till the posting of a regular incumbent,” a notification issued by the Cabinet Secretariat said.

According to the PMO, a high-level inquiry committee, headed by former interior secretary Shahid Khan, has launched an investigation.

State-run APP reported that Establishment Division Secretary Dr Barrister Nabeel Awan was also included in the committee.

Further, a notification issued by the Islamabad district magistrate said that a fact-finding committee, headed by the additional deputy commissioner general, had been formed to determine the facts behind the fire.

The members of the committee included the director general of the Capital Emergency Services, the City police station superintendent, the assistant commissioner (Industrial Area), the director general of the Capital Development Authority’s Electrical and Mechanical wing, representatives from Pims and Islamabad Electric Supply Company.

The committee was tasked with determining the exact cause of the fire, assessing whether adequate and functional fire-safety measures were in place, and evaluating the response time and effectiveness of the rescue and fire-fighting operations.

The notification said that a report would be furnished within 24 hours.

Ambulances are parked outside a mortuary following a deadly fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad on August 26, 2026. — AFP

Minister of State for Law Barrister Aqeel Malik assured in a post on X that a “complete, transparent, and impartial investigation of the incident will be conducted to determine the true causes of this catastrophe and any possible negligence”.

“In the event that negligence or failure is proven at any level, strict action will be taken against the responsible individuals in accordance with the law,” he added, extending his condolences to the bereaved families and expressing grief over the incident.

Meanwhile, PPP leader Nayyer Hussain Bukhari, who reached Pims along with other party leaders, demanded that the head of the MCH be removed.

He said it was not just negligence but rather criminal negligence and should not be ignored.

Nation expresses grief

President Zardari expressed heartfelt condolences and sympathy to the bereaved families. In a statement, the president said that the loss of lives was “heartbreaking and an irreparable loss”.

“Responsibility for the incident should be determined and action should be taken in accordance with the law,” he said.

Effective fire safety and emergency arrangements must be ensured in hospitals for the protection of patients, especially newborn babies, the president urged.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said he was deeply saddened by the incident.

“My deepest condolences to the bereaved parents and families. No words can ease the pain of losing an innocent child. May Allah Almighty grant the families strength and sabr in this unimaginably difficult hour,” he said.

As per the prime minister’s orders an immediate and thorough investigation will establish the causes of this tragic incident to ensure that those found responsible face the strictest action. The safety of our children must remain paramount,” he said.

PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said the loss of innocent lives was an unbearable tragedy for the entire nation and expressed heartfelt sympathy and solidarity with the bereaved families.

He called for an impartial investigation into the incident and said that the nation be informed how such a tragedy occurred at a major hospital.

“Those responsible for negligence or failing to ensure the safety of patients must be held accountable,” he added, stressing that the federal government must ensure the safety of patients and medical staff at all hospitals under its administration.

First Lady and MNA Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari also expressed “profound grief and sorrow over the tragic loss of newborn babies” and conveyed her “deepest sympathies to the bereaved families”.

“The loss of innocent newborn lives is heartbreaking and deeply distressing,” a statement by the Presidency quoted her as saying.

She called for a “thorough, swift and transparent investigation” into the incident.

PML-N President Nawaz Sharif said he was “deeply grieved” to hear about the deaths. He urged the government to take strict action against those responsible and ensure measures were put in place to prevent such incidents in the future.

Senate Chairman Syed Yousuf Raza Gilani expressed deep grief and sorrow over the tragic incident. In a statement, he offered his condolences to the families affected.

He said effective safety measures, fire safety systems and all necessary arrangements to deal with emergencies must be ensured in hospitals to prevent such incidents.

“Any negligence in safety measures is unacceptable,” he said. Gilani urged the relevant authorities to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the incident and take effective and practical steps to prevent such tragedies in the future.

National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq also expressed profound grief and sorrow over the deaths of the infants.

In a statement, he said he was “heartbroken” over the incident and shared equally in the pain and grief of the bereaved parents.

United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund (Unicef) called for an urgent review as it expressed grief over the incident.

“Unicef is deeply saddened by the tragic loss of at least 14 newborn lives following a fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad today.

“We extend our deepest condolences to the bereaved families and all those affected by this devastating incident,” it said in a statement.

The UN agency added, “ Every newborn deserves a safe start to life, and every mother and child should be able to receive care in a safe, secure health facility.

It called for the urgent review and strengthening of fire prevention and safety standards across health facilities.

The British High Commission in Pakistan termed the incident “heartbreaking news”.

“Our deepest condolences and thoughts are with the parents and families at this unimaginably difficult time,” it said.

The French embassy shared the sentiment, describing the incident as “deeply distressing”.

“Our hearts go out to the families who lost their newborn children in the tragic fire at Pims in Islamabad. Loss of innocent lives is heartbreaking and deeply distressing. Embassy of France extends its deepest sympathies to bereaved families and everyone affected by this tragedy,” it said in its message on X.

The Pakistan Medical Association (PMA) said in a statement that it was in “deep mourning” over the incident.

“The association reiterates that healthcare facilities are designed to protect and restore human lives, yet administrative failure and regulatory oversight lapses have turned these institutions into danger zones,” it said.

It demanded action against officials “whose failure to uphold safety codes resulted in this catastrophe”. It also demanded enforcing strict consequences so that “systemic failure serves as a decisive warning, preventing future lapses across both public and private medical facilities”.

It further said that there should be immediate restructuring and public accountability of health regulatory authorities responsible for enforcing safety protocols, building codes and emergency infrastructure in hospitals.

The PMA also called for “full institutional backing for the grieving parents, ensuring they receive complete legal, financial, and emotional justice”.

Additional input from AFP and Reuters

World.title: On Eid Miladun Nabi, PM Shehbaz and President Zardari urge nation to follow teachings of the Holy Prophet
World.content:
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday urged the nation to draw guidance from the life and the teachings of the Holy Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) and make hard work and service to humanity the purpose of their lives, state-run Radio Pakistan reported.

In separate messages on Eid Miladun Nabi, both leaders extended heartfelt felicitations to the nation and the Muslim Ummah on the birth anniversary of Holy Prophet (PBUH).

In his message, the president said, “It is incumbent upon us to practically promote justice and fairness, tolerance, inter-sectarian and interfaith harmony, and the protection of human dignity in our society.

“This day reminds us of the great blessing of Allah Almighty through which humanity was granted the perfect path of faith, guidance, justice, mercy and noble character,” he added.

Meanwhile, PM Shehbaz said that in order to overcome the economic, social and moral challenges confronting the country, “we must mould our collective lives in accordance with the perfect guidance provided by Islam”, the state broadcaster reported.

The prime minister called for playing a role in making Pakistan a strong, prosperous, peaceful and welfare state.

In a separate post on X, he said that the life and teachings of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) “remain an eternal source of guidance for all humanity — calling us towards compassion, justice, tolerance, unity and service to others”.

“Let us pledge to illuminate our character and collective conduct with the light of Seeratun Nabi and work together for a peaceful, and prosperous Pakistan,” he said.

World.title: Mayor Mamdani opposes NYC event with leader of India's Hindu nationalist group
World.content:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said on Tuesday he did not support an upcoming event in his city featuring the leader of the Hindu nationalist group that is the ideological parent of India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

Mohan Bhagwat, chief of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), is scheduled to speak at a Manhattan event on Saturday, according to the event’s website.

“I don’t support the rally, but I don’t know if the city has any jurisdiction on cancelling a private event,” Mamdani, who is the first Muslim and Indian American mayor of New York City, said when asked if the event should be cancelled.

“The vision of India that I was taught by my family and one that I grew up being very familiar with was of a pluralistic society of a secular Republic that believed in the belonging of each and every person who was from India. And it has been incredibly troubling to see the rise of a movement that is predicated on an exclusionary vision.”

The event’s website casts the August 29 gathering as the “Universal Oneness Celebration” bringing together the Hindu American community.

The organisers, American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue, say the event is backed by several Hindu American groups and promotes shared heritage and interfaith unity. Many local organisations have criticised it over Bhagwat’s attendance and the RSS’ history.

The RSS, a powerful Hindu group from which Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s BJP emerged, said in May it had organised foreign visits, including to the US, to counter perceptions it is a paramilitary outfit involved in attacks on minority communities.

The US Commission on International Religious Freedom says the RSS “has been involved in acts of extreme violence and intolerance against members of minority groups for decades”.

The RSS disputes intolerance accusations and says it is a “Hindu-centric civilisational, cultural movement” whose goal is to “carry the nation to the pinnacle of glory”, including by uniting Hindus.

United Nations and human rights groups say abuse of Indian minorities has risen in recent years, pointing to rising hate speeches, a religion-based citizenship law, the demolition of Muslim-owned properties, the removal of occupied Kashmir’s autonomy and an anti-conversion legislation that challenges freedom of belief.

The BJP-led Indian government denies being discriminatory and says its policies, including food subsidy programmes and electrification drives, benefit all communities.

World.title: Security, traffic plans for Eid Miladun Nabi processions
World.content:
Authorities have made elaborate security and road traffic arrangements across the country for rallies in connection with the 12th Rabiul Awwal on Wednesday.

Karachi

In Karachi, 4,208 policemen have been deployed to secure religious rallies and gatherings in the metropolis, of whom 1,702 have been stationed in South Zone and 765 in East Zone, according to an official statement by police.

Police said 397 officers and personnel had been deployed for the security of the main 12th Rabiul Awwal procession at Nishtar Park, and 362 more had been stationed at the entry points of the park.

Karachi Additional Inspector General Azad Khan, the metropolis’s police chief, had directed law enforcers to remain on high alert on routes of all processions, and traffic police had been instructed to ensure smooth flow of traffic, the statement said.

He also issued directions for the effective monitoring of the security situation through CCTV cameras.

Meanwhile, the city’s traffic police said three main processions were planned in the city.

The first procession was scheduled to depart from Shaheed Masjid in Kharadar at 2:30pm, pass through Memon Masjid and conclude at Gulzar-i-Habib Mosque at the time of Asr prayers. The second was scheduled to depart from Memon Masjid at 2:30pm and conclude at Aram Bagh Masjid at the time of Asr prayers.

The main procession would depart from Memon Masjid after 3pm and conclude at Nishtar Park at around 6pm.

Map of procession routes in Karachi — Traffic Police

According to the traffic plan for the day, commuters travelling from Nazimabad can proceed towards their destinations from Lasbela Chowk via Nishtar Road towards Garden. Those coming from Liaquatabad can turn left at Teen Hatti and proceed towards Central Jail (Martin Road).

Commuters travelling from Hassan Square towards PIB Colony can use Kashmir Road to reach Society Light Signal (Shahrah-i-Quaideen). Those travelling from the Jail Flyover towards Teen Hatti can use Nishtar Road via Lasbela Chowk.

No traffic is allowed to travel from the Governor House towards Numaish.

Commuters travelling from Sharea Faisal via Shahrah-i-Quaideen (Noorani Kabab) towards Numaish can turn right at Society Light Signal onto Kashmir Road to reach their destinations.

Those travelling from Central Jail Gate (Jamshed Road) via Guru Mandir towards M.A. Jinnah Road can use Guru Mandir Bypass Road and Soldier Bazar.

Commuters travelling from Garden Chowrangi towards M.A. Jinnah Road can turn right at Anklesaria Hospital towards Gul Plaza, or turn left at Coast Guard/Holy Family Hospital to reach their destinations.

Traffic coming from Lucky Star towards M.A. Jinnah Road and Empress Market will be diverted from Saddar Dawakhana towards PP Chowrangi. Similarly, traffic heading towards Preedy Road will be diverted from Abdullah Haroon Road towards M.A. Jinnah Chowk, from where it can proceed towards its destination.

Traffic is not allowed to travel from M.A. Jinnah Chowk towards Court Road (Kabootar Chowk). All traffic is to be diverted via Strachan Road towards Pakistan Chowk.

Traffic heading from Shahrah-i-Liaquat towards Preedy Road will be diverted from Aram Bagh Light Signal towards Pakistan Chowk, from where it can proceed to its destination.

Rawalpindi

In Rawalpindi, more than 910 traffic police personnel have been deployed to regulate traffic during the processions.

A total of 120 processions will be taken out across the city, including two categorised as A, 10 as B and 108 as C, according to the traffic police.

Murree Road will remain closed in both directions during the processions. Traffic travelling from Rawalpindi to Islamabad will be diverted via Tipu Road towards Liaquat Bagh Chowk while vehicles coming from Islamabad will be diverted from the Rawal Road turn towards Rawal Road.

Traffic travelling from Liaquat Bagh to Fawara Chowk will be diverted from DAV College towards Gawalmandi.

For the second procession, which will start from Chungi No. 22, traffic coming from Kalma Chowk will be diverted towards Harley Street. The procession will pass through Tench Road, Dhoke Syedan Chowk, Kalma Chowk, No. 22 Chowk, Adiala Road, State Life Building turn, MH Chowk, Mahfuz Chowk, Mansehra Adda, Thana Cantt, Nishtar Street, Adamji Road, Mithu Khan Complex, Railway Road, Military Accounts and Kamran Market to conclude at GTS Chowk.

Traffic heading towards Khattak Chowk, CMH and Tench will be diverted towards Harley Street during the procession. When the procession reaches Mall Road, traffic coming from Peshawar Road will be diverted from Qasim Market towards Sher Khan Road, the traffic police said.

Traffic travelling from Kutchery Chowk towards Peshawar Road will be diverted from TM Chowk to Murree Road. Tractor trolleys, trailers and trucks will not be allowed to enter the procession routes.

No parking will be allowed within 300 yards of the stage.

A special traffic plan has also been prepared to facilitate ambulances, fire engines and other emergency vehicles.

Traffic will be diverted from highways where processions are held, while citizens have been advised to avoid unnecessary travel on procession routes, Chief Traffic Officer (CTO) Farhan Aslam said.

Peshawar

The main procession in Peshawar will be held under the banner of Idara Tableeghul Islam.

It will start after Isha (night) prayers from Milad Chowk in the city and, after passing through its traditional routes, will culminate at Qissa Khwani Bazaar where the main Mehfil-i-Milad will be held.

Several small processions will also be taken out from Sikandar Pura, Qissa Khwani, Saddar, Kohati, Gulbahar and other areas.

According to the plan prepared by the city’s traffic police, four superintendents of police, 12 deputy superintendents of police (DSP) and 600 personnel and wardens have been deployed across the city.

Citizens can also get traffic updates via helpline 1915.

Lahore

According to Lahore traffic police, 16 DSPs, 45 sector in-charges and over 1,400 wardens and patrolling officers have been deployed in the city, where two main processions will be taken out.

In addition, 172 rallies and 125 Milad gatherings will be organised, the traffic police posted on X.

Overall in Punjab, 8,000 traffic police officers and personnel had been deployed across the province, according to a statement by the Punjab traffic police.

It said 1,436 Miladun Nabi gatherings and 2,479 processions had been planned across the province, while 216 processions and 111 Milad gatherings would be held in Lahore.

The Punjab Police have deployed 55,000 personnel for about 4,500 gatherings and processions across the province for Eid Miladun Nabi.

Punjab Inspector General of Police (IGP) Abdul Kareem said that the Counter-Terrorism Department would also monitor the main gatherings other than the field police officers, including regional and district police officers, across the province.

He said that security would remain on high alert during the Eid Miladun Nabi programmes.

World.title: Nepal floods at China border kill 8, cause 'major casualties' in Tibet
World.content:
Massive flooding killed eight people in Nepal on Wednesday as Chinese state media reported “major casualties” from a mudslide at a Tibet trade hub on China’s side of the nations’ shared border.

Images shared by Nepali police showed floodwater surging through a river, sweeping away houses in its path, while AFP images depicted the top floor of a house sticking out from muddy soil.

“So far, eight bodies have been found. Rescue operations are underway,” Nepal police spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle told AFP.

Videos shared by Nepal police and others on social media showed torrents of muddy water crashing through mountain valleys in the Himalayan district bordering China.

“I witnessed the flood sweep away eight or nine trucks, along with houses and people,” Suman Chalise, a 34-year-old teacher, told AFP in Nuwakot district.

“It was absolutely heart-wrenching. I had not witnessed such devastation before.”

The police spokesman told AFP earlier that authorities did not know the extent of the damage but said they had “alerted people who are staying near the riverside to relocate”.

The Nepal Army said it had deployed helicopters and disaster response personnel to the affected area.

The Nepal Electricity Authority said about 430 megawatts of production capacity, including from hydropower and solar facilities, had been damaged.

“The disaster has damaged the production, transmission and distribution facilities of the Authority… resulting in disruption of electricity supply,” it said.

Sarthak Shrestha, a remote sensing and geo-information analyst at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), said a preliminary assessment showed “no anomalies” from China’s side of the border.

“We believe a rock-ice avalanche occurred in Nepal, blocking the Lhende River and causing the cascading flood event,” he told AFP.

Mudslide risk

Several highways were also closed, Nepali authorities said.

Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported on Wednesday that “a mudslide disaster on the Nepalese side resulted in major casualties and missing people at the Gyirong Port” in Tibet.

Footage shared by the broadcaster, which AFP was unable to immediately verify, showed rushing water carrying tree branches and debris, as well as a flooded road.

State news agency Xinhua said Chinese President Xi Jinping had urged “all-out” rescue operations, but did not provide figures on injuries or deaths.

Xi said that “the most urgent task is doing everything possible to search for and rescue the missing people … quickly treat injured people and minimise casualties to the greatest extent possible”, according to CCTV.

Traffic authorities in Tibet’s Shigatse said roads in the area were “at risk of mudslides and unsafe for passage” in a post to social media on Wednesday.

In July last year, 17 people went missing after a mudslide near the Gyirong Port, Xinhua reported at the time.

Monsoon rains from June to September regularly trigger deadly floods and landslides across South Asia.

Scientists say climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events in the region.

Qianggong Zhang, head of climate and environmental risks at ICIMOD, said a second flood may be imminent.

“With a blockage still lodged upstream on the Nepal-China border river, authorities warn a second flood may occur,” he told AFP.

World.title: Indepe­ndent power producers found overcharging users through costly coal procurement
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Indepe­ndent power producers (IPPs) operating on impor­ted coal have been found imposing an additional burden on electricity consumers through opaque and inefficient coal procurement practices, with the cost ultimately passed on through monthly fuel price adjustments (FPAs).

While consumer groups have been raising concerns over such practices at various forums, including public hearings, the power division and the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) have now also pointed to inefficiencies in coal procurement and their financial impact on consumers.

The issue gained prominence after recent competitive bidding for coal supply to the 660MW state-owned Jamshoro Power Plant attracted a discount of $7.12 per tonne from a Karachi-based supplier compared to discounts of only 20 to 50 cents per tonne in some contracts involving IPPs.

“The power division has identified significant inefficiencies in the procurement of imported coal by power plants,” an official statement said on Tuesday, adding that fresh policy guidelines had been iss­ued “for corrective action that could save the natio­nal exchequer up to Rs380 million annually”.

In a recent order, Nepra had already pointed out concerns over coal procurement by Port Qasim Electric Power Company (PQEPC) under a six-year contract involving discounts of $0.20 to $0.50 per tonne based on estimated coal prices.

“This type of evaluation has never been observed in any bidding by any other power plant, including PQEPC, and does not seem justified, as it is based on estimated coal prices, which may change in future,” Nepra said in its judgement.

The regulator also noted that the Port Qasim plant had published its tender notice only in China instead of reaching out to a broader pool of potential bidders.

“Had discounts been incorporated into the bid evaluation as a major criterion, it may have yielded more competitive and higher discounts from prospective bidders,” Nepra said.

The regulator also observed that the plant had not disclosed that it had already executed a long-term coal supply agreement when the matter was discussed with the regulator on two occasions, prompting “proceedings regarding misstatement and/or non-disclosure of information”.

Nepra subsequently directed the Port Qasim plant to conduct fresh bidding for a long-term coal supply agreement within three months of its March 2026 FPA decision.

However, officials said that after the March 25 order, the company procured about 1.2 million tonnes of coal, enough for almost an entire year, just before a new tender.

They said the contract again involved a discount of around $0.50 per tonne against the $7.12 discount secured by the public-sector Jamshoro plant.

The difference alone works out to around $8 million, officials said. If similar procurement practices were followed by other IPPs, the impact could rise substantially.

The power division said the procurement inefficiencies were identified during a series of meetings presided over by the power minister, where officials reviewed actual data, contractual arrangements and market practices.

“Pakistan has a significant fleet of coal-fired power plants with a combined capacity of approximately 5,280 megawatts that rely wholly or partly on imported coal. These include three major 1,320MW plants at Port Qasim, Hub Power and Sahiwal, as well as the Lucky and Jamshoro plants which also have the capability to use imported coal,” it said.

The division said coal import prices for IPPs were linked to internationally recognised benchmarks such as the API-4 index, but the final price paid by a plant also depended on the discount negotiated with the supplier.

PQEPC Chief Financial Officer Adil Ashraf and Procurement Chief Liang Ding Ping did not respond to Dawn’s written queries.

Published in Dawn, August 26th, 2026

World.title: 'A privilege, not a right': US to revoke visas of up to 200,000 asylum seekers
World.content:
The US government plans to revoke the visas of foreigners who came to the country for tourism or business but sought to stay longer by applying for asylum, the State Department said on Tuesday.

The crackdown marks another step in the Trump administration’s signature drive to reduce immigration into the United States.

The administration said it is now working with the Department of Homeland Security to identify and revoke the visas of people who, it said, came to America billing themselves as temporary visitors but then applied for asylum so they could stay permanently.

“Obtaining a visa in order to seek asylum is fraud — which is grounds for visa revocation,” State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said in a statement that confirmed press reports about the new policy.

The White House, in a post on X, suggested “up to two hundred thousand visas” would be affected and claimed it would be the “largest mass visa revocation in history”.

The State Department neither confirmed nor denied that number.

Pigott said, “The number of revocations remains dynamic and will be done on a rolling basis.”

Early this month, the department said that since President Donald Trump returned to power in January 2025, some 175,000 foreigners had seen their US visas revoked on grounds ranging from criminal offenses, including driving under the influence, to praising the killing of the right-wing activist Charlie Kirk.

The administration also recently revoked the visas of Mexican officials, including the son of the former president Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador. This prompted a complaint from the current president, Claudia Sheinbaum.

Trump, who won reelection in large part on his promise to fight illegal immigration, has expelled huge numbers of people who were in the country without proper residence papers.

But he has also worked to restrict the entry of foreigners who do go by the rules and has gone after those who overstay their visas after they expire.

Some of these measures have been challenged and curtailed by the courts.

Last Friday a federal judge struck down a government ban on visas to nationals from 75 countries who wish to settle in the country indefinitely.

These countries included Afghanistan, Brazil, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Nigeria, Somalia, Thailand and Yemen.

The Trump administration is also planning to expand vetting of the social media accounts of visa applicants.

“We are making clear that a visa is a privilege — not a right,” Pigott said on Tuesday.

World.title: Fresh efforts at mediation revive hopes for US-Iran climbdown
World.content:
COMMERCIAL vessels are seen in the Strait of Hormuz, near the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas, as Tehran and Muscat agreed on a phased arrangement for the troubled waterway. According to the two sides, the agreement covers the formation of a temporary joint navigation corridor, mine clearance, information exchange and traffic management.—Reuters

• Back-to-back Tehran trips by CDF Munir, Omani FM yield progress on key issues

• Despite public brinkmanship, Washington ‘ready to show flexibility’ on economic sanctions if Iran meets ‘certain conditions’, US media reports

• Diplomatic sources point to ‘softer than expected’ sanctions, say Islamabad taking the lead in conveying messages from Tehran to Washington, and vice versa

• Iran seeks return to terms agreed in Islamabad MoU; eyes Hormuz agreement with Oman

ISLAMABAD / WASHINGTON: Progress made during two key visits to Tehran — by Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir and Omani Foreign Minister Badr Al-Busaidi — may have opened the first potentially workable pathway towards de-escalation in the Gulf, since the breakdown of the armistice secured through the Islamabad Memor­andum of Understanding (MoU).

Although there has been no clear breakthrough yet, and fundamental differences persist between Iran and the United States, the latest diplomatic activity has brought the political and technical dimensions of the dispute back into focus.

In Washington too, there seems to be a willingness to consider sanctions relief as part of a broa­der understanding with Tehran, provided Iran meets certain conditions.

According to some US media reports, Washington has offered an end to economic sanctions and the naval blockade against Iran in exchange for Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz to shipping and halting attacks by Iran-aligned regional groups.

However, the specific terms have not been publicly confirmed by Washington or Tehran.

Importantly, unlike the period following the collapse of the June understanding, when the two sides were largely talking past each other and the crisis was bec­o­ming increasingly militarised, there is a renewed push towards establishing a new mechanism for maintaining the ceasefire.

Observers believe Field Mars­hal Munir’s visit served to reopen channels bet­w­­een Tehran and Washington, through Islamabad.

It is also noteworthy that the Iranian reaction to the visit was unusually positive, with Seyed Mehdi Tabatabaei, deputy for communications and information at the Iranian president’s office, describing it as “highly fruitful” and saying it had produced “highly valuable diplomatic achievements”.

The CDF’s meeting with Gen Mohsen Rezaei — the Supreme Leader’s representative on the Supreme National Security Council – was particularly significant in testing whether the security side in Tehran was also prepared to join the renewed process.

Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), too, said the Iranian leadership appreciated Pakistan’s “constructive role and sincere efforts” for dialogue and de-escalation.

But Tehran has so far not publicly indicated any readiness to make unilateral concessions to US, rather, the message emerging from the meetings was that Iran remains prepared to return to the understanding formalised under Islamabad MoU, provided Washington first addresses what Tehran considers its violations of the memorandum, and returns to implementing the understanding.

‘Softer than expected’ sanctions

Diplomatic sources in Washington also confirmed that Pakistan’s mediation role is being supported from the top, with Field Marshal Munir remaining in touch with both President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, complemented by working-level contacts between US and Pakistani officials.

Asked whether Pakistan had conveyed any US proposals to Iran, sources confirmed that this was the case, adding that Tehran’s proposals have also been relayed to Washington, “along with their comments”.

“So, they are not only facilitating but also [carrying out] mediation, which includes conveying their opinions as well,” sources said.

The description is broadly consistent with reporting by CBS News and The Wall Street Journal, both of which have identified Pakistan as an important conduit between Washington and Tehran.

As evidence of the impact this messaging is having on the Trump adm­in­­istration’s actions, diplomatic sources in Washin­gton pointed to the recent announcement of economic sanctions against Iran.

Although the Trump administration had billed the sanctions as spelling an “economic doomsday” for Tehran, diplomatic sources said: “The restrictions are softer than expected, and also, on the other side, there have been no recent attacks on Gulf states”.

While the Treasury Department has announced new sanctions on 60 individuals, entities and vessels, but the list did not feature any of the Chinese financial institutions thought to be facilitating Iran’s oil trade.

The Iranian position, nevertheless, remains conditional as it continues to regard the Islamabad MoU as the appropriate framework, but wants Washington to demonstrate through concrete action that it is prepared to honour its commitments.

The dispute over Hormuz is, meanwhile, not being treated by Iran as a separate maritime issue rather it has been tied to the issues of sanctions, the US naval blockade and reciprocal implementation of the June understanding.

Hormuz progress

In this context, the progress made in Oman-Iran talks assumes greater significance.

Al-Busaidi’s visit to Tehran produced some forward movement on navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, with the two sides agreeing on a phased arrangement.

As per the joint statement, the understanding between Oman and Iran includes a temporary joint navigation corridor, mine clearance, information exchange and traffic management, while technical discussions would continue on a permanent navigation arrangement.

Al-Busaidi said in a post on X after the meeting that he hoped the countries would “soon announce” the temporary corridor in the strait.

“Future management of the strait and a permanent solution will follow in due course,” he said.

Technical negotiations will continue to determine a “permanent navigational corridor and future administration of the Strait, as well as a mechanism for information-sharing, traffic management, and the provision of relevant navigational and security services”, the earlier joint statement read.

The announcement came as US President Donald Trump repeated claims on Truth Social that “all mines have been removed and/or detonated from within the International Waters of the Strait of Hormuz”, citing the US navy.

“Iran has been notified that any ship or boat placing new mines will be immediately and systematically destroyed… There is a Zero Tolerance policy on mine placement in full force and effect,” he added.

Meanwhile, the Reuters news agency reported that Washington is beginning to send personnel back to some diplomatic missions in the Middle East that were evacuated or downsized amid tensions with Iran.

The move suggests Washington sees a lower risk of the conflict with Iran escalating in the near term, though some embassies will initially operate below full capacity.

Published in Dawn, August 26th, 2026

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.
